jobs.title: Product Manager, Integrations
jobs.excerpt: 👋 Welcome to Hi Rasmus! At Hi Rasmus, people are at the heart of everything we do.
jobs.description:
👋 Welcome to Hi Rasmus!

At Hi Rasmus, people are at the heart of everything we do. Whether you're just joining us or have been part of our journey, we’re excited to have you on board!

We’re on a mission to make evidence-based autism care accessible to families everywhere. 🌍 Families shouldn’t have to uproot their lives to access support—that’s why we break down barriers while keeping the human touch at the center of our work. Our goal? To positively impact the lives of 1 million children with autism.

Rooted in a culture that values trust, collaboration, and balance, we foster a workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered.

🎯 Our Core Values

  • Innovation 🧠 – We embrace creativity and seek better solutions.
  • Integrity ⚖️ – Honesty and trust guide everything we do.
  • Collaboration 🤝 – Together, we achieve more.
  • Growth 🌱 – We’re committed to personal and professional development.
  • Empathy ❤️ – We prioritize understanding and human connection.

🚀 What It’s Like to Work Here

At Hi Rasmus, we trust our team to do great work, their way. Flexibility, autonomy, and balance are key—we know that when life and work fit together, everyone thrives. 🏡✨
  • Flat structure, open doors – Every voice matters. Collaboration and shared decision-making drive us forward.
  • Balance is a priority – Recharge, make time for what matters, and do your best work in a way that works for you.
  • Real impact, real growth – Be part of a team making a difference for families worldwide, while growing your skills along the way.

Join us in shaping a future where exceptional autism care is within reach for all. 💡💙

🔗 Why This Role Matters

As Hi Rasmus grows, our customers increasingly operate within an ecosystem of systems alongside ours — EHRs, practice management platforms, payer systems, data platforms, and tools we haven’t met yet.
Those systems need to work together.
A broken or poorly designed integration isn’t simply a technical problem. It can create duplicate work, unreliable data, disconnected workflows, frustrated clinicians and operations teams, and less confidence in the systems people depend on every day.
But building great integrations requires more than connecting two systems.
Someone needs to understand how the work actually happens: what information needs to move, who depends on it, which system owns what, where workflows break down, and which problems are important enough to solve.
That’s where you come in.

📢 About the Role

📍 Location: Fully remote - US
💼 Department: Product
🤝 Reports to: Product Leadership
⏳ Job Type: Full-time, Exempt
💰 Compensation: Range of $90,000 to $115,000 annually
🕜 Working Hours: Flexible within US time zones. Because this role partners closely with our Denmark-based team, some morning overlap with European hours matters most—Eastern Time works seamlessly, and Pacific or other time zones work well for those able to start their day a bit earlier.

As our Product Manager, Integrations, you’ll own a product area that sits at the intersection of customers, partners, operations, data, and Engineering.
You’ll become deeply curious about how ABA organizations operate and how Hi Rasmus fits into their broader technology ecosystem. You’ll work directly with customers and integration partners, get underneath their requests to understand the actual workflow problems they’re trying to solve, and help determine where Hi Rasmus should invest.
You’ll also partner deeply with Engineering.
On this team, technical discovery may often be engineering-led — and that’s a good thing. Your job isn’t to tell engineers how to build an integration. Your job is to bring the customer, partner, operational, product, and business context that helps the team decide what problems are worth solving and why.
This isn’t a requirements-handoff role.
You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be technically curious and fluent enough to ask good questions, understand tradeoffs, build credibility with technical partners, and connect what’s happening between systems back to the people and workflows depending on them.
Your goal is deceptively simple:
Make Hi Rasmus easy to integrate with — and dependable once you do.

🎯 What You’ll Help Make Possible

🔌 Objective 1: Make Integrations Dependable + Scalable

Create an integration experience where partners can connect to Hi Rasmus with confidence — without every new integration becoming a custom project.
How we’ll know it’s working:
  • Partners can integrate predictably, with fewer preventable implementation issues and less ongoing intervention from Hi Rasmus.
  • Existing integrations remain healthy as Hi Rasmus evolves.
  • We increasingly solve recurring integration needs through scalable patterns and capabilities rather than one-off solutions.

🔄 Objective 2: Turn Operational Workflows Into Better Product Decisions

Develop a deep understanding of how ABA organizations actually operate — and use that understanding to identify where integrations and data movement can remove friction, manual work, and disconnected workflows.
How we’ll know it’s working:
  • Integration priorities are grounded in real customer workflows and clearly understood problems, not simply incoming requests.
  • Manual reconciliation, duplicate work, and data inconsistencies decrease in the workflows we choose to support.
  • Product and Engineering can clearly connect integration investments back to meaningful customer and operational outcomes.

🤝 Objective 3: Create Clarity Across Customers, Partners + Teams

Become the connective tissue between Engineering, external partners, Customer Success, Implementation, Commercial, and Product — helping Hi Rasmus make thoughtful prioritization decisions and setting our partners up for success.
How we’ll know it’s working:
  • Partners have clear expectations around integration scope, capabilities, responsibilities, and changes.
  • Engineering and customer-facing teams have the context they need to make good decisions without unnecessary handoffs or escalation.
  • We can make hard prioritization decisions across customer demand, partner needs, technical complexity, reliability, and company priorities — and clearly explain why.

🛠️ What You’ll Own

🧭 Customer + Operational Understanding

  • Build a deep understanding of how ABA organizations operate and where technology, data, and workflows intersect.
  • Spend time with enterprise operations teams, clinicians, Customer Success, Implementation, and other people close to the work.
  • Get underneath integration requests to understand the underlying problem: What is the customer actually trying to accomplish? What happens today? Where does it break? Who feels the pain?
  • Learn the Hi Rasmus platform and domain deeply enough to connect customer workflows to meaningful product opportunities.
  • Build ongoing feedback loops so Product and Engineering stay close to how integrations perform in the real world.

🤝 Integration Partner Experience

  • Build strong working relationships with external integration partners and the technical teams building alongside Hi Rasmus.
  • Confidently lead conversations about operational workflows, product needs, constraints, expectations, and priorities while partnering with Engineering on deeper technical decisions.
  • Help partners understand how Hi Rasmus works, what our integrations can support, and where boundaries or tradeoffs exist.
  • Create a partner experience built on clarity, predictability, trust, and good communication.
  • Help improve the documentation, onboarding, testing, support, and feedback mechanisms partners need to successfully integrate with us.

🧩 Integration Product Strategy

  • Own the product problems, discovery, prioritization, product bets, roadmap, and outcomes within the Integrations charter.
  • Turn recurring customer and partner needs into scalable capabilities rather than accumulating bespoke solutions.
  • Balance new integration opportunities with the reliability and platform work necessary to keep existing integrations healthy.
  • Define what success looks like before building — and stay with product bets after launch to understand adoption, reliability, customer value, and what we should do next.
  • Help the organization make thoughtful tradeoffs between customer value, technical complexity, scalability, strategic importance, and effort.
  • Explore where integrations and data delivery create enough customer value to support future packaging and monetization opportunities.

🧠 Product × Engineering

  • Work with Engineering as one problem-solving team, not as Product writing requirements for Engineering to execute.
  • Bring deep customer, partner, operational, commercial, and product context while Engineering brings deep technical and architectural expertise.
  • Frame problems, intended outcomes, assumptions, constraints, and tradeoffs clearly enough that the team can shape solutions together.
  • Participate meaningfully in technical conversations while knowing when Engineering should lead the technical decision.
  • Partner on questions around data exchange, system dependencies, integration reliability, APIs, and technical tradeoffs without needing to design the architecture yourself.
  • Use data, prototypes, AI, partner feedback, and experimentation to learn quickly before committing significant engineering investment.

📣 Product + Customer Enablement

  • Partner with Customer Success and Implementation to understand where integrations create friction — and where scalable product capabilities can replace manual work.
  • Help customer-facing teams understand what our integrations can and cannot do, how they should be positioned, and where expectations need to be set.
  • Partner with Commercial teams to understand enterprise demand, emerging integration needs, and where data delivery creates meaningful customer value.
  • Translate what we learn from partners and customers back into context the broader organization can use.

🤝 How You’ll Work Across Hi Rasmus

You’ll have meaningful ownership of the problems, discovery, product bets, prioritization, roadmap, and success measures within your charter.
You’ll work particularly closely with:
Engineering — to deeply understand problems and shape solutions together. Engineering owns technical architecture and implementation; Product brings deep customer, partner, operational, and business context. Neither solves the problem alone.
Customer Success + Implementation — to understand how customers actually work, where data movement creates friction, and where better integrations can eliminate manual effort. Ensuring that these teams also have a clear understanding as we release updates to our integrations.
Commercial — to understand enterprise demand, partner opportunities, and where integration and data capabilities create meaningful customer value.
External Partners — to understand their systems and workflows, build trust, navigate constraints, and create integration experiences that work for both sides.
Product Leadership + other PMs — to make hard prioritization decisions and ensure integration work supports the broader Hi Rasmus product strategy rather than becoming an isolated technical roadmap.

🌟 The Kind of Product Person We’re Looking For

You’re technically curious without needing to be the smartest engineer in the room.

You genuinely enjoy figuring out how systems and people fit together.

When someone says, “We just need an integration,” your instinct is to ask: Why?
What is the workflow today? What information needs to move? Which system owns what? Who depends on it? What happens when something goes wrong? And are we solving something once — or creating something that can solve the problem again and again?
You’re equally comfortable talking with an engineer about how systems interact and an operations leader about why two systems disagreeing is making someone’s Tuesday miserable. 🙂
You can walk into a complex domain you don’t yet understand, stay humble and curious, and become knowledgeable enough to make good product decisions.
You’re comfortable saying no, not yet, or there’s a better way to solve this — and can bring customers, partners, and internal teams along with you.
And you care about what happens after something ships.
Because when other people’s workflows and systems depend on ours, “it works” isn’t enough. It needs to keep working.

🧩 What You Bring

You likely bring:
  • Product Management experience in B2B SaaS, platform products, healthcare technology, developer products, or another technically complex environment.
  • Direct experience working with integrations, interoperability, data exchange, APIs, or other connected product ecosystems.
  • Experience working directly with external technology partners, enterprise customers, developers, IT teams, or similarly complex stakeholders.
  • Enough technical fluency to work credibly alongside engineers and integration partners — understanding APIs, data exchange, system dependencies, integration reliability, and technical tradeoffs without needing to be the engineer designing the solution.
  • Strong product discovery and judgment — you know how to get underneath a request to understand the real customer or operational problem.
  • Demonstrated ability to learn a complex operational domain quickly and deeply enough to make strong product decisions.
  • Experience turning complex customer or partner needs into scalable product capabilities rather than accumulating bespoke solutions.
  • Strong prioritization skills and comfort making decisions when customer value, technical complexity, partner needs, and business priorities compete.
  • Clear, confident communication and the ability to build trust across technical and non-technical audiences.

✨ Helpful, But Not Required

  • Experience with healthcare integrations, including EHR/EMR, payer, practice-management, or other healthcare technology ecosystems.
  • Familiarity with healthcare interoperability standards or data exchange.
  • Experience building developer-facing products, APIs, integration marketplaces, or data products.
  • Experience with data-delivery or integration-based business models.
  • Experience in ABA, behavioral health, or another complex healthcare environment.
Most importantly, you don’t need to arrive knowing ABA.
You do need to be the kind of person who will want to learn it — getting close enough to our customers, clinicians, operations teams, partners, and product to understand how the world actually works before deciding how technology should change it.

💙 Why Hi Rasmus?

We’re building technology in a space where better products can give clinicians time back, make operations easier, improve access to care, and ultimately help more children and families.
You’ll have meaningful ownership, work alongside people who care deeply about the problems we’re solving, and help shape an area of the Hi Rasmus platform that will become increasingly important as we grow.

If you love untangling complex workflows, connecting systems and people, and turning messy problems into products people can depend on, we’d love to meet you.

💙 Perks & Benefits You'll Love

🏥 Health & Wellness:
  • 100% covered health, dental, and vision premium for employee-only standard plan (Family can join too, with a variable cost)
  • Employer Sponsored Short-Term Disability Coverage
  • Employer Sponsored Life Insurance
  • Optional group benefits: AD&D, long-term disability
  • Participation in a 401k plan through Empower
🎓 Growth & Development:
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Room for growth within the company
🏖️ Time Off to Recharge:
  • Paid Time Off: 10 vacation days, 5 sick days, 7 paid holidays + 3 floating holidays for ultimate flexibility
🐣 Parental Leave:
  • All Parents/Caregivers: 6 weeks fully paid
  • Birthing Parents: Up to 14 weeks paid
🏡 Work Style That Works for You:
  • Fully remote and flexible work environment—work from wherever feels right!
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the Autism healthcare space

📩 How to Apply

Use our applicant tracking system Pinpoint to answer the role-specific application questions. These questions were thoughtfully designed to give you more insight into the role and to give us more insight into you. Please write a thoughtful response—a human really reads these.
If you need accommodations during the application process, just let us know—we’re happy to help. 😊

jobs.excerpt: About BJAKThe original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money.
jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

About Sandy Hook Promise
Sandy Hook Promise (SHP) envisions a future where all children are free from school shootings and other acts of violence. As a national nonprofit organization, SHP’s mission is to educate and empower youth and adults to prevent violence in schools, homes, and communities. Creators of the lifesaving, evidence-informed Know the Signs prevention programs, SHP teaches the warning signs of someone who may be in crisis, socially isolated, or at-risk of hurting themselves or others and how to get help. SHP also advances school safety, youth mental health, and responsible gun ownership at the state and federal levels through nonpartisan policy and partnerships.

SHP is led by several family members whose loved ones were killed in the tragic mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School on December 14, 2012. 

Commitment to Belonging, Community, Engagement, and Respect 
SHP strives to ensure its culture and work environment reflect the values of belonging, community, engagement and respect. We actively seek to understand and respond to the diverse perspectives and lived experiences of individuals across socioeconomic backgrounds, rural and urban communities, and diversity of thought, in addition to traditional protected categories. We are committed to ensuring that every SHP employee feels heard, valued, and a true sense of belonging. SHP encourages individuals who share our commitment to these core values and to our mission to apply.  

Location
We are a U.S. based organization and most of our staff work remotely. This role will require 15% travel (on an as-needed basis). Candidates should reside within a reasonable distance (30-miles) of a major airport to ensure efficient, cost-effective travel. Team members are expected to make thoughtful travel decisions that balance cost, convenience, and sustainability.

About the Role
The Senior Director, Learning Architecture, Professional Learning serves as the organizational lead for designing and operationalizing high-impact, evidence-based learning strategies for educators, educational staff, administrators, and out-of-school time (OST) professionals at Sandy Hook Promise (SHP). This role is responsible for defining and carrying out a long-term vision for scalable, accessible, and effective professional learning across asynchronous, virtual, and in-person modalities that supports program fidelity, implementation quality, capacity development, and school and community impact.

Drawing on deep expertise in curriculum and professional learning design, development, and facilitation, this leader translates research into practical, user-centered learning solutions that support effective implementation of violence prevention programs. They provide leadership in train-the-trainer models, educational strategy, and cross-functional alignment to advance the strategic priorities, innovation, and program effectiveness of the organization.

Job Responsibilities

Strategic Vision & Ownership

  • Develop and lead the strategic vision for SHP's professional learning architecture, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, partner needs, best practices, and field trends.
  • Translate strategy into actionable plans, roadmaps, metrics, and accountability measures to drive implementation and results.

Professional Learning Materials

  • Oversee the design, development, writing, and continuous improvement of educator-facing materials, implementation resources, and tools that support high-quality program delivery and fidelity.
  • Manage external subject matter experts, consultants, contractors, and vendors to ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with organizational standards.
  • Ensure materials incorporate evidence-based approaches, implementation science, violence prevention, and related frameworks, while remaining practical and adaptable across school, district, OST, and regional settings.
  • Align all professional learning materials with the needs of program Implementation teams.

Train-the-Trainer & Professional Development Strategy

  • Lead the design, development, and writing of scalable train-the-trainer systems and professional learning offerings.
  • Direct the development of program-agnostic learning opportunities through SHP Learning Studio to meet evolving educator and staff needs.
  • Ensure learning experiences are aligned with adult learning principles, program theories of change, and implementation goals.
  • Partner across teams to integrate professional learning into training and technical assistance models.

Annual Planning, Monitoring & Reporting

  • Lead annual planning for the Professional Learning team, aligning priorities, resources, and improvement efforts with organizational goals.
  • Monitor progress through established metrics and provide regular updates to executive leadership on outcomes, risks, trends, and recommended adjustments.
  • Use internal and external data to identify opportunities for improvement and inform strategic decision-making.

Data-Informed Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Evaluation and Quality Improvement teams to pilot, assess, and refine professional learning offerings using feedback and impact data.
  • Establish and monitor KPIs related to engagement, learning outcomes, implementation quality, and program effectiveness.
  • Apply continuous improvement and implementation science principles to strengthen learning strategies and outcomes.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Represent professional learning on cross-functional committees, initiatives, and leadership forums.
  • Proactively identify, communicate, and address risks, opportunities, and operational challenges affecting goals, implementation, or sustainability.
  • Keep leadership informed of progress, challenges, and recommended actions to support timely decision-making and strategic adjustments.
  • Collaborate across departments to advance organizational priorities and support successful program implementation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned based on organizational needs.
  • A commitment to SHP’s mission and values.
Desired Skills and Experience
  • Master's degree or higher in Adult Education, K-12 Education, Curriculum & Instruction, or a related field required.
  • 7+ years of experience designing, developing, and writing professional learning for educators, youth-serving professionals, or related audiences.
  • 10+ years of experience working with K-12 school systems, out-of-school time (OST) programs, community-based education settings, or similar learning environments.
  • 5+ years of experience managing contractors, vendors, subject matter experts, or other external partners supporting educational products and programs.
  • Demonstrated expertise in adult learning principles, instructional design, and professional learning delivery across in-person, virtual, and asynchronous formats.
  • Proven ability to translate research, theory, and evidence-based practices into practical, educator-facing learning tools and resources.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives simultaneously.
  • Experience collaborating cross-functionally with diverse stakeholder groups to develop and implement educational programs and products.
  • Experience developing culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and inclusive learning materials for diverse educational settings and communities.
  • A professional learning sample designed and written by the applicant will be required for candidates advancing in the selection process.
Benefits and Salary Range
The salary range for this position is $110,000-$120,000.
SHP uses a structured internal rubric to guide salary placement and ensure equitable pay. Typically, new hires are placed at the start of the salary range to ensure equity with current employees, and as a practice, we do not negotiate salaries.

    • 401k match

    • Employer Paid Employee Assistance Program.
Our organization operates within a distributed workforce, allowing for location flexibility across the country for most positions. We provide remote office support for all staff, which includes a laptop, home office reimbursement, monthly Wi-Fi reimbursement up to $40, and monthly cell phone reimbursement up to $50.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Lending Operations Specialist - Remote

Here at Knock, we strive to always put people first and go above and beyond to service our partners and customers with our first-of-its-kind Knock Bridge Loan™. Knock enables borrowers to use the money “tied up” in their current home to purchase their next one. jobs.description:
Director, Client Delivery

Through our dedicated associates, Conduent delivers mission-critical services and solutions on behalf of Fortune 100 companies and over 500 governments - creating exceptional outcomes for our clients and the millions of people who count on them. You have an opportunity to personally thrive, make a difference and be part of a culture where individuality is noticed and valued every day.

Are you an experienced and results-driven professional looking for a challenging leadership role?

About this Role:

The Director, Client Strategy & Product is responsible for connecting client needs, market trends, HCS capabilities, and product strategy to improve the competitiveness, growth, and long-term value of the HCS portfolio.

This role works horizontally across the HCS client portfolio to identify common client needs, product gaps, emerging market requirements, and opportunities for service expansion. The leader serves as the primary bridge between Client Delivery, Product, Technology, Operations, Sales, and other stakeholders to ensure client and market insights are translated into actionable product priorities, service improvements, and growth opportunities.

Unlike Client Delivery, which owns individual client relationships and account-level growth, Client Strategy & Product is accountable for identifying portfolio-level opportunities, shaping solutions, influencing product and technology roadmaps, and enabling Client Delivery teams to bring differentiated HCS capabilities to clients.

The successful candidate will bring deep benefits administration domain knowledge, strong commercial and product acumen, executive presence, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate client and market needs into practical business and product strategies.

Responsibilities:

  • Establish and maintain a structured Voice of the Client process that captures client feedback, unmet needs, product requests, market observations, and emerging requirements across the HCS portfolio.
  • Analyze client feedback and account-level opportunities across the portfolio to identify recurring needs, common themes, product gaps, and opportunities that can create value across multiple clients.
  • Partner with Client Delivery leaders to identify potential cross-sell, upsell, product adoption, and service expansion opportunities.
  • Develop portfolio-level growth opportunities and solution concepts that Client Delivery and Sales can bring to appropriate clients.
  • Partner with Product and Technology leaders to translate client and market requirements into product strategy, roadmap priorities, enhancements, automation opportunities, and investment recommendations.
  • Establish structured communication and feedback loops between Client Delivery, Product, Technology, Operations, and Sales so that client needs and product developments are consistently understood across HCS.
  • Maintain a portfolio-level view of product utilization and adoption and identify opportunities to increase client adoption of existing HCS capabilities.
  • Evaluate HCS capabilities across clients to identify opportunities for standardization, reuse, and scalable solutions rather than developing unnecessary client-specific solutions.
  • Gather and synthesize market intelligence, competitive insights, advisor feedback, industry trends, and emerging client requirements to inform HCS product and service strategy.
  • Partner with Sales and Client Delivery to strengthen HCS positioning, value propositions, client presentations, and executive-level discussions.
  • Support Client Delivery on strategic client conversations requiring product, market, innovation, or broader HCS portfolio expertise.
  • Develop business cases for product investments, service enhancements, automation, AI capabilities, and other strategic initiatives based on client demand, revenue potential, competitive differentiation, risk, and financial return.
  • Partner with Operations and CoE & Risk to ensure product and service enhancements consider operational feasibility, scalability, regulatory requirements, controls, and delivery impact.
  • Maintain transparency into the HCS product roadmap and ensure Client Delivery leaders understand planned capabilities, timing, priorities, and dependencies relevant to their clients.
  • Establish mechanisms to communicate product developments and new capabilities to Client Delivery and Sales teams so that opportunities can be proactively introduced to existing clients.
  • Measure the business impact of product and portfolio initiatives, including product adoption, revenue opportunities generated, client value, and return on investment.
  • Create a culture of client-driven innovation, collaboration, commercial thinking, transparency, and disciplined prioritization.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • A total of 7+ years of progressive leadership experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and enable existing-client growth opportunities, including cross-sell, upsell, product adoption, and service expansion.
  • Experience generating qualified expansion pipelines and translating client needs into revenue-generating solutions.
  • Strong Voice of the Client expertise, with the ability to synthesize client feedback and market insights into actionable product and service strategies.
  • Experience aligning product roadmaps and investment priorities with client needs, market demand, and business objectives.
  • Proven ability to evaluate product performance, adoption, and investment ROI to drive measurable business outcomes.
  • Demonstrated success identifying opportunities for cross-client standardization, scalability, and reuse of products and services.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills, with experience partnering across Product, Client Delivery, Technology, and other stakeholders to advance strategic priorities.
  • Commercial acumen and a track record of translating product and portfolio initiatives into measurable revenue growth and client value.

Flexible Working

At Conduent, we want you to be yourself. We recognize that everyone is different and that how people want to work and deliver at their best is different for everyone too.
In this role, you can expect the following working conditions:

  • Remote work: Enjoy the convenience of working from home and maximize your time.
  • Flexible Working Hours: Flex the times you work during the day, allowing you to balance your home life and work.

Working For You

Perks and rewards designed for you:

  • Health and Welfare Benefits: Our health and welfare benefits can be tailored to fit your needs and start on the first day of employment.
  • Retirement Savings: We support you as you invest in your future.
  • Employee Discounts: We offer you access to a vast selection of global, national, and local discounts on merchandise, services, travel, and more.
  • Career Growth Opportunities: We help you thrive, so together, we can grow. We provide opportunities to advance your career with a vast portfolio of businesses and a global footprint.
  • Training: Earn while you learn and continue to grow with access to award-winning learning platforms throughout your Conduent career.
  • Great Work Environment: We are proud of our award-winning culture and the recognition we’ve received for our diversity efforts.

Join Us

At Conduent, we are one team, one mission. We understand that our success is directly related to the success of our associates. We strive to create a culture where you can:

  • Bring your authentic self to work.
  • Grow and thrive, both personally and professionally
  • Make a difference with our clients, in our communities, and with the millions of people we support.

When you join Conduent, you are engaged in creating the future - both our company’s and your own. With more than 60,000 associates across 24 countries, we will provide you the opportunity to grow with a team of people who will challenge and inspire you to be the best.

Pay Transparency:

Pay Transparency Laws in some locations require disclosure of compensation and/or benefits-related information. For this position, actual salaries will vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. In addition to base pay, this position, based on business need, may be eligible for a bonus or incentive. In addition, Conduent provides a variety of benefits to employees including health insurance coverage, voluntary dental and vision programs, life and disability insurance, a retirement savings plan, paid holidays, and paid time off (PTO) or vacation and/or sick time. Your primary responsibilities will include drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial, partnership, and energy storage agreements, assessing potential risks, and ensuring compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

About Voltus

Voltus aims to be the distributed energy platform that fulfills the promise of the energy transition. Voltus represents the "potential of us" to better manage energy through simple, cost and risk-free programs for distributed energy resources. Our commercial and industrial customers generate cash by allowing us to maximize the value of their operational flexibility in energy markets. What's more, there are significant community benefits that accompany working with Voltus – a cleaner, more reliable energy future and dollars invested back into your business.

Location

    Voltus is a fully-remote company, however, the candidate must reside in the United States and be authorized to work in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review, draft, negotiate, and interpret a wide range of energy and commercial contracts, including battery energy storage system (BESS) agreements, tolling agreements, power purchase agreements (PPAs), interconnection agreements, BESS equipment supply agreements, battery-specific safety, decommissioning, and end-of-life obligations, and other distributed energy resource contracts

  • Serve as senior legal advisor on structuring, negotiating, and closing battery storage and other energy storage transactions, working closely with commercial, engineering, and finance teams

  • Advise the sales and partnership teams on legal implications, risks, and opportunities associated with various commercial structures under consideration, and support those teams in achieving commercial objectives consistent with legal risk tolerance

  • Provide substantive guidance on regulatory and market-specific issues affecting energy storage and demand response transactions across ISO/RTO markets (e.g., PJM, ERCOT, MISO, NYISO), including storage participation models under FERC Order Nos. 841 and 2222

  • Utilize and build upon deep knowledge of legal issues relating to energy regulatory matters, IP, data use, privacy, and labor and employment law

  • Prepare, maintain, and improve template agreements, playbooks, training, and operational guidance for storage and commercial contracting

  • Mentor and provide guidance to junior members of the legal team on contract negotiation and energy industry matters

  • Work closely with teams across sales operations, product, finance, marketing, field operations, regulatory, and engineering to ensure terms align with company objectives and priorities

  • Help develop processes to ensure ongoing compliance with contractual commitments and provide practical, solutions-oriented advice to help client teams navigate issues that may arise

  • Define and implement best practices around workflow and process to further scale the legal department

  • Assist with ad-hoc legal matters as needed

Desired Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor degree from an accredited law school; strong academic credentials

  • Minimum of seven to ten (7-10) years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience in the energy industry (required)

  • Direct experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating battery energy storage system (BESS) contracts and related transactions (required)

  • Extensive experience drafting, preparing, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial agreements, particularly energy storage, PPAs, tolling agreements, strategic partnership, and product agreements

  • Working knowledge of U.S. energy markets, ISO/RTO structures, and regulatory frameworks governing distributed energy resources and energy storage

  • Experience with behind-the-meter or C&I-sited storage, and with storage participating in demand response or wholesale capacity/ancillary services markets is strongly preferred

  • Strong problem solving, innovation, and collaboration skills, as well as business acumen

  • Ability to independently manage a diverse and complex workload while maintaining priorities and anticipating issues

  • Excellent drafting skills and attention to detail

  • Able to perform quickly in a dynamic, fast-paced work environment to successfully multitask and manage deadlines

  • Experience working in Google Drive, Salesforce, Adobe PDF, Ironclad, and DocuSign strongly preferred but not required

Please note that at this time, we do not sponsor visas or transfers for new hires. Voltus teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location (in the US or Canada, unless otherwise indicated on the role description).


Additionally, while Voltus is an all-remote workplace, we have limitations on where employees are able to work for regulatory and security reasons. We expect that Voltans are working primarily from their home country. Working while traveling to other countries must be approved as per our Global Remote Travel Policy.

About the opportunity:

As the Manager, Business Operations (Business Development), you’ll be a driving force behind the growth and success of our partner ecosystem. You’ll strategically manage and strengthen existing partnerships while identifying and securing high-value new collaborations that align with our long-term vision. By leveraging your deep understanding of market dynamics, you’ll propose innovative tools and product solutions that unlock scalable opportunities for both our business and our partners.

This high-impact role involves collaborating closely with cross-functional teams—product, operations, data, and sales—to craft and execute partnership strategies that deliver lasting business outcomes. Reporting directly to the VP of Partnerships, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping the strategic direction of our partnership portfolio and accelerating growth across the organization.

Jerry is building the first super app to help people optimize all aspects of owning a car – insurance, buy/sell, registration, loans, safety, repairs, parking, etc – a $2T market in the U.S. We started with insurance in 2019, and since then we’ve launched loan refinancing, driving insights, a repair marketplace, car diagnostics, and a GenAI-powered chatbot & voicebot. We have amassed over 5M customers, raised $240MM in funding, scaled our revenue 60X and our team to 225 across 6 countries.

How you will make an impact:

  • Foster Strong Partner Relationships: Be the go-to person for building and nurturing deep, trusted relationships with existing partners. Your ability to serve as the primary point of contact will ensure long-term success and collaboration.

  • Drive Strategic Growth: Take ownership of developing and executing structured business plans or quarterly OKRs that align with each partner's unique goals, maximizing the potential of strategic partnerships through a deep understanding of their business.

  • Optimize Performance: Use your analytical skills to dive into data, uncover trends, and identify key opportunities for improving business KPIs. Your insights will be critical in driving smarter decisions and better outcomes for both sides.

  • Generate New Opportunities: Lead the charge in creating new growth opportunities with both existing and potential partners. Your expertise in negotiating will be key in structuring mutually beneficial deals that drive expansion.

  • Deliver Actionable Insights: Perform Analysis and regularly provide valuable insights and updates to both partners and internal teams, ensuring that everyone stays aligned, informed, and empowered to make the right decisions.

  • Resolve Challenges Quickly: Be the problem-solver, triaging operational and executional issues that arise across partners and internal teams. Your ability to act swiftly and decisively will keep everything running smoothly.

Ideal profile:

  • 4+ years of experience in Business Development, Partnerships, or Management Consulting

  • Proven track record of successfully managing complex projects from inception to completion, with meticulous attention to detail and a strong bias for action.

  • A go-getter with a strong work ethic, a willingness to learn and adapt quickly, and a desire to contribute to the success of a high-growth company.

  • A data-driven approach to decision-making, with the ability to analyze complex situations and make informed, actionable decisions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively communicate complex ideas to both internal and external stakeholders.

About Jerry.ai

Jerry is building the first AI-powered advisor to manage all your physical assets.

Your car, home, and motorcycle aren't just purchases, they're the physical embodiment of the life you've worked hard to build. Yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every step of the journey — buying, insuring, maintaining, repairing, selling — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Imagine having a trusted friend in your pocket who takes care of everything: they find you the right car or home at the right price, lock in the best insurance rate without you lifting a finger, remind you before that service appointment turns into an expensive repair, and help you sell at the best price when the time is right. That friend is Jerry.

We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, and achieved profitability in 2024. We're now expanding into home, motorcycle, RV, and beyond.

Led by serial entrepreneurs and backed by Y Combinator, our team comprises talented and big-hearted leaders from places like Nvidia, Meta, Amazon, BCG, McKinsey, Bain, and GEICO. Our culture is the #1 reason people join Jerry and stay — we are a small and mighty team of competitive but kind people who think and act like owners, care deeply about the quality and impact of our work, and are relentless in our pursuit of learning and mastery over our craft.

We are proud to consistently rank as one of Y Combinator's Top Companies, Forbes and Statista's Best Startup Employers, and to have received other accolades in fintech and insurtech innovation, workplace culture, and leadership.

We are a remote-first company, but if you prefer in-person or hybrid, we also have offices in Palo Alto, New York City, Chicago, and Toronto.

Job Description Summary


This position can be based remotely anywhere in the U.S. (there may be some restrictions based on legal entity). Please note that this role would not provide relocation as a result. The expectation of working hours and travel (domestic and/or international) will be defined by the hiring manager. This position will not require travel.

Take the lead in shaping the success of clinical trials at Novartis by driving complex contract negotiations that directly impact study timelines and patient access. As a Senior Contract Manager, you will play a critical role at the intersection of legal expertise, financial strategy, and clinical operations—partnering with global stakeholders to deliver high-quality agreements, unlock efficiencies, and resolve challenges with confidence. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact by ensuring trials start faster, run smoother, and ultimately bring innovative therapies to patients sooner.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Independently negotiate and execute complex clinical trial agreements, including Master Agreements and Confidentiality Agreements
  • Develop, review, and finalize clinical trial budgets, ensuring alignment with fair market value principles
  • Lead contract and budget negotiations with investigational sites to achieve timely contract execution and study start-up goals
  • Resolve stalled negotiations and provide strategic support to Contract Managers to maintain study timelines
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders including Legal, Regulatory, Quality, and Clinical teams
  • Identify, assess, and communicate contractual and budgetary risks to key stakeholders for approval
  • Collaborate with global and local teams to resolve complex contractual challenges efficiently
  • Analyze grant plans and budget proposals to support accurate and compliant financial decisions
  • Drive continuous improvement by identifying trends and leading initiatives to enhance contracting processes
  • Partner with clinical teams and vendors to optimize budgets and deliver cost-saving opportunities

Essential Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, legal, finance, science, or related field
  • 5+ years of experience in contract management within clinical trials or pharmaceuticals
  • Proven expertise in negotiating clinical trial agreements and complex contracts independently
  • Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical industry regulations and United States privacy requirements
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and project management skills with strong attention to detail
  • Advanced negotiation and conflict resolution skills in complex, multi-stakeholder environments
  • Ability to work effectively in a matrix organization with global and cross-functional teams
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with a customer-focused mindset

The salary for this position is expected to range between $89,600 and $166,400 per year.

The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors.

Location(s): US (remote), Boston (hybrid), New York (hybrid), San Francisco (hybrid)

Bready* to make a change?

Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy. Because our technology is purpose-built for restaurants, by restaurant people - and increasingly shaped by AI in both what we build and how we build - restaurants can trust that we'll deliver on their needs for today while investing in the experiences that will power their restaurant of the future.

Developer Experience builds the tools and platforms Toast engineers use to write, build, and understand their code. We own local development environments and the inner loop, build tooling and shared libraries, and the internal developer portal and self-service golden paths. We also empower developers across the company by building and maintaining the testing frameworks and core libraries used for developing web services. We contribute to the AI developer workflows that are changing how software gets built at Toast. Our goal is to make every engineer at Toast faster, more independent, and more confident in what they ship.

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to set the technical direction for how Toast engineers build software. You'll pick the highest-leverage problems in the developer workflow, design solutions that work across hundreds of services and many teams, and stay hands-on while you build them. AI is quickly changing what developer tooling can do, and you'll help define what an AI-native developer experience looks like at Toast.

About this roll* (Responsibilities)

  • Set technical direction and long-term architecture across Developer Experience's areas: local development, build tooling, shared libraries, and the developer portal.
  • Oversee the architecture of the testing frameworks and core libraries used for developing web services.
  • Stay hands-on: design, build, and ship the highest leverage and most cross-cutting parts of the platform yourself.
  • Collaborate with Product using data and direct engineer feedback to find the biggest sources of friction in the developer workflow, and help turn them into a prioritized, measurable roadmap.
  • Design self-service golden paths and paved roads that let product teams create and evolve services with minimal friction or hand-holding.
  • Drive technical alignment with partner teams in areas like AI, CICD and Cloud Infrastructure so the end-to-end developer journey feels like one cohesive experience.
  • Partner with customer-facing teams to align developer platform solutions with customer and business needs.
  • Raise the bar across the team through design reviews, mentorship, and code-pairing, and by growing other engineers into technical leaders.

Do you have the right ingredients*? (Requirements)

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience.
  • Deep expertise in at least one general-purpose language (e.g. Kotlin, Java, Go, or TypeScript) and comfort working across several.
  • Strong experience with build systems and dependency management at scale (e.g. Gradle, Maven, npm), including managing software migrations across hundreds of services.
  • A track record of leading technical initiatives across multiple teams, from defining the problem through design, delivery, and adoption.
  • Experience designing developer-facing products such as CLIs, SDKs, shared libraries, testing frameworks, or portals, with a focus on usability and adoption.
  • Hands-on experience with, and strong opinions about, AI-assisted development tools and agentic development practices.
  • Strong communication skills, including writing clear technical strategy and design documents and influencing without authority.
  • Deep empathy for engineers as customers, and a habit of measuring outcomes rather than shipping features.

What will help you stand out:

  • Experience with internal developer portals or service catalogs (e.g. Backstage).
  • Experience building or integrating LLM-powered developer tools, coding agents, or MCP servers.
  • Experience with containerized or cloud-based development environments (e.g. Dev Containers, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS ECS).
  • Experience defining and instrumenting developer productivity metrics (e.g. DORA, SPACE, build and test analytics).

AI at Toast

At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it’s a core part of our culture.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

The Impact of a Sr Security Engineer at Coupa:

Coupa's Security Engineers keep our enterprise, product, platform, and customer data safe. As a Senior Security Engineer, you'll take ownership of complex, ambiguous security problems end to end — building cloud security controls, setting engineering standards, and partnering closely with Engineering, IT, and Compliance to ship durable, automated security tooling rather than one-off fixes. You'll set the technical standard for how the team remediates and automates, and you'll be a go-to resource other engineers turn to when a finding needs real root-cause analysis instead of a quick workaround.

What You'll Do:

  • Design and implement multi-cloud security controls across Coupa's cloud environment, including VPC segmentation, security groups/NACLs, IAM policy design using least-privilege and permission boundaries, and Organizations/SCPs for guardrails at scale.
  • Build policy as code and IaC security guardrails and wire them into CI/CD as pre-merge and pre-deploy gates rather than after-the-fact reviews.
  • Harden containerized workloads and Kubernetes clusters — image scanning, admission control, pod security standards, network policies, and container/workload runtime detection.
  • Own vulnerability analysis of application packages, container images, and third-party dependencies; triage findings by exploitability and business impact rather than CVSS score alone.
  • Design and implement remediations (not just report findings) including secure code fixes, cloud configuration changes, and IAM policy adjustments using least-privilege principles.
  • Support incident response and forensics as a technical contributor — log analysis, root-cause investigation, and remediation validation using cloud-native and EDR tooling.
  • Partner with the Risk & Compliance team to provide technical evidence and control validation for audit frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP).
  • Support and mentor other security engineers — reviewing designs and remediation plans, sharing root-cause analysis techniques, and helping less experienced teammates work through complex or ambiguous findings.
  • Participate in the on-call/incident rotation and help continuously improve remediation and response runbooks.

What You Will Bring to Coupa:

  • 5+ years of experience in security engineering or cloud operations, with a track record of independently owning complex assessments from scoping through remediation.
  • Practical experience with cloud security fundamentals (AWS, GCP, or Azure) — IAM, networking, and common misconfiguration classes — sufficient to both find and fix cloud findings.
  • Strong scripting/automation skills in Python, Bash, or JavaScript, with experience building or extending internal security tooling.
  • Experience with dependency/container vulnerability scanning tools and integrating them into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Working knowledge of common compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP) and what auditable evidence looks like.
  • Critical thinking and root-cause analysis skills — comfortable digging past a scanner's output to understand and explain why a vulnerability exists.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills for translating technical findings into remediation guidance for engineers and risk context for stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Relevant certifications a plus: CISSP, CCSP, CISA, or AWS/GCP security certifications.

jobs.description:
Empower Pharmacy is a visionary healthcare company dedicated to making quality, affordable medication accessible to millions of patients nationwide. As the nation’s most advanced 503A compounding pharmacy and FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facility, we’re redefining what’s possible in personalized medicine and pharmaceutical manufacturing. We’re proud to be recognized as one of Houston’s fastest-growing private companies and ranked #116 in Healthcare & Medical on the Inc. 5000 List for 2025.

Our strength is built on four core values: People, Quality, Service, and Innovation. Guided by these principles, we’ve created a uniquely integrated healthcare platform powered by advanced technology, operational excellence, and a relentless commitment to patient care. From manufacturing and quality control to distribution and customer experience, our teams work together to raise industry standards, expand access to critical medications, and improve outcomes for patients and providers across the country.

At Empower, joining our team means more than starting a new role. It means becoming part of a mission-driven organization that’s transforming healthcare at scale. We invest deeply in our people, encourage bold thinking, and create opportunities for growth, leadership, and innovation at every level. Your ideas matter here, your development is supported, and the work you do has a direct impact on the lives of millions.

If you thrive in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment where innovation, collaboration, and ambition come together, Empower Pharmacy is the place for you. Let’s transform healthcare together.

POSITION SUMMARY

Prescribers put their name on every prescription, and they count on us to deliver the right medication, made right and on time. Our medications reach patients through prescribers, clinics, and telehealth partners. Many compounders work with the same molecules, and compliance shapes what we can say. That makes execution the difference: launches that land on schedule, pricing that protects margin, provider tools the field relies on, and prescriber-facing pages that convert.

As Product Marketing Manager, you’ll own one to two therapy lines with real revenue attached from day one, in areas such as hormone health, sexual health, aesthetics, and longevity. You’ll run launches end to end, keep the scorecard, execute pricing, and equip our sales team and partners to win. You’ll report to the Senior Director, Product Marketing, and work within the category strategy, pricing structure, and formulary roadmap that role sets.

This is a hands-on role with room to grow. You’ll work close to pricing and portfolio decisions, own the commercial metrics behind your lines, and help shape how we launch, with AI built into the workflow. It’s experience that prepares you for broader category and portfolio leadership, at a company where marketing has a seat at the growth table.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Launch Execution

  • Launch Management: Run launches in your therapy lines from workback plan to post-launch readout. Coordinate Clinical, Pharmacy Operations, Quality, and Regulatory at each step, and bring a clear recommendation to the go/no-go decision.
  • Launch Materials: Build provider materials, clinical reference resources developed with Medical Affairs, partner announcements, and web content. Carry each piece through Medical Affairs, Regulatory, and Legal review while keeping it clear and useful.
  • Launch Readouts: Track script volume, provider adoption, partner uptake, and reorders after each launch, then report results with recommended next steps.

Pricing Support

  • Price Execution: Implement pricing updates, bundles, and clinic volume tiers within the established pricing structure across the 503A and 503B channels.
  • Price Monitoring: Run regular competitive price checks across compounders and telehealth platforms in your therapy lines.
  • Margin Tracking: Monitor margin and partner economics, and catch margin erosion, unplanned discounting, and pricing risks early.

Category Scorecard

  • Performance Tracking: Maintain the scorecard for your therapy lines: script volume, provider acquisition and retention, reorder rates, and margin. Report monthly on what’s changing, why, and what to do about it.
  • Roadmap Inputs: Build the market research, competitive sizing, and demand signals behind new formulation business cases and forecasts, and use them to inform the formulary roadmap.
  • Field Intelligence: Join sales calls and provider conversations, review win/loss notes, and turn what you learn into messaging, pricing, and roadmap recommendations.

Provider and Partner Enablement

  • Sales Tools: Build battlecards, objection-handling guides, proof points, and pitch support with the sales team, and keep them current.
  • Partner Enablement: Create launch kits, onboarding materials, and ordering resources that help telehealth platforms and clinic partners bring your therapy lines to their prescribers.
  • Compliant Copy: Draft copy and new claims with Medical Affairs and Regulatory, carry them through MLR review, and turn approved language into pre-cleared language the team can reuse. Write for what’s approvable from the first draft.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
