Description

At Ledgebrook, we’re building a next-generation insurance infrastructure — fast, smart, and scalable — and are looking for a Director of Finance who can build Stonehaven’s finance and accounting infrastructure from the ground up to support the launch of Ledgebrook’s new third-party hybrid fronting carrier, Stonehaven Specialty Insurance Company.

This role reports to the Chief Operating Officer and works closely with the Stonehaven Operations and Claims team on bordereaux review and approval, and with Ledgebrook’s parent finance team as needed.

About the Role

Stonehaven is seeking a Director of Finance to build and own its finance and accounting infrastructure, turning third-party bordereaux data into trustworthy financials and a per-program economic picture. This role requires deep P&C statutory and GAAP accounting expertise, reinsurance accounting experience, and comfort standing up finance infrastructure at a new or early-stage carrier.

What You’ll Do

  • Establish the chart of accounts, GL, and month-end close process aligned to the NAIC Annual Statement from inception.
  • Participate in due diligence on prospective MGA and program partners, assessing financial strength, premium handling and trust account practices, and the quality of their bordereaux and financial reporting.
  • Review and approve incoming MGA and TPA bordereaux jointly with the Stonehaven Operations and Claims team before Shared Services posts them to the ledger.
  • Own the integrity of financial data flowing between Stonehaven and its MGA, TPA and reinsurance partners, with transaction processing (GL entries, AR/AP, cash and bank reconciliations) performed by Shared Services under this role’s oversight.
  • Ensure statutory (STAT) accounting and reporting are accurate, timely and compliant with NAIC requirements.
  • Own bordereaux-driven premium and loss accounting, reconciled to cash, ledger, and cessions with support from operations and technology resources.
  • Own reinsurance accounting: ceding commissions, recoverables, funds withheld, Schedule F, risk-transfer testing support.
  • Own fronting-fee revenue recognition and per-program economics reporting.
  • Establish capital-management practices reflecting reinsurance credit risk and the claims-pay-then-recover liquidity buffer; maintain the cash-flow model.
  • Support the Reserve Committee, the Audit Committee and the ORSA process.

About you

Here at Ledgebrook, we are passionate about creating a team that is on a continuous learning journey and that shares our excitement about building a company from the ground up. Some of the characteristics we hold dear are:

  • A passion to deliver world-class customer service experience to both internal and external customers.
  • Intellectual curiosity and desire to innovate processes/procedures versus being satisfied with the status quo.
  • A desire to continue learning through on-the-job mentorship or formal educational/training opportunities.
  • Agile prioritization skills coupled with a keen sense of urgency that seeks to balance getting it right versus getting it done right now.
  • A strong drive and desire to win together as a high-performing team.
  • A moral compass to “do the right thing, period”, with zero tolerance for toxic behaviors.

Requirements

Need to Have

  • ﻿10+ years in P&C insurance finance/accounting, including STAT and GAAP dual-basis reporting.
  • Direct experience with reinsurance accounting (ceded premium, recoverables, Schedule F).
  • Background in Delegated Underwriting Authority programs, whether at a program administrator or on the carrier side.

Nice To Have

  • CPA with P&C statutory accounting expertise.
  • Fronting or program-carrier finance experience, where bordereaux-driven accounting is the norm.
  • Experience standing up finance infrastructure at a new or early-stage carrier.
  • Rating-agency relationship experience (AM Best BCAR submissions specifically).

Benefits

  • Full remote flexibility and asynchronous work culture.
  • Unlimited PTO and fully paid sick leave.
  • Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus HSA and FSA options.
  • Additional financial protection and retirement benefits, including a 401(k), company-paid life insurance, and disability coverage

Actual compensation may vary based on a variety of relevant factors including experience, qualifications, geographic location and other relevant factors.

﻿For Candidates Applying From The U.S.:

Please note: This position is open only to candidates who are authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future employer-sponsored work authorization. We are unable to offer sponsorship at this time.

jobs.description:
Decile Group ( is transforming venture capital into a force for good in the world. We are working to launch 10,000 next-generation venture capital firms by 2030, fundamentally changing the face of venture capital.

We operate an integrated platform for modern venture capital, spanning education, software, and fund operations. VC Lab trains the next generation of fund managers. Decile Hub provides AI-enabled tools for fund operations. Start Fund enables managers to launch institutional-grade funds in under 24 hours. Decile Capital deploys capital into emerging managers. Together, these offerings make venture capital more accessible to anyone with world-class ideas and execution.

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join the Decile Group product team and own quality across Decile Hub and Start Fund. Read more about how Decile Group builds here:

This is not a role where someone hands you a test script and you follow it. Your job is to anticipate issues before they come up. You will build the QA system: the agents, the test plans, the release checks, and the habits that catch problems before a fund manager or LP ever sees them.

The ideal candidate is agentic from day one. You set up cutting-edge AI agents that test, monitor, and flag problems on their own. You understand our customers well enough to predict where they will get stuck, from a fund manager launching a fund to an LP logging in for the first time to sign documents or wire capital. You still bring the discipline of a classic QA: organized, thorough, and relentless about follow-through.

You don't need to come from a big company. You need to show us that you can catch what others miss.

Basic requirements:

  • You must live and work within a few time zones of Pacific (California) time.
  • You must be actively building with AI agents, not just using chat tools.
  • You must be able to own quality end to end without waiting for instructions.
  • You must be willing to get close to customers (calls, tickets, onboarding sessions) and turn what you learn into tests.

If you want to build the quality system for a platform that thousands of investors use to run their firms, you belong at Decile Group.

And we want to work with you too.

What You'll Do

  • Anticipate issues before release. Study each feature, the customer using it, and the flows around it, and find the problems before they ship. You are measured by what never reaches customers.
  • Build an agentic QA system. Set up and maintain AI agents that run regression tests, explore new features, check customer flows, and flag risks automatically. Keep improving them as the tools get better.
  • Know the customer. Learn how fund managers, LPs, and our internal teams actually use Decile Hub and Start Fund. Read support tickets, shadow onboarding calls, and turn real customer confusion into test cases.
  • Own the onboarding and login flows. Make sure every step a new LP or fund manager takes (invites, login, verification, documents, capital calls) works the first time, every time.
  • Run classic QA with discipline. Write test plans, maintain regression suites, track and triage bugs, and run release checks. Keep it all organized so anyone on the team can see what was tested and what is at risk.
  • Partner across Decile Group teams. Work closely with engineering, product, and customer success. When something breaks or looks risky, escalate early and clearly.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years in QA, test engineering, or a related role on a SaaS product
  • Hands-on experience building with AI agents and automation tools
  • A track record of catching issues before release, not just logging them after
  • Experience with test automation for web applications
  • Strong organization: test plans, bug tracking, and release checklists that other people can follow
  • Clear written communication. Your bug reports tell an engineer exactly what happened and how to reproduce it
  • Customer empathy. You can put yourself in the shoes of a first-time user and see where they will get lost

Nice to Have

  • Experience with venture capital, fund administration, or financial compliance workflows
  • Experience with Ruby on Rails applications
  • Experience testing onboarding, identity verification, or payment flows

How to Apply:

If you don't tick every box above, we'd still encourage you to apply. We're building a diverse team whose skills balance and complement one another.
Please describe why you are uniquely qualified for this position in the competitive field of Venture Capital, including an example of an issue you anticipated and caught before it reached customers, as well as submitting your resume.
Salary and benefits are commensurate with experience.

Scam Warning

VC Lab and Decile Group never conduct hiring interviews via chat, and we will never ask candidates to send money, purchase equipment, or share financial information. Scammers may impersonate real employee names. If you are contacted about a role outside our official channels, do not engage.

Reports to: Regional Sales Manager

Purpose of the Role

As an Account Executive (AE) for the West region, you will be responsible for driving new revenue growth for Cybernut through strategic acquisition of K–12 education customers. You will identify and close new business opportunities with school districts and education partners, helping them strengthen their Cybersecurity Awareness Training for both Staff and Students through Cybernut’s solutions.

West Territory (subject to change): CA, OR, WA, AZ, AK, UT, WY, MT, ID, ND, SD

Your goal is to generate new ARR, expand Cybernut’s presence in your territory, and represent the brand with professionalism, expertise, and enthusiasm.

Key Objectives

  • Own your territory develop and execute a go-to-market plan to acquire new customers across the West.

  • Drive new revenue by identifying, engaging, and closing opportunities with K12 school districts, charter networks, and education agencies.

  • Be a K12 industry expert – understand district challenges, funding sources, and procurement processes.

  • Represent Cybernut as a trusted advisor and brand ambassador within your region.

  • Deliver compelling demos that connect Cybernut’s value proposition to customer pain points.

  • Use consultative selling techniques to uncover needs and tailor solutions.

  • Collaborate with marketing, channel partners, and internal teams to drive pipeline generation and deal velocity.

  • Accurately forecast and maintain CRM (Hubspot) data for visibility and accountability.

  • Exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets through consistent, disciplined execution.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Prospect, qualify, and engage new leads within your assigned territory using a multi-channel approach (email, phone, events, referrals).

  • Manage the full sales cycle from discovery to contract signature for new Cybernut customers, or Cross Sell opportunities.

  • Deliver customized presentations and product demonstrations that speak directly to K–12 priorities.

  • Develop and maintain a healthy, predictable pipeline of new business opportunities.

  • Collaborate with Marketing to execute territory campaigns and lead generation activities.

  • Partner with internal Implementation Engineers to ensure smooth onboarding for new clients.

  • Represent Cybernut at trade shows, education conferences, and local industry events to build awareness and generate leads.

  • Stay current on competitor offerings, district funding trends, and market dynamics to position Cybernut effectively.

Performance Metrics

Your performance will be measured by:

  • Achievement of quota attainment (net new bookings and cross-sell bookings).

  • Volume and quality of qualified opportunities generated.

  • Contribution to team culture and alignment with Cybernut values.

Performance reviews will be supported through your 1:1 documentation of goals, initiatives, and achievements.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, and CRM platforms (HubSpot preferred).

  • Strong communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.

  • Business acumen and ability to align solutions to strategic district priorities.

  • Self-motivated, organized, and capable of managing a complex, multi-stakeholder sales process.

  • Ability to travel within the North East for meetings and events (up to 30%).

  • Resilient, resourceful, and results-driven.

jobs.excerpt: Hiring: Full-time - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Remote 🌟 About us, WeAssist, the hiring team 💡 🌍 Led by a Founder Who Cares– Reef Colman built WeAssist to empower individuals and create meaningful opportunities that support families.
jobs.description:
Hiring: Full-time - Chief Financial Officer (CFO) - Remote

🌟 About us, WeAssist, the hiring team 💡

🌍 Led by a Founder Who Cares– Reef Colman built WeAssist to empower individuals and create meaningful opportunities that support families.

⚡ Fast & Purposeful Recruiting– We move quickly but prioritize long-term fit, stability, and growth over just filling roles.

🌎 Connecting Global Talent– With 100+ outsourced professionals and growing, we link top talent worldwide with thriving US businesses.

❤️ Giving Back Matters– From building schools to feeding the homeless, we believe true success means making a difference.

🤝 An Inclusive & Thriving Culture– Your skills and unique gifts matter. We create an environment where outsourced professionals don't just work—they grow.

⚒️ Key Responsibilities of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) 📝

📈 Financial Planning & Projections

🔮 Forecasting & Scenario Modeling

💵 Budgeting & Cost Management

🌊 Cash Flow Management

📊 Financial Analysis & Reporting

🧭 Strategic Finance & Executive Partnership

🛡️ Controls, Compliance & Risk Management

⚙️ Finance Systems & Process Building

⚒️ Key Qualifications of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) 📝

Must-Haves:

  • 🎓 Proven Finance Leadership– Extensive experience in senior finance roles (CFO, VP Finance, Finance Director, or FP&A Lead), ideally within a growing, service-based or US company.
  • 📐 Financial Modeling Mastery– Expert at building forecasts, budgets, and multi-scenario models that leadership can actually make decisions from.
  • 📚 Strong Accounting Foundation– Deep understanding of GAAP, financial statements, accrual accounting, and month-end close.
  • 🌊 Cash Flow Expertise– Track record of managing liquidity, working capital, and runway in a scaling business.
  • 🧭 Core Values Alignment– Strong personal integrity and a clear fit with WeAssist's values around communication, ownership, emotional regulation, and excellence.
  • 🤖 AI Awareness & Proficiency– Solid understanding of modern AI tools and how to use them to speed up analysis and reporting.
  • 🗣️ Executive-Level Communication– Able to turn complex numbers into clear, actionable insights for the CEO and leadership team.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • 🏅 CPA, CMA, or CFA (Bonus)– A professional certification is a strong plus.
  • 🌐 Staffing / Recruiting or Agency Experience (Bonus)– Familiarity with placement-based revenue, recurring client billing, and contractor payroll.
  • 🇺🇸 US Tax & Entity Knowledge (Bonus)– Exposure to US tax considerations, multi-entity structures, or cross-border payments.
  • 💼 Fundraising / M&A Exposure (Bonus)– Experience supporting financing, investor reporting, or acquisitions.

Additional Information:

Review this Doc first!

How to Prepare for the Recruiting Process -

📢 Why Are We Hiring a CFO? 🏢

Our CEO, Reef Colman, is on a mission to reshape the future of remote work and create life-changing opportunities for talented professionals around the world. As WeAssist continues to scale—more clients, more Outsourced Professionals, and more moving parts—our financial strategy needs to grow just as fast. We're hiring a Chief Financial Officer to own our financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, reporting, and cash flow, and to become Reef's strategic partner in every major business decision.

This isn't a back-office seat. You'll build the financial foundation that powers WeAssist's next chapter of growth—turning numbers into clarity, clarity into decisions, and decisions into impact.

If you're a strategic finance leader who loves building forecasts, sharpening margins, and helping a mission-driven company scale with confidence—this is your moment to shine! 💼✨

Responsibilities of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO):

Your responsibilities include:

  • 📈 Financial Planning & Projections
  • Build and own WeAssist's annual financial plan and long-range (3–5 year) projections
  • Translate company goals and growth targets into clear financial plans and milestones
  • Model the financial impact of new services, pricing changes, hiring plans, and growth initiatives
  • Partner with the CEO on setting and tracking company-level financial targets
  • 🔮 Forecasting & Scenario Modeling
  • Maintain rolling monthly and quarterly forecasts for revenue, expenses, and profitability
  • Forecast revenue based on the client pipeline, placements, retention, and churn
  • Build best-case, base-case, and worst-case scenarios to guide decision-making
  • Regularly compare forecasts to actuals and refine assumptions
  • 💵 Budgeting & Cost Management
  • Lead the annual budgeting process and set department-level budgets with team leads
  • Monitor budget vs. actuals and flag variances early, with clear recommendations
  • Identify cost-saving opportunities and improve operational efficiency
  • Review vendor, software, and tool spend to ensure every dollar is working hard
  • 🌊 Cash Flow Management
  • Own daily, weekly, and monthly cash flow visibility and forecasting
  • Manage working capital, including receivables, payables, and collections timing
  • Ensure payroll for internal staff and Outsourced Professionals is always funded on time
  • Maintain healthy cash reserves and plan runway for upcoming investments
  • 📊 Financial Analysis & Reporting
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and management reports
  • Build and maintain executive dashboards and finance KPIs (gross margin, client profitability, LTV, CAC, revenue per placement, etc.)
  • Analyze profitability by client, service line, and team to inform strategy
  • Present clear, actionable financial insights to the CEO and leadership team
  • Contribute finance metrics to the company scorecard and leadership meetings
  • 🧭 Strategic Finance & Executive Partnership
  • Act as a strategic advisor to the CEO on growth, pricing, investments, and risk
  • Evaluate the ROI of new initiatives, hires, markets, and partnerships
  • Guide pricing and fee-structure decisions to protect margins as WeAssist scales
  • Support financing, banking relationships, and any future capital or M&A conversations
  • 🛡️ Controls, Compliance & Risk Management
  • Establish and maintain strong internal controls, approval workflows, and audit readiness
  • Oversee bookkeeping, month-end close, and reconciliations for accuracy and timeliness
  • Coordinate with external CPAs, tax advisors, and auditors on tax filings and compliance
  • Identify financial risks and put proactive mitigation plans in place
  • ⚙️ Finance Systems & Process Building
  • Design and document finance SOPs that scale with the business
  • Evaluate, implement, and optimize finance tools, integrations, and automations
  • Use AI and automation to streamline reporting, forecasting, and reconciliation
  • Mentor and guide any finance or bookkeeping support as the team grows

🏡 Get To Know WeAssist!

(Not your average Recruiting Firm…)

Started by Reef Colman just seven years ago, WeAssist is not your typical staffing agency... We are a dynamic recruiting firm focused on creating fair opportunities in the business world. We have a team of over 120 Outsourced Professionals. We help US businesses find skilled remote workers and connect these workers with good employers.

What makes us different is how much we care about our people! We give good benefits, support personal growth, and get involved in the community. We also support good causes like building schools, helping the homeless, and improving education. Come join us at WeAssist, where remote workers do their best! ✨

Company Culture and Core Values:

At WeAssist, we move fast, think big, and create lasting impact. 🚀 We're more than just a recruiting firm—we're a tight-knit community that values integrity, accountability, and growth, ensuring every professional and client finds the right fit, not just any fit. Here, you'll thrive in an inclusive, high-performance culture that challenges you to be 1% better every day while making a real difference in the world. 🌍✨

Our core values include:

  • 🧭 Integrity – Do the Right Thing, Always
  • Even when no one's watching, we lead with honesty, character, and trust.
  • 🎯 Expectation – Set the Target Early
  • We align from the start—no guessing games. Clarity creates confidence.
  • 🔁 Reiteration – Say It Back, Get It Right
  • We confirm understanding by repeating what we heard. Listening is a two-way street.
  • 🧱 Major Ownership – Being 1% Better Every Time
  • No blaming, no excuses. We take full responsibility and ask, “What can I do better?”
  • 🔍 Radical Transparency – Keep It Real
  • We speak with openness and honesty.
  • 🚀 Proactive Effort – Stay Ahead of the Game
  • We don't wait for fires—we prevent them. Anticipate, act, exceed.
  • 🗣️ Communication – Listen First, Speak with Clarity
  • We listen to understand, not just to reply. The clearer we are, the stronger we move!
  • 🧑‍💼 We Talk About Projects, Not People – No Gossip Zone
  • We go directly to the source. Discuss issues, not individuals—unless it's for solutions.
  • 🧠 Be Curious – Ask, Learn, Level Up
  • Curiosity drives growth. We ask smart questions and never stop learning.
  • 🧊 Emotional Regulation – Keep Cool Under Pressure
  • We stay calm, think clearly, and lead with emotional maturity—especially when it's tough.
  • 🏅 A-Player Mentality – Results Over Excuses
  • We get things done. Whatever it takes to win with integrity, we're in.
  • ➕ One More Mindset – Because It Matters to Someone
  • One more call. One more check-in. One more push. Every extra effort counts.

Join a team that values growth, action, and real impact—where what you do truly matters! 🎉

What's in it for you? 😏

Joining us means not just filling a role but embarking on a personal development journey. The growth potential is substantial, with opportunities to:

  • 🏛️ A True Seat at the Table– Work directly with the CEO and shape the financial strategy of a fast-growing, mission-driven company.
  • 🏗️ Build It Your Way– Design the finance function, systems, and processes from the ground up.
  • 🌱 Endless Growth Opportunities– Your role evolves with the company—take on more scope and leadership as WeAssist scales!
  • 💰 Competitive Compensation– Pay that reflects your experience, expertise, and impact.
  • 🎉 13th Month Bonus– Because we appreciate your hard work and dedication. Wild, right? 🤯
  • 🏆 Performance-Based Raises, Bonuses & Prizes– Your results directly impact your compensation!
  • 👨‍⚕️ Health, Dental, and Mental Health Insurance– Comprehensive coverage to take care of you inside and out.
  • 💡 Proactive, Collaborative, Supportive, and Forward-Thinking Environment– Work alongside passionate leaders who value your input!
  • 🌴 Permanent Remote Set-Up– Your office is wherever you want it—whether that's your couch, bed, or hammock!

This opportunity is ideal for a finance leader ready to make a meaningful impact on our journey to success! 🚀

Specifics:

Time

  • Full Time, PST Timezone
  • Be available during business hours to communicate responsively with the CEO and leadership team
  • This is a remote position so you can have the freedom to work from anywhere

Miscellaneous

  • Attire - business casual when in meetings
  • Professional setup (Pains me I actually need to write this down… 👀)
  • Clean background
  • Good camera
  • Good microphone
  • Strong wifi

Tech Stack

  • 🔑 Must-Have Skills (Baseline Requirement):
  • 📒 Accounting software – QuickBooks Online, Xero, or similar
  • 📊 Advanced Excel / Google Sheets – financial modeling, pivot tables, and dashboards
  • 🤖 AI tools – ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and prompt engineering to speed up analysis and reporting
  • 💬 Collaboration tools – Google Workspace, Slack, and project management platforms
  • ✨ Highly Preferred (The Dream Candidate Has These!):
  • 📈 FP&A / BI tools – e.g., Fathom, LivePlan, Power BI, Looker Studio, or Tableau
  • 💳 Payroll & payments platforms – e.g., Gusto, Deel, Wise, or Payoneer
  • 🧾 Billing & expense tools – e.g., Bill.com, Ramp, or Expensify
  • ⚙️ Automations – Zapier, Make.com, or N8N for finance workflows
  • 🔁 CRM familiarity (especially GoHighLevel) for pipeline-based revenue forecasting

Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits.

CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: System Administrator
jobs.excerpt: The MissionWe need a "Infrastructure Commander" to own, optimize, and fortify the backbone of our digital operations.
jobs.description:
The Mission

We need a "Infrastructure Commander" to own, optimize, and fortify the backbone of our digital operations. Your job is to manage our bare-metal virtualization layers, build highly available storage meshes, automate deployments, and safeguard our corporate parameters from internal workstations to high-performance web routing. This is a remote, high-availability role for a systems specialist who views infrastructure as code and infrastructure as a fortress.

We value technical depth, self-reliance, and precision over corporate pedigrees. Whether you are a Linux purist who builds high-performance clusters in your sleep or a seasoned network engineer who can spot a vulnerability before a scan finishes, we want you. If you have the drive to maintain absolute uptime across our servers, automate our operational loops, and audit our ecosystem with cold, calculating precision, you will find your home here.

Key Responsibilities

  • Virtualization & Storage Management: Architect, scale, and maintain our bare-metal hypervisors and highly available storage architectures, ensuring maximum data integrity and low-latency performance.

  • Environment Configuration: Deploy, harden, and scale our core Linux environment pools, using clean scripting and automated orchestration to keep configurations consistent.

  • Infrastructure Monitoring: Maintain absolute visibility over server health, application metrics, and infrastructure clusters, proactively hunting down system anomalies and resolving bottlenecks.

  • Outage & Incident Response: Stand as the front-line shield against unexpected downtime, troubleshooting system errors, server faults, and physical switch or routing issues with calm precision.

  • Security & Compliance Architecture: Deploy strict firewall rule sets, manage deep network routing loops, execute vulnerability scans, and maintain access controls to clear internal and external audits.

  • IT Logistics & Documentation: Manage internal user environments, build clear manuals for user access policies, handle technology tooling procurement, and run the IT backbone that keeps our global team secure.

The Technical Arsenal

You must possess deep hands-on expertise and deployment experience across the following stack:

  • Operating Systems: Linux Ubuntu (Advanced configuration, kernel tuning, and hardening).

  • Virtualization & Storage: Proxmox VE & Ceph (High-availability clustering, storage pools, block devices, and node management).

  • Databases & Web Servers: MySQL / MariaDB (Replication, indexing, queries) and Nginx (Reverse proxies, load balancing, SSL configuration).

  • Cloud & Automation: AWS (Core services infrastructure), Puppet (Configuration management), and Bash / Python scripting (Automating daily operations and maintenance patches).

  • Monitoring Systems: Nagios / Zabbix (Telemetry tracking, custom alerting rules, log aggregation).

  • Networking & Firewalls: pfSense, hardware switches, VLAN structuring, VPN routing, and clean network segmentation.

  • Corporate & Security Tools: Google Workspace (Identity provider provisioning, access paths), Vulnerability Scanning tools, and Penetration Testing frameworks.

The Requirements

Extraordinary Careers. Endless Possibilities.

With the nation’s largest home infusion provider, there is no limit to the growth of your career.

Option Care Health, Inc. is the largest independent home and alternate site infusion services provider in the United States. With over 8,000 team members including 5,000 clinicians, we work compassionately to elevate standards of care for patients with acute and chronic conditions in all 50 states. Through our clinical leadership, expertise and national scale, Option Care Health is re-imagining the infusion care experience for patients, customers and team members.

Our organization requires extraordinary people to provide extraordinary care, so we are investing in a culture that attracts, hires and retains the best and brightest talent in healthcare.

Job Description Summary:

Job Summary

The Sr. Facilities Manager is the accountable owner of the reactive and program repair and maintenance (R&M) vendor network that supports Option Care Health’s non-cleanroom facilities portfolio. This role runs the day-to-day performance of reactive service vendors and recurring program vendors, owns the maintenance and repair (R&M) program budget, leads emergency management and escalation, and builds and maintains the scopes of work for recurring programs.

The role is highly analytical and system-driven. The Sr. Manager uses the CMMS as the system of record for work orders, vendor performance, and spend, and translates that data into vendor decisions, scope refinements, cost controls, and clear reporting to Facilities leadership. The Sr. Manager partners closely with Operations, Patient Care leadership, Finance, Procurement, Construction & Design, Real Estate, Facilities Controlled Environments, and external vendors to keep sites safe, compliant, and operating.

Job Description: ​

Job Responsibilities (listed in order of importance and/or time spent)

  • Own the reactive and program R&M vendor model, including vendor selection, onboarding, performance management, escalation, and exit decisions across all trades.
  • Manage reactive service delivery: ensure work orders are dispatched, prioritized, completed, and closed within defined service levels, with clear ownership, aging control, and escalation paths.
  • Manage recurring program vendors (e.g., HVAC, refrigeration, generators, fire/life safety, pest control, janitorial, and exterior/snow/landscaping), ensuring services are delivered on schedule, to scope, and with documented proof of service.
  • Build, write, and maintain scopes of work for recurring programs, defining service frequencies, specifications by location type, and measurable performance standards; eliminate subjective or open-ended language and lead periodic scope reviews and re-bids.
  • Serve as the financial owner of the R&M program: develop and manage the annual budget, forecast and track spend by trade, location, and vendor, review and approve invoices, manage accruals with Facilities Analyst, AP, & Finance, and drive cost-avoidance and savings initiatives.
  • Lead emergency management for the facilities portfolio, including severe weather preparedness, outage and flooding response, vendor mobilization, executive and site communication, and post-event recovery and reporting.
  • Own CMMS discipline: ensure all work, assets, vendors, and costs are accurately captured and routed through the CMMS; define workflows, data standards, reporting, and dashboards; and partner on system configuration and continuous improvement.
  • Analyze CMMS and financial data to identify trends, recurring failures, repeat-call locations, aging work orders, SLA performance, PM compliance, and spend variances; convert findings into corrective actions and recommendations.
  • Establish vendor governance, including onboarding standards, insurance and compliance requirements, rate and pricing review, scorecards, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs).
  • Provide recurring operational and executive reporting on program performance, vendor performance, emergencies, spend versus budget, and risk.
  • Serve as an escalation point for Operations and Patient Care leadership on facility issues that affect patient care or business continuity, ensuring timely communication and resolution.
  • Develop standard operating procedures, checklists, and playbooks that standardize how work is requested, approved, executed, and closed out.
  • Support capital planning by identifying end-of-life assets and recommending repair-versus-replace decisions based on asset history and cost data.
  • Lead, coach, and develop facilities managers, coordinators and/or analysts supporting the program.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This position has direct supervisory responsibilities, including hiring, performance management, and development of facilities managers, coordinators and/or analysts supporting the program.

Basic Education and/or Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business, or a related field preferred (or equivalent experience).
  • 7+ years of progressive facilities management experience, including vendor management, CMMS administration, and budget ownership across a multi-site portfolio.

Basic Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience managing reactive and recurring R&M vendors across multiple trades and multi-site portfolios.
  • Hands-on CMMS experience (work order, asset, vendor, and invoice management), including reporting and dashboard development.
  • Strong analytical skills, including advanced Excel and the ability to turn work order and spend data into decisions.
  • Proven financial accountability for a maintenance or R&M budget, including forecasting, invoice approval, and variance management.
  • Experience leading emergency response and business continuity for multi-site facilities.
  • Experience writing and managing scopes of work, service-level expectations, and contracts for recurring programs (e.g., janitorial, HVAC, pest control, fire/life safety, grounds/snow).
  • Working knowledge of building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, generators, fire/life safety) sufficient to validate vendor findings and proposals.
  • Strong communication and influence skills with the ability to partner with operational, clinical, finance, and vendor stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels in a fast-paced, distributed environment.

Physical Demand Requirements

  • Primarily office-based or remote work, with periodic site visits to buildings, mechanical spaces, and rooftops; may require ladder use and light tools.

Travel Requirements

  • Ability to travel up to 25% for site visits, vendor meetings, and emergency response, including on short notice.

Preferred Qualifications & Interests (PQIs)

  • CFM or equivalent facilities certification.
  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy, or other regulated multi-site environments.
  • Experience with enterprise CMMS, and with vendor RFP and transition execution.
  • Experience with building and executing on centralized programs.
  • Experience with Power BI or similar analytics tools.

jobs.description:
Metric Systems LLC is a direct‑hire employer partner dedicated to helping companies connect with the right talent for their open roles. We are not a staffing agency—instead, we work alongside employers to identify strong candidates, streamline the hiring process, and support both sides through each step. Once hired, you become an employee of the client organization directly, ensuring a seamless transition into your new role and long‑term career alignment.

My client is building a Fuze product line within its Weapons & Networked Solutions (WNS) business unit to support next-generation programs including the Terrain Shaping Obstacle (TSO), autonomous ground munitions, and precision guided weapon fuzing. The organization seeks a Principal Systems Engineer with deep, hands-on expertise in Electronic Safe Arm Fuze and Device (ESAD/ESAF) design, verification, and manufacturing to anchor this team and mentor the next generation of fuze engineers.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the end‑to‑end development of fielded fuze systems from initial concept through full safety certification.
  • Prepare, present, and guide fuze designs through WSESRB, NNMSB, and AFSRB review processes.
  • Work directly with Army, Navy, Air Force, and DoD laboratory teams to advance fuze engineering efforts.
  • Leverage established relationships across military branches to accelerate approvals, resolve technical issues, and support program success.
  • Architect and develop ESAD/ESAF components, including ESD, S&A, and firing chain elements, ensuring compliance with MIL‑STD‑1316 and MIL‑STD‑1911.
  • Build sensing mechanisms that detect critical environmental conditions such as release, setback, spin, and all‑up‑round dynamics.
  • Create qualification test plans aligned with JOTP, MIL‑STD‑331, and MIL‑STD‑810; conduct environmental testing and perform failure analysis and root‑cause investigations.
  • Design electrical or electromechanical S&A devices that meet safety, reliability, and operational requirements.
  • Build and validate electronics for safety‑critical and mission‑critical fuze applications.
  • Create and qualify capacitor discharge units (CDU) and EFI selections; perform or oversee HERO margin analysis to ensure safe operation in electromagnetic environments.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, or a related Science, Engineering or Mathematics field
  • 10 years of relevant experience; or Master's degree, plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience.
  • ESAD/ESAF Architecture & Design (Expert): Led design of fielded ESAD/ESAF; can independently architect ESD, S&A, and firing chain; Experience designing systems compliant to MIL-STD-1316 or MIL-STD-1911
  • Environmental Sensing design (Expert): Designed sensing systems that sense environment conditions such as release, setback, spin, and all-up-round environments
  • Environmental testing of fuze systems (Expert): Designed qualification tests for fuzing systems iaw JOTP, MIL-STD-331, and MIL-STD-810; performed environmental qualification; performed failure and root cause analysis on failures
  • Safe and Arm (S&A) mechanism design (Expert): Designed electrical or electromechanical S&A devices
  • High reliability electronics (Advanced): Experience designing high reliability electronics systems for safety critical or mission critical systems
  • Firing chain design (CDU / EFI) (Advanced): Designed capacitor discharge units; selected/qualified EFI. Experience performing or overseeing HERO margin analysis
  • Self-destruct / self-neutralize design (Advanced): Designed self-destruct/neutralization mechanisms to reduce UxO
  • Fuze system-level requirements decomposition (Advanced): Traces system requirements to ESD, S&A, firing circuit, and software; manages RVTM
  • Target detection & classification (Intermediate): Working knowledge of magnetic influence, seismic, acoustic, or pressure-based target sensing systems
  • Built-in test (BIT) design for fuze systems (Advanced): Designed continuous and power-on BIT for S&A, battery, and sensor health; fault lockout logic; experience with BIT coverage analysis
  • Active Secret clearance

Highly Desired:

  • AFSRB board presenter: Has personally presented to the AFSRB — extremely rare; commands immediate credibility within the Air Force fuze community
  • Multi-service fuze programs: Delivered fuzes for two or more military services (Army + Navy, or AF + Army), demonstrating breadth across service-specific requirements
  • Proximity fuze / active sensing: Designed active proximity fuze systems (RF, laser, acoustic) in addition to passive influence fuzing
  • Autonomous system integration (UAS/UGV payloads): Integrated fuze with autonomous delivery platforms
  • MOSA / open architecture fuzing: Designed fuzes to modular open systems architecture (MOSA) principles; plug-and-play payload integration
  • Digital twin / simulation: Built quantitative physics-based fuze simulations for firing chain timing, magnetic signature modeling, or safety FTA
  • Picatinny / NSWC / AFRL lab background: Government lab background in fuze engineering — brings inside understanding of Government test and qualification processes
  • University relationships: Maintains academic connections (Colorado School of Mines, Penn State ICT, Auburn, Purdue, Texas A&M ballistic programs) for talent pipeline support

This position is fully onsite or hybrid/flex with opportunity to be fully remote/telework for candidates with strong experience and background. If remote, 25% travel to Ft. Wayne, Indiana site with possibility of surge support based on scheduled events.

We welcome and consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected under federal, state, or local law. Job Summary

At EDB, we are committed to delivering an exceptional employee experience across our global workforce in the Americas, Europe, and India. We are seeking an experienced Workday, Payroll & HRIS Specialist to support our global HR technology, payroll operations, employee data, and HR processes.

The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with Workday, payroll operations, HR data management, and advanced Excel, along with a strong understanding of global HR processes. This role will partner closely with HR, People Partners, Payroll, Finance, Talent Acquisition, and other stakeholders to ensure accurate, efficient, and scalable HR operations.

The role will be responsible for Workday administration and data integrity, payroll-related processes and audits, reporting and analytics, process documentation, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement.

  1. Workday Administration & HRIS Operations
  • Serve as a Workday subject matter expert and key point of contact for HR stakeholders.
  • Manage and support Workday processes across the employee lifecycle, including hires, transfers, promotions, compensation changes, organizational changes, and terminations.

  • Support Workday business processes, approvals, security, reporting, and data audits.
  • Troubleshoot Workday issues and partner with relevant teams to identify root causes and implement solutions.
  • Support Workday releases, testing, enhancements, and system optimization.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify and automate HR processes using Workday and other technology solutions.
  1. Payroll Operations & Compliance Support
  • Support payroll processes across relevant geographies, working closely with payroll vendors, Finance, and HR teams.
  • Ensure accurate and timely payroll inputs from Workday and other HR systems.
  • Perform payroll data validation, reconciliation, and variance analysis.
  • Investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies, employee pay issues, and data-related errors.
  • Support payroll audits, year-end activities, reporting, and compliance requirements.
  • Partner with Finance and Payroll teams to ensure accurate employee, compensation, deduction, and payroll data.
  • Support payroll-related Workday integrations and downstream systems.
  • Maintain payroll process documentation and SOPs.
  1. Reporting, Analytics & Advanced Excel
  • Develop and maintain Workday reports, dashboards, calculated fields, and HR analytics.
  • Use advanced Excel to analyze, reconcile, and validate large HR and payroll datasets.
  • Create complex spreadsheets using functions such as XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, IF/IFS, Pivot Tables, and conditional logic.
  • Build data validation and reconciliation tools to identify discrepancies between Workday, payroll, and other systems.
  • Develop dashboards and reports that provide actionable insights to HR and business leaders.
  • Support workforce, payroll, compensation, headcount, and organizational reporting requirements.
  • Maintain strong data integrity and confidentiality when handling sensitive employee information.
  1. Process Improvement & Automation
  • Identify opportunities to improve HR, Workday, payroll, and HRIS processes.
  • Standardize and simplify processes across regions while accounting for local requirements.
  • Support automation initiatives using Workday, ServiceNow, Jira, Excel, and other technology platforms.
  • Develop and maintain detailed SOPs, process documentation, and knowledge resources.
  • Participate in HR technology projects, system enhancements, integrations, and process transformation initiatives.
  • Stay current with Workday functionality, payroll technology, HR technology, AI-enabled tools, and industry best practices.
  1. Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Partnership
  • Partner closely with HR, People Partners, Payroll, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Compensation, IT, and external vendors.
  • Act as a trusted partner for resolving Workday, payroll, employee data, and HR technology issues.
  • Communicate issues, root causes, recommendations, and resolutions clearly to stakeholders.
  • Manage multiple priorities while maintaining high levels of accuracy and service.
  • Support global HR initiatives, organizational changes, acquisitions, and other HR transformation projects.

What You Will Bring

About the Team

Launched in 2021, Fanatics Betting and Gaming is the online and retail sports betting subsidiary of Fanatics, a global digital sports platform. The Fanatics Sportsbook is available to 95% of the addressable online sports bettor market in the U.S. Fanatics Casino is currently available online in Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. Fanatics Betting and Gaming operates twenty-two retail sports betting locations, including the only sportsbook inside an NFL stadium at Northwest Stadium. Fanatics Betting and Gaming is headquartered in New York with offices in Denver, Leeds and Dublin.

As a Senior Manager, Content Amplification at Fanatics Betting & Gaming (FBG), you are here to… help us create an entertaining betting proposition that appeals to Fanatics customers. Reporting into the Director of Sportsbook Content, you will play an integral role in the Sportsbook Content team, as well as the wider Fanatics Betting & Gaming. Sportsbook Content Analysts will work to prepare and manage a range of daily custom offers that differentiate the Sportsbook and integrate seamlessly with the features of the Fanatics Betting & Gaming product.

The Role

Own the paid amplification layer that supports organic content and creator output. This role takes what's produced by the content and creator teams and makes sure it reaches scale through smart amplification. The mandate is awareness and share of voice.

What You'll Own

Amplification Strategy & Execution

  • Run boosting across owned, creator, and aggregate accounts, prioritizing spend against content that's already showing organic traction
  • Build and operate the programmatic amplification engine that fires off real-time performance thresholds, in lockstep with the Programming/Real-Time Response function
  • Set and manage the paid boosting budget as part of the Senior Director's annual portfolio, forecasting spend against content calendar and moment-driven opportunities
  • Prioritize CPM-based media buys over CPA/CPC structures. This role is bought for reach efficiency and brand exposure, not click or install performance, and should be evaluated on cost per thousand impressions against benchmark, not cost per acquisition
  • Split amplification spend and reporting across the two brand mandates, Fanatics Sports & Casino and Fanatics App, so awareness lift can be attributed to each rather than blended into a single top-line number

Measurement

  • Report against reach, non-follower reach, engagement, and share of voice, the same scoreboard the Senior Director owns, not payback or CPA
  • Build a clean read on amplification's contribution to unaided awareness, separate from any conversion-tied media
  • Maintain the boundary: no SUO, promo code, or conversion mechanic runs through this budget. Anything with a payback requirement gets routed to Performance Media, full stop
  • Goaled on CPM efficiency and reach delivery against target, not conversion volume. Any deal structured on CPA, CPC, or revenue share gets flagged and routed to Performance Media rather than counted toward this role's targets
  • Track unaided awareness and brand favorability lift for Fanatics Sports & Casino and Fanatics App as the primary success metrics, with share of voice and non-follower reach as leading indicators between brand studies
  • Report media efficiency in CPM terms against category benchmarks (sportsbook, casino, and broader app-based competitors), not against payback multiples

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Partner with Performance Media on shared platforms (paid social, CTV/OLV) where buying responsibility is split, per existing delineation guidelines
  • Coordinate with Creator & Talent on which creator content gets amplification support and at what threshold

What You’ll Bring

  • 4+ years in paid social or programmatic media buying, with direct experience in reach/awareness-oriented (CPM) buying rather than performance/direct response
  • Experience building or operating a programmatic, rules-based amplification engine triggered by performance thresholds
  • Fluency in reach, non-follower reach, engagement, and share of voice as primary success metrics, and comfort being evaluated on CPM efficiency rather than CPA/CPC
  • Experience managing a paid media budget and forecasting spend against a content calendar
  • Judgment to flag and route any CPA, CPC, or revenue-share-structured deal to Performance Media rather than absorbing it into this budget
  • Experience in sports, betting, gaming, or a comparable fast-moving consumer category is a plus

jobs.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

This is an opportunity to build your career in communications at a fast-growing fintech that's reshaping SME finance. You'll be part of iwoca's external communications team, helping drive coverage across our expanding product portfolio, working on data-led campaigns and supporting our work with government and policymakers.

Our comms function works across the business to position iwoca as a leading voice in SME finance. You'll collaborate closely with Product, Commercial, and Executive teams to translate business priorities into compelling narratives that drive both brand awareness and customer acquisition.

The role

We're looking for a Communications Executive with up to two years' experience to join our UK comms team. Working alongside the team, you'll help publish our major data-driven campaigns, own the communications for a couple of our newest products, and support our public affairs and policy work. You'll also help with the BAU media activities that keep iwoca front-of-mind with key journalists and stakeholders.

Examples of the type of work you'll be doing:

1. Support data-driven PR campaigns

Working with the team, you'll run several established data-driven campaigns:

  • Top 25 UK Cities for SME Jobs: Our annual ranking combines ONS employment data, business figures, and economic indicators. You can refine the methodology if needed, analyse the latest data, and craft narratives for regional and national media.

  • SME survey research: Twice a year you'll help commission original survey research, working with established research partners to design questionnaires capturing timely SME sentiment. You'll help ensure we generate "business news" coverage that responds to real economic issues.

  • You'll be comfortable working with raw datasets - not just presenting finished analysis. Spotting surprising findings, identifying regional variations, understanding which angles interest journalists versus policymakers.

2. Start shouting about our new products

You'll eventually own the communications for a couple of iwoca's newest products, working directly with Venture Leads to drive awareness and customer acquisition. Here are a few we've just launched that you could be working on:

  • Credit Compass: Our credit-building tool helping SMEs improve their scores. You'll identify customer success stories, translate credit score trends into compelling narratives, and position this as iwoca's answer to the credit access gap.

  • SME Insurance: Help launch this proposition to market - identifying angles around why SMEs need this product and announce new strategic partners as and when we secure them.

  • iwoca Credit Card: You'll be involved from the ground up - understanding competitive positioning, identifying what's newsworthy in a crowded market, building a launch campaign that breaks through.

  • iwocaPay (launched in 2020): Our instant payment solution - you'll help scale awareness as this product continues to grow, finding ongoing news hooks beyond what we've already done in recent years.

  • For each product, you'll get under the hood with the Venture Leads - understanding commercial objectives, customer pain points, competitive landscape - then translating that into comms plans that drive both coverage and business outcomes. You'll own two products, with the split decided once you're in the job.

3. Support our public affairs and policy work

iwoca works with government and policymakers to make the case for better access to finance for small businesses. You'll support this work, engaging with relevant government departments, industry bodies and ministers where relevant. This could include:

  • Tracking policy and regulatory developments that affect SMEs and SME lending.

  • Helping draft consultation responses, policy briefings and position papers.

  • Using our lending and survey data to build the evidence behind our policy positions.

  • Preparing briefing materials for meetings with officials, industry bodies and ministers.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Up to two years' experience in communications, PR, public affairs, policy, journalism or a related field. Internships and placements count, and we welcome recent graduates.

  • Excellent writing skills with the ability to craft data-driven stories, press releases, briefing materials, and media pitches that cut through.

  • Ability to work at pace across multiple projects simultaneously, with strong organisational skills.

  • You'll need to be confident managing and analysing data with either Excel or Google Sheets.

  • A genuine interest in the economy, policy and politics, and how they affect small businesses.

Bonus:

  • Some experience in, or a strong interest in, tech, fintech, financial services or B2B technology.

  • Experience in public affairs, policy or government relations, or an understanding of how policy is made.

  • Any exposure to product launches or translating complex propositions into accessible narratives.

  • Experience pitching to journalists or securing coverage in relevant press.

  • Comfortable working with senior stakeholders.

jobs.excerpt: Senior Product Manager (Data Cooperative & Activate) Company OverviewInfutorData, an ActiveProspect company, delivers privacy-compliant consumer identity and data solutions that help marketers find, understand, and reach the right people.
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager (Data Cooperative & Activate)

Company Overview

InfutorData, an ActiveProspect company, delivers privacy-compliant consumer identity and data solutions that help marketers find, understand, and reach the right people. Our identity graph covers roughly 250 million US consumers and 120 million households. We are now building a transparent, consent-based data cooperative for consumer lead-generation publishers, and we are looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead it from concept to launch.

Job Summary

As Senior Product Manager, Data Cooperative & Activate, you will own a new publisher data cooperative and the Activate product line it powers. Publishers contribute on-site and form data under clear, documented terms. In return, they receive member services such as industry analytics and benchmarking, data appends, fraud and bot detection, and identity resolution.

This is a 0-to-1 build with a direct line to revenue on an established product line. You will design the member value exchange, sign and onboard publisher members, align other product teams around a shared member offering, and work with Engineering and Data to deliver the collection script, data feeds, and member services. You will work closely with Legal, Privacy, Sales, Finance, and an outside consulting firm, with regular exposure to executive leadership.

The role is an equal blend of partnership and product management. You should be as comfortable negotiating a data-sharing agreement with a publisher as you are writing acceptance criteria with an engineer.

Responsibilities:

Co-op Strategy & Member Value Exchange

  • Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the publisher data cooperative.
  • Define what members contribute and what they receive, including tiering (for example, Core and Premium) based on publisher discovery.
  • Build and test member value propositions; decide which benefits lead and how to prove their value.
  • Scope and launch member industry analytics (benchmarking and trend reporting) with the Data team, protecting each member's data in aggregate reporting.
  • Model co-op economics and data-licensing value to inform packaging, pricing inputs, and investment decisions.

Publisher Partnerships

  • Own the publisher pipeline from discovery through signed member agreement and onboarding.
  • Lead conversations with publisher members and prospects on value exchange, integration, and data-use terms.
  • Facilitate a Publisher Advisory Board to validate the model and gather ongoing feedback.
  • Work with Legal and outside advisors to standardize member agreements and data-use terms.
  • Select and launch pilot publishers, then scale membership month over month.

Cross-Product Collaboration

  • Inventory existing products that can be offered to members (for example, API data appends, identity resolution, fraud and bot scoring).
  • Partner with other product managers on what is included, at what tier, and on what timeline.
  • Define packaging, entitlements, and member-facing positioning for bundled services.
  • Identify new data products and member services that can be built on co-op data.

Activate Product Line

  • Own the Activate roadmap, pricing inputs, and inventory health.
  • Plan the transition of current Activate data sources into the co-op model so inventory holds during cutover.
  • Partner with Sales and Finance on revenue attribution and commercial performance.

Execution & Delivery

  • Write clear requirements and acceptance criteria with Engineering and Data for the collection script, scheduled data feeds, and member services.
  • Define POC scope and success criteria with Data and Engineering.
  • Work through dependencies across data infrastructure, identity, and integration teams.
  • Build privacy into the program by design, including publisher notice and opt-out requirements, recertification, and consumer opt-out and deletion handling.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate research, requirements, analysis, and prototyping.

Governance & Measurement

  • Set up program governance: KPIs, operating cadence, and decision forums.
  • Report program health to leadership, including members signed, data volume, match rates, data quality, churn, and revenue.
  • Build a repeatable operating model for membership growth and member retention.

What Success Looks Like

  • First 90 days: Move committed advisory publishers toward signed member agreements. Define the value exchange and tiering. Agree on partner products for the member offering. Finalize POC scope and name pilot publishers. Build the Activate transition plan.
  • 12 months: Co-op launched publicly. Pilot publishers live on the script and data feed. Activate inventory at or above baseline. Member agreements standardized. Industry analytics and at least two partner products live in the member offering.
  • 18 months: Membership growing month over month. At least one new data product or member service built on co-op data. Clear revenue attribution to the co-op.

Qualifications and Skills

  • 6+ years in product management, partnerships, or data products.
  • 2+ years working at or with a data cooperative or data-sharing network (for example, offline/catalog co-ops, identity networks, or data collaboration platforms).
  • A track record of recruiting, negotiating with, and managing data partners.
  • Experience building value propositions, member benefit programs, or tiered data product offerings.
  • Working knowledge of data licensing and co-op economics.
  • Experience writing PRDs and acceptance criteria for data products.
  • Understanding of on-site tags, data feeds, and basic data analysis.
  • Sound privacy judgment and experience working with Legal on consent, opt-outs, and US state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and others).
  • Strong negotiation, executive communication, and influence without authority.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and building from scratch.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in lead generation or performance marketing, especially on the publisher side.
  • Identity resolution or identity graph product experience.
  • Experience launching a new co-op or data network.
  • Familiarity with Snowflake, JavaScript tag or SDK products, consent management platforms, GPC, or hashed-identifier matching.
  • Public speaking at industry events and advisory board facilitation.
  • MBA or a degree in a quantitative field.
  • Spanish language skills.

Reports to:

  • VP of Product Management

jobs.description:
About the Role

We are looking for a rigorous, systems-minded quantitative leader to own our core commercial intelligence engine end-to-end. This is not a traditional dashboard-building or BI reporting seat. You will define, build, and encode the mathematical logic, unit-economic models, and predictive forecasting systems that power our product and drive real commercial decisions for our brands.

You will sit at the intersection of finance, data science, and product engineering, turning complex commercial data, messy founder inputs, and predictive models into defensible, automated product logic and AI agent workflows.

Key Accountabilities

1. Proprietary Systems: Growth Forecasts & P&Ls

  • Growth Forecasting: Build and own the methodology that takes a brand’s current performance and projects a defensible 12-month forecast, complete with a rigorous assumption set.

  • Financial Architecture: Construct brand-level P&Ls directly from the forecast, mapping revenue, COGS, contribution margin, and operating costs.

  • Variance & Calibration: Continuously run models against real outcomes, measure errors, track actuals against projections, and explain every variance.

2. Productization & Agentic Workflow Design

  • Product Logic: Translate sophisticated financial and statistical models into production-ready product logic so the system calculates and delivers outputs natively.

  • AI Agent Specification: Define what data agents compute, what internal data/benchmarks they draw on, and what assertions they are strictly barred from making.

  • Human-in-the-Loop Orchestration: Replace manual validation with automated product rules while establishing clear review gates for human sign-off before deliverables ship.

  • Data Schemas & Engineering Collaboration: Specify data structures, validation rules, and pipelines across structured commercial inputs, partnering directly with engineering to bring models to life in production.

3. Decision Framing & Commercial Rigor

  • Decision-First Modeling: Design every analysis backwards from the specific commercial decision it is meant to change.

  • Uncertainty & Stated Confidence: Size uncertainty statistically, state clearly what sparse or self-reported data cannot support, and attach a stated confidence level to every output.

  • Benchmark Library Management: Define and version the benchmark repository (category, stage, market) to evaluate brands accurately even when data is sparse.

4. Enablement & Commercial Communication

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Present complex numbers, models, and uncertainties to founders and operators with clarity and authority.

  • Quantitative Literacy: Raise the analytical bar across the business by teaching teams how to read and interpret model outputs correctly.

  • Documentation & Standards: Write airtight documentation and standards for data/finance deliverables so cross-functional delivery teams can execute autonomously.

What This Seat Is Not

  • Not a BI/Reporting Seat: Dashboards are merely one downstream output of this work; your primary focus is proprietary modeling and product architecture.

  • Not Research Without Action: We judge models by the decisions they actually changed, not academic complexity.

  • Not a Data Engineering Seat: You will specify pipelines, schemas, and logic for engineering to build—you won't be maintaining core infrastructure tables yourself.

Ideal Background & Qualifications

Must-Haves

  • Experience: 6–8 years in growth, marketing, commercial, or product analytics within DTC, e-commerce, marketplaces, or specialized platforms.

  • Proven Track Record: End-to-end ownership of a forecasting, unit-economics, or media-mix model that commercial teams relied on for high-stakes budget or strategic decisions. You can name the decisions your model changed and what followed.

  • DTC Unit Economics Mastery: Deep fluency in CAC, AOV, COGS, contribution margin, LTV, payback period, breakeven, retention cohorts, and working capital reconciliation.

  • Modelling with Incomplete Data: Demonstrated ability to build robust outputs from banded, self-reported, or partial founder inputs while explicitly quantifying confidence levels.

  • Statistical Rigor: Strong foundation in sizing uncertainty, managing sample limitations, and maintaining analytical integrity.

  • Technical Depth: Hands-on daily fluency in SQL and Python.

  • Product & Engineering Collaboration: Experience working directly with engineering teams to turn quantitative models or metric definitions into production software.

  • Communication: Exceptional presence and ability to defend underlying assumptions and model uncertainty under direct challenge.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Media mix modeling (MMM), incrementality testing, or causal measurement methodologies.

  • Applied machine learning experience (forecasting, propensity, or segmentation models in production).

  • Experience evaluating generative AI or multi-agent system outputs.

  • Familiarity with modern data stack layers (Snowflake, BigQuery, dbt) and attribution platforms (Triple Whale, Northbeam, Rockerbox).

  • Exposure to multi-brand ecosystems via agency, consulting, or platform environments.

  • Experience in early-stage product environments where models and products were co-developed from scratch.

The best time to join Valerie was yesterday. The next best time is now 🤓

👋Our Hiring Process

We want interviews to be valuable for both sides. Throughout the process, you'll meet the people you'll work with, learn more about the role, and get a chance to understand how we think and operate.

Our process typically includes:

  • Introductory conversation with our Talent team <> 30 mins

  • Hiring Manager interview <> 30-45 mins

  • Role-specific assessment or practical exercise (where applicable)

  • Cross-functional or stakeholder interviews <> 30-45 mins

  • Final conversation with leadership <> 30-45 mins

We'll always let you know what to expect before each stage.

💪🏾What You Can Expect

  • Meaningful work with visible impact

  • High ownership from day one

  • Collaboration with experienced founders, operators, and specialists

  • A team that values curiosity, initiative, and continuous improvement

  • Competitive compensation and the tools you need to do your best work

  • Opportunities to grow as Valerie grows

Valerie is committed to building an inclusive workplace where people from different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can thrive. We hire based on skills, potential, and the ability to contribute to our team.

We’re at an inflection point in our journey. After 2 years of profitable growth with a stable core business (car insurance marketplace), we’re ready to expand our product offerings and accelerate customer growth.

We’re looking for 2-3 Product Managers to drive progress across one of our key new product bets, including motorcycle insurance (just launched), home insurance (also just launched), new insurance products for other assets like boat and RV (concept phase), as well as non-insurance products to make car and home ownership easier such as helping customers save money on their property taxes (about to launch).

Each of these new product areas comes with its own operational complexity, its own customer personas and painpoints, and its own path to scale. And we’re looking for builders who are excited to take ownership of one of these new bets.

  • 0-to-1 scope: The products you will work on are new territory for us. There are no established frameworks, no prior PM who has figured it out.

What you'll own

There are several new product bets in the motion. The specific product you will work on will largely depend on your prior experience, interests/preferences, and our business priorities when you join the team.

The goal in every case remains the same: ramp quickly on a new domain, distill data and insights to identify the highest leverage areas to prioritize (including quantitative data from our Data Science team and qualitative data from our Customer Insights & Research team), build and ship new products, get customer feedback quickly, apply learnings and iterate, and compound on what works.

About the role

We're hiring a Strategic Account Executive to win and grow strategic enterprise accounts. You will own the commercial outcome, from pipeline creation to close, by practicing insight-led selling: reframing the customer's initial problem, quantifying the cost of inaction, and mobilizing buying committees around a compelling "why now."

You'll lead multi-stakeholder enterprise cycles with CFO/CIO/Shared Services/Procurement leadership, partnering closely with Solutions Engineering, Marketing, and Customer Success to run disciplined deal plans, deliver value-based proposals, and land enterprise rollouts.

Pipeline creation and territory strategy

  • Build and execute a territory/account plan: target accounts, stakeholders, sequencing, and multi-threading strategy.

  • Create net-new pipeline through outbound prospecting, partner motion, events, and customer referrals.

  • Maintain disciplined pipeline hygiene and forecasting, and report proactively on progress, risks, and what you need from the organization.

Insight-led selling and deal shaping

  • Practice insight selling: challenge the customer's initial framing and introduce a sharper point of view on where value is trapped (exceptions, approvals, master data, controls).

  • Run executive discovery to uncover operational bottlenecks and decision friction, and translate it into a crisp target-state narrative, urgency, and mutual action plan.

  • Build internal alignment across CFO/CIO-led buying committees, including champions, economic buyers, IT/security, and process owners.

Commercial ownership: value case, negotiation, and close

  • Own the business case, pricing strategy, proposals, negotiation, and contracting.

  • Quantify and communicate value (capacity release, cycle time reduction, control/compliance improvements, stack simplification) and tie it to executive priorities and budget.

  • Drive the deal to closure with clear next steps, strong deal governance, and accurate forecasting.

Orchestration across presales and delivery

  • Partner with Solutions Engineers to run workshops/demos and de-risk technical concerns (security, integration, rollout).

  • Align with Customer Success on implementation readiness, success criteria, and expansion paths.

  • Ensure clean handoffs from close to kickoff, maintaining continuity of value narrative and outcomes.

Competitive positioning

  • Position blp against point tools and fragmented stacks (OCR/IDP/workflow/process mining/RPA) with an "end-to-end + exceptions-first" narrative.

  • Anticipate and neutralize competitive plays with crisp differentiation and proof.

What we're looking for

Must-haves

  • 5–10+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS selling experience (or equivalent complex solution sales), with a consistent track record of hitting/exceeding targets.

  • Proven ability to run insight-led enterprise sales cycles: you can respectfully push back, quantify impact, and mobilize buying committees.

  • Strong executive presence with CFO/CIO/Head of Shared Services and comfort navigating enterprise procurement.

  • Ability to manage complex, multi-threaded deals: mutual action plans, MEDDICC-style qualification, forecasting discipline.

  • Strong collaboration with presales/SE and post-sales teams; you sell what can be delivered.

Strong plus

  • ERP/SAP exposure (S/4, ECC, Public/Private Cloud) or selling into finance/procurement/shared services transformations.

  • Experience selling automation platforms (workflow/RPA/process mining/IDP) and winning against incumbents.

  • Experience with global enterprise rollouts and multi-country stakeholders.

Language

  • Fluent in English and German (or another major European language depending on territory).

What you'll get

  • A product that wins. Strong differentiation and real enterprise proof points.

  • Uncapped earnings. High, realistic OTEs with uncapped commission.

  • Real ownership. Employee-owned company; choose annually to take variable compensation in cash or shares.

  • Growth and autonomy. Build your path in a rapidly scaling, international company.

  • Continuous learning. Structured onboarding plus ongoing coaching.

  • Exceptional team. Ambitious, collaborative colleagues who push each other to excellence.
