Position: Head of Upper School (HOUS)

Reports to: Head of Academics and Student Affairs, and Head of School

Salary: $115,000

Direct Reports:

  • Heads of Department (in coordination with the Director of Curriculum & Instruction)

Position Overview

The Head of Upper School (HOUS) is responsible for overseeing the Upper School program (Grades 9–12) at Dwight Global, with the ultimate goal of achieving Dwight Global’s mission of igniting the spark of genius in every child. The HOUS works and collaborates with a team, including the Upper School Deans, Curriculum & Instruction, Heads of Department, the Dean of Student Life, the IB DP Coordinator, and Upper School faculty members, as well as with administrators and faculty members within The Dwight Schools worldwide network.

This position is remote; the Head of Upper School should anticipate travel to New York City a few times each year.

Responsibilities of the Position

Academic Department Support and Supervision

  • Work with the Head of Academics and Student Affairs and the Director of Curriculum & Instruction, overseeing the recruiting, hiring, evaluation, and supervision of faculty (Grades 9–12).
  • Collaborate with the Curriculum & Instruction team to oversee the creation, implementation, and ongoing development of the Upper School curriculum, ensuring rigor, innovation, and alignment with school-wide standards.
  • Oversee and develop Division and Grade Level meetings that incorporate vertical, horizontal, pastoral, and departmental planning.
  • Address and coordinate scheduling and staffing for unique student situations (new class sections, personalized classes, independent studies, etc.).

Pastoral Care, Student Discipline, and Deans

  • Work with the Associate Head of Academics and Student Affairs to oversee the Upper Deans
  • With the Deans, build a healthy school culture through assemblies, advisories, and other programs that promote belonging, integrity, and leadership.
  • Oversee creation and continued improvement of the Upper School Orientation course and parent education programs
  • Cultivate an Upper School school culture that values academic honesty, intellectual curiosity, and ethical decision-making. Develop and implement clear expectations and practices around academic integrity, ensuring that students understand the importance of original work, responsible scholarship, and accountability.
  • Coordinate Honor Council to maintain fairness, transparency, and integrity across all academic and behavioral processes.
  • Manage and implement online proctoring review and disciplinary process for academic honesty infractions
  • Manage summer grade recovery process for Upper School students

College Counseling and Post-Secondary Planning

  • Collaborate with the Associate Head of Academics and Student Affairs and Director of College Counseling to ensure that each student in Grades 9–12 receives personalized and developmentally appropriate guidance.
  • Oversee integration of academic advising and college counseling through joint meetings, workshops, and parent sessions.
  • Support the implementation of standardized testing, college readiness programming, and family information sessions.

Accommodations/Quest

  • Work with the Head of Quest and Learning Support to oversee accommodations and ensure support for students with learning needs in Grades 9–12.
  • Ensure that Quest plans are implemented consistently across academic departments and that faculty are equipped to support students with approved accommodations.

School Authorization and Accreditation

  • Work in conjunction with the Head of Academics and Student Affairs on all school accreditation and authorization processes (Cognia, IB, etc.).
  • Provide evidence, documentation, and data as required for accreditation and program evaluations related to Grades 9–12.

Other Responsibilities

  • Work with the Scheduler to develop the Upper School Schedule.
  • Update the Head of School, Head of Academics and Student Affairs regularly on all significant issues in each area of the school under their supervision.
  • Participate in admissions programs as needed (e.g., open houses, student interviews, committee reviews).
  • Participate in cross-campus projects and worldwide Dwight-Franklin collaborations.

Data Analysis

  • With the Curriculum & Instruction team, review all Upper School assessment data (internal and external), including AP, IB, PSAT, and other performance indicators.
  • Ensure that data informs curriculum development, personalized learning strategies, and student success planning.
  • Work with Heads of Department to use data for reflection, goal-setting, and instructional improvement.

jobs.title: Elite AI Agent Engineer- B2B Lead Generation & Automation
jobs.excerpt: PlanITROI is hiring a proven, hands-on AI Agent builder who specializes in B2B lead generation.
jobs.description:
PlanITROI is hiring a proven, hands-on AI Agent builder who specializes in B2B lead generation.

You must have personally architected, built, deployed, and operated AI agents that generate measurable B2B prospecting results.

We’re seeking an AI engineer who can build the intelligence behind the system

AI agents that use tools, make decisions, coordinate workflows, and turn enterprise buying signals into qualified sales meetings.

If you are an expert at building AI agents for B2B lead generation and can prove they work, we want to meet you.

About PlanITROI

25 years of success. Global industry recognition. Founder-led. No corporate red tape. An ambitious future powered by AI and Robotics!

For more than 25 years, PlanITROI has helped enterprise organizations maximize the financial value of retired technology through IT lifecycle management, repair, refurbishment, redeployment, remarketing, reverse logistics, and secure IT Asset Disposition (ITAD). PlanITROI is recognized in Gartner’s ITAD Market Guide, is an IAITAM Platinum Sponsor, and has built our business around reuse-as-intended-use, prioritizing reuse over recycling.

Our mission: Maximize the financial value of technology while extending its useful life. Every device we recover creates value for clients, reduces unnecessary electronic waste, and gives technology a second life as affordable technology.

Why you’ll love working here

Founder-led. Move fast. Get things done. Work directly with entrepreneurial leadership. No layers of corporate bureaucracy or endless approval cycles. Great ideas get heard, tested, and implemented.

Built like an AI startup, backed by an established company. Bring your engineering ideas to a business with 25 years of enterprise relationships, operating experience, and real market opportunities.

Engineer something big. Build AI agents capable of researching 5,000+ enterprise accounts, identifying buying signals, reaching 250,000+ potential right contacts, and generating qualified meetings at scale.

See measurable results. Your agents will directly influence enterprise revenue and help more technology get repaired, reused, and returned to productive use.

Work with people who value builders. We believe in optimism, discipline, humility, ownership, continuous improvement, and recognizing teammates who help others succeed.

Your mission: Build an intelligent AI-powered lead generation engine

Design, build, deploy, and continuously improve an interconnected system of specialized AI agents that identifies enterprise buying opportunities and converts them into qualified meetings. You will own the technical outbound engine end to end, from buying-signal detection and account intelligence to contact discovery, multichannel orchestration, CRM integration, experimentation, and measurement. Our target market (ICP) includes enterprise organizations with 5,000 to 1,000,000+ employees, 80%+ mostly knowledge workers with complex buying committees, and existing technology providers. Your challenge is to find the right buyer, recognize the right moment, and create a compelling reason to engage in PlanITROI.

This role reports to the Founder & CEO and the Chief Strategy Officer. You’ll work directly with them and the VP of Marketing, with no layers in between.

Your goal: Qualified enterprise meetings generated and MSA’s signed!

What you will build and own

  • AI Intent Signal Detection Agents. Identify, ingest, evaluate, and score buying signals, including technology refresh cycles, leadership changes, office moves, M&A, RFP activity, contract timing, job postings, technology initiatives, and social activity. Trigger the right next action.
  • AI Buying Committee Intelligence Agents. Identify high-value ICP accounts, research enterprise organizations, map buying committees, select the best 1 to 5 contacts for each entry point, validate contact information, and continuously track changes.
  • AI Personalization & Challenger Messaging Agents. Combine account intelligence, buying signals, persona-specific pain points, account history, and incumbent-provider context to create relevant, personalized outreach at scale.
  • AI Multichannel Orchestration Agents. Coordinate email, LinkedIn, voicemail drops, AI calling where appropriate, and human SDR/BDR follow-up. Manage sequencing, timing, channel rules, routing, and next-best actions.
  • AI Objection Handling & Follow-Up Agents. Recognize and respond intelligently to objections such as “We already have a provider.” Maintain conversational context, determine appropriate follow-up, and escalate to humans when needed.
  • AI Performance & Optimization Agents. Measure results across signals, personas, channels, and campaigns. Identify winning and losing hypotheses, recommend experiments, and improve qualified meeting conversion.

These are functional capabilities, not a requirement to deploy six separate agents. You will design the architecture, build the agents, integrate the systems, and make them work together.

Non-negotiable technical requirements: This role requires a hands-on builder. You must design, build, and demo production AI agents yourself. If you qualify, we’ll give you a real project to prove it. You’ll integrate tools like Salesforce, Apollo, and Clay. Using them isn’t the role; building the agents that run on top of them is.

We are seeking proven hands-on expertise in:

  • AI agent engineering: LLMs, tool calling, reasoning workflows, agent memory, state management, multi-agent orchestration, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Agent frameworks: LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, or comparable frameworks.
  • Software development: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, APIs, webhooks, custom integrations, and automation architecture.
  • GTM integrations: Salesforce, Apollo, ZoomInfo, Clay, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, 6sense, Bombora-type intent sources, and AI calling/voicemail platforms.
  • Enterprise prospecting: Intent signals, ICP scoring, buying-committee identification, contact resolution, enrichment, personalization, objection handling, and multichannel sequence design.
  • Production operations: Agent monitoring, debugging, data quality, CRM synchronization, deduplication, deliverability, compliance, error handling, and auditability.
  • Scale: Engineering reliable systems capable of very high outbound volumes, reaching 250,000+ contacts across email, LinkedIn, and voicemail, while protecting platform limits, accuracy, compliance, and deliverability.

You must understand both the technical engineering and the B2B prospecting strategy required to turn agents into a functioning revenue system.

What success looks like

  • Qualified meetings generated: Your primary business outcome. Meetings must satisfy defined ICP, persona, and business-need criteria.
  • Signal-to-meeting conversion: How effectively your agents convert meaningful buying signals into conversations and qualified meetings.
  • Contact Precision: Reaching the right decision-makers and buying committees.
  • Agent deployment velocity: How quickly you turn a campaign idea into a reliable, working agent and live test.
  • Multichannel conversion: Positive responses, conversations, qualified meetings, and opportunities by signal, persona, channel, and campaign.
  • System reliability: Data accuracy, deliverability, CRM integrity, routing, compliance, and scalability.
  • Learning rate: How quickly do you identify what isn’t working, fix root causes, and scale what produces results.

Our hiring process: Show me, don’t tell me

We hire proof, not interviews alone. We’re not interested in theoretical AI expertise or polished presentations about what agents might do.

The process has three stages:

  • Live demo. Show us AI agents you personally built and deployed for B2B lead generation, and the results they produced.
  • Build a project. Build an outbound agent from a campaign premise we give you, using your own tools.
  • Live technical session. Demo your build, work a live account, and walk us through your architecture.

Across these stages, be ready to show:

  • Your agent architecture, decision logic, prompts, tools, data integrations, and orchestration.
  • How your agents identify opportunities and execute prospecting workflows.
  • How do your agents handle exceptions, incomplete data, failures, and human intervention?
  • Real performance data: qualified meetings, pipelines, conversions, or measurable improvements your systems produced.

Ready for the challenge?

If you love solving difficult technical problems and want to build something ambitious, PlanITROI is where you can make an impact. Bring your engineering expertise, working agents, ideas, and your drive to succeed. We’ll bring 25 years of industry experience, enterprise relationships, a substantial market opportunity, and the ability to move fast.

Build the agents. Own the results. Help us grow.

PlanITROI offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and more. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and value diversity at all levels of the organization.

Learn more: PlanITROI.com | NextraTech.com | DigitalDreamsProject.com

Darkroom is hiring an AR & Billing Specialist to join the Finance team. You’ll own billing, collections, accounts payable, creator payments, and cash visibility across more than 80 client accounts and around 100 invoices a month. You’ll report to the SVP of Finance and work closely with the Finance Operations Manager, who sets our collections strategy, as well as our account leads and external bookkeeper.

This is not a reminder-sending role. We want someone who knows every account, spots payment risk early, and decides how to approach each client so we get paid on time without damaging the relationship.

This role is built for someone who sees AI as a core part of how finance gets done. You’ll use tools like Claude to check calculations, automate repetitive billing and follow-up work, and build workflows that raise both the speed and accuracy of our output.

This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone (9 AM–5 PM EST).

What You’ll Do

  • Own collections execution end to end: run the follow-up calendar, manage AR aging and days sales outstanding, and follow the collections strategy set for each account.

  • Join the daily cash flow check-in led by the Finance Operations Manager.

  • Flag at-risk accounts early, such as slipping payment patterns, disputes, or unresponsive contacts, with a recommended action.

  • Prepare the weekly cash and AR report, and draft the cash and collections section of the monthly report.

  • Keep the weekly cash forecast current, with expected receipts by client and by week.

  • Run accounts payable in Ramp: enter vendor bills, check them against approvals and contracts, schedule payments, and keep vendor records current.

  • Pay creators, partners, and referral payouts in Ramp once amounts are approved, and keep payee records current.

  • Record invoices and payments in QuickBooks, working alongside our external bookkeeper.

  • Peer-check teammates’ work, such as reported MRR and client data against billing records.

  • Maintain and improve our collections playbook and billing processes.

You Should Apply If This Sounds Like You

  • You have 2–4 years of experience in accounts receivable, accounts payable, billing, or collections, ideally at an agency, professional services, or SaaS company with US clients.

  • You have a high bar for accuracy. Invoices you send are right the first time.

  • You’re a confident communicator, polite but firm with US client contacts, by email and on calls.

  • You have good judgment about people and priorities. You know when to push, when to escalate, and when to wait.

  • You take initiative. You raise problems together with a proposed fix instead of waiting to be told.

  • You use Claude or similar AI tools in your work, or you’re eager to.

  • You’re fluent in written and spoken English.

We’re looking for an experienced Lead Software Architect to take technical ownership of the architecture and continued productisation of SteelBuy, our secure B2B marketplace connecting buyers and sellers of metal.
SteelBuy is part of tk accelis Trading, formerly thyssenkrupp Materials Trading, combining the agility of a developing digital platform with the industry expertise and international reach of an established global materials trading organisation.
Our immediate commercial and operational focus is the US market, but our ambitions go further. We want to develop SteelBuy into a scalable and adaptable technical product that can support different markets, business models and integrations in the future, potentially including Europe.

This is an opportunity to have a significant influence on that journey.

Key Responsibilities


As Lead Software Architect, you’ll provide the technical vision and architectural direction for the platform while remaining close enough to the technology to make pragmatic, informed decisions.
You’ll lead and mentor our back-end engineering team based in India, collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders across the UK, Europe and US, and help establish the technical standards and ways of working that enable us to build a secure, scalable and high-quality product.
The role will cover back-end architecture, microservices, DevOps, enterprise integrations, APIs and distributed systems, alongside providing technical leadership to our internal development teams and external partners.

Although you'll occasionally work across international time zones, the role operates primarily around UK working hours. Routine alignment to US hours isn't expected.

What you’ll be doing

  • Own and evolve the overall software and systems architecture for SteelBuy, ensuring the platform is scalable, secure, maintainable and adaptable.
  • Help transform the platform from a primarily US-focused implementation into a reusable technical product capable of supporting future markets and business models.
  • Translate business and system requirements into clear high-level technical designs, architecture and documentation.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Impact and Intelligence
jobs.excerpt: Position overview SNV is building a catalytic commercial accelerator, built to close the gap between capital and impact in markets where both are urgently needed.
jobs.description:
Position overview
SNV is building a catalytic commercial accelerator, built to close the gap between capital and impact in markets where both are urgently needed. The Senior Manager for Impact and Intelligence is the intellectual engine within the unit. This role has two distinct but connected responsibilities: delivering client-facing impact measurement as a billable service, and synthesising knowledge across the portfolio to build a body of evidence that sharpens our offer and strengthens our market position.

This is not a back-office role. Impact measurement is a revenue line in its own right — impact investors, DFIs, and corporations with sustainability commitments are increasingly willing to pay for rigorous, credible measurement of their programmes. The right person combines analytical rigour with commercial awareness, and understands that evidence is only valuable if it changes decisions.

SNV holds a significant body of institutional knowledge — proposals, evaluations, programme data, sector evidence — accumulated across 50+ years and 25+ countries. Most of it is inaccessible or underused. This role is responsible for changing that: activating SNV’s knowledge base as a commercial asset, not just an archive.

Who you are
You are a curious and analytical professional who enjoys uncovering insights that help organisations make better decisions. You look beyond the data to understand what is happening, why it matters, and how evidence can be translated into practical action and measurable results.

You combine analytical rigour with commercial awareness. You understand that research, impact measurement, and intelligence create value when they influence strategy, strengthen client relationships, support business growth, or improve development outcomes. You are comfortable working with both quantitative and qualitative data and know when deep analysis is required and when a pragmatic, timely recommendation is the better solution.

You are collaborative, proactive, and enjoy working across disciplines, bringing together perspectives from colleagues, clients, and partners. When you identify important trends, insights, or opportunities, you share them and help others act on them.

Most importantly, you are excited by the opportunity to turn evidence into impact. You identify insights that can be leveraged across the organisation, helping shape new approaches, strengthen market positioning, and inform business development decisions. You are equally motivated by building knowledge systems and intelligence mechanisms that support better future decision-making, reducing uncertainty through the effective use of data, intelligence, and learning.

Key Responsibilities

Client-facing impact measurement

  • Design and deliver impact measurement frameworks for clients — impact investors, blended finance facilities, agribusinesses, and government counterparts.
  • Develop results chains, theories of change, and indicator sets for IDF and ICVC engagements where measurement is part of the scope.
  • Conduct primary and secondary data collection, analysis, and reporting to investor-grade standards.
  • Package measurement outputs as standalone deliverables — not appendices to strategy documents.
  • Identify and convert standalone measurement mandates: fund impact reporting, programme evaluations, baseline and endline studies.
  • Stay current with impact measurement standards — IRIS+, IMP, GIIRS, and equivalents — and advise clients on which frameworks fit their reporting requirements.

Cross-portfolio intelligence

  • Synthesise findings and evidence across all Accelerator engagements into consolidated intelligence: what is working, for whom, at what cost, and under what conditions.
  • Build and maintain a knowledge base that captures reusable assets — frameworks, datasets, case studies, and sector-specific evidence — from every completed engagement. Every engagement should produce a reusable asset. You own the system that makes that happen and the quality standard it is held to.
  • Identify patterns in the portfolio that strengthen the offer: which client types convert fastest, which interventions generate the strongest returns, which geographies show the most traction.
  • Produce quarterly intelligence briefs covering portfolio-level insights and implications for strategy.
  • Own the donor and tender intelligence function: maintain a systematic view of active and upcoming funding opportunities relevant to the Accelerator’s two streams. This is an early operational priority — a structured weekly digest feeding the pipeline, not an ad hoc scan.

Sales enablement and competitive intelligence

  • Build and maintain the Accelerator's sales collateral: sector evidence packs, impact data sheets, and proof-of-concept case studies for both IDF and ICVC streams.
  • Conduct competitive landscape analysis — who else operates in our space, how they position, what they charge, where we are differentiated.
  • Track market trends in impact finance and value chain development that are relevant to pipeline development. Feed findings to the team.
  • Support proposal development with data, evidence, and impact methodology sections where required.

What you bring

To be considered for this role, you bring:

  • At least 8 years of experience in impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation, or related analytical roles — with a significant portion in a commercial or advisory context.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering impact measurement as a client-facing service, not just as internal reporting.
  • Familiarity with the impact investing and development finance landscape — understanding what DFIs and impact funds require from their portfolio companies and TA providers.
  • Experience synthesising evidence across multiple programmes or geographies into actionable insights.
  • Track record of producing high-quality analytical outputs under time pressure — reports, evidence reviews, data packs — to external standards.
  • Experience building or managing knowledge systems in a professional services or advisory context. A list of documents is not a knowledge base. You know the difference.

Additionally, we value:

  • Fluency in impact measurement frameworks: IRIS+, IMP, DCED, GIIRS, and at least one results-chain methodology.
  • Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills. Comfortable with both survey data and financial models.
  • Ability to translate complex evidence into clear, commercial-facing narratives.
  • Experience with knowledge management — building systems that people actually use, not just filing evidence.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted knowledge tools — document analysis, synthesis, search across large bodies of material. We are building AI-powered knowledge infrastructure and this role is its primary user.
  • English required. French or Portuguese an advantage.
  • Reporting line: Director
  • Location: Flexible.We welcome applications from candidates based anywhere within the time zones spanning Ghana to Singapore. As this role involves international collaboration and travel, candidates should be located within reasonable reach of a well-connected international airport.
  • Travel requirements: International travel will be required.
  • Expected start date: November/December 2026

What we offer
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package. Compensation is determined based on relevant experience, skills, and internal equity, ensuring a fair and consistent approach across the organisation.

Location & Travel
Flexible location. We are particularly interested in candidates based within the time zones between Singapore and Ghana, where most of our work is concentrated. International travel will be required, so candidates should have access to a major international airport.

Contract duration: We are looking for someone to play a long-term role in building and growing the Accelerator. Contract arrangements will vary by location and local employment requirements, and details will be discussed with shortlisted candidates.

Working at SNV
At SNV we challenge and inspire and offer continuous growth. We offer meaningful opportunities to shape the future, expand your skills, and collaborate with a vibrant, global network of experts. At SNV your contribution matter, and your development is our priority.

We are home to 57 cultures working in 22 countries, with about 95% of our team members holding the nationality of the respective countries we work in. We promote international career development. Our workforce consists of a mix of both people with longstanding tenure, willing to share their institutional knowledge, as well as people with local expertise and knowledge. All with an inquisitive view and united in ‘ONE SNV’ working towards our purpose.

Together, we are committed to the effective and efficient stewardship of resources and maximising positive, lasting impacts. Our ability to deliver results rests on our robust foundation of experience, technical knowledge, evidence and learning; our commitment to strengthening capacities and catalysing partnerships; and the relationships and trust of those we work alongside.

SNV is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment and make recruitment decisions based on merit, competence, and organisational needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, nationality, marital status, or any other status protected by applicable law. Women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from under-represented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

How to apply
If you meet the key requirements and feel inspired by this opportunity, we warmly welcome your application. Please submit your CV and motivation letter by 1st November 2026 via SmartRecruiters.

To ensure a focused and respectful recruitment process, we kindly ask that you apply only if you meet the essential qualifications and are available to work in the specified location.
Please note that only candidates progressing to the next stage of the selection process will be contacted. Individual feedback cannot be provided.

If this role isn’t the right fit but you’re interested in joining SNV in the future, we invite you to follow us on LinkedIn and our career page Vacancies | SNV to stay updated on new opportunities that match your profile.

Reference and vetting check
At SNV, our belief in the CARE principles — Commitment to impact, Adaptive to Context, Respecting Difference and Expertise in Practice — shapes how we work with each other and every interaction we have with our colleagues, partners, and the communities we serve. These values guide how we welcome new team members, ensuring our workplace remains a place of trust, safety, and dignity for all.

As part of our commitment to a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, we carry out reference and background checks for all determined positions, with particular attention to safeguarding. You will be invited to provide the contact details of [two] referees, and we will only approach them once you have given your permission. We handle this process with care, empathy, and strict confidentiality, using the information solely for purposes related to your application and the role you have applied for.

SNV is committed to safeguarding and to protecting children and adults from all forms of harm, with zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, or any other form of misconduct. As part of creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive working environment, all staff, consultants, and partners are expected to uphold SNV’s safeguarding, child protection, ethical standards, and CARE principles. In line with these commitments — and as a participant in the Inter‑Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS) — SNV will request a Statement of Conduct from your previous employer(s), covering any substantiated findings of misconduct, to ensure a recruitment process that safeguards and protect the communities we serve.

About SNV Proximate
What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale? SNV’s newly established impact capital accelerator aims to do exactly that: develop commercially viable solutions that generate both business value and development impact. Combining expertise in impact-driven finance and inclusive commercial value chains, SNV Proximate will operate with the pace, ambition, and commercial mindset of a boutique advisory firm while leveraging the reach, credibility, and market presence of a global development organisation.

Working with companies, investors, development finance institutions, foundations, and governments, this is your chance to join the team that will design, test, and grow new approaches to mobilising investment, strengthening markets, and building more inclusive and resilient value chains across emerging economies. It is a place for people who are excited by building something new, comfortable operating across both commercial and development environments, and motivated by turning ambitious ideas into scalable results.

The Director, Product Management - Data Systems leads product strategy for our enterprise data foundation, including the Snowflake-based platform and supporting data systems that power OmniAnalyst, OmniInsights, and our broader data product ecosystem. Reporting to the Vice President of Data Product Management, this role defines the capabilities, governance, and roadmap needed to deliver scalable, secure, and trusted data products across the enterprise.

As the product leader for the data platform, this individual serves as the primary intake and prioritization point for platform requests, aligns stakeholders across business and technology teams, and ensures the platform delivers business value while maintaining long-term scalability, performance, and cost efficiency.

Essential Responsibilities

Define Platform Capabilities

  • Defines the capabilities required of the enterprise data foundation, including governed data sharing, access controls, entity resolution, semantic models, shared definitions, and data quality standards.
  • Partners with Data Architecture and Data Engineering to design scalable, secure, and well-governed platform capabilities aligned with enterprise standards.
  • Champions modern data architecture practices, including data mesh and layered (medallion) architectures, to drive consistency and reusability across the enterprise.
  • Establishes standards for semantic context, metadata, governance, and data design to ensure data is consistently understood by business users, analytics tools, and AI applications.

Set Vision & Roadmap for Data Systems

  • Defines and owns the vision and multi-year roadmap for the enterprise data foundation, beginning with the Snowflake platform and evolving as business needs grow.
  • Partners with Data Architecture leadership, business stakeholders, and internal data consumers to align platform investments with enterprise priorities.
  • Collaborates with product leaders supporting OmniAnalyst, OmniInsights, and other data products to ensure platform capabilities meet downstream product needs.
  • Establishes and monitors platform success measures, including data quality, availability, performance, adoption, operational efficiency, and cost optimization.
  • Applies Product Operating Model principles to platform intake, prioritization, backlog management, and outcome measurement.

Intake, Prioritization & Platform Governance

  • Owns the intake and prioritization process for enterprise data platform initiatives, maintaining a transparent framework for evaluating business requests.
  • Balances business value, urgency, risk, dependencies, effort, and cost when prioritizing platform investments and managing tradeoffs.
  • Maintains a strategic backlog and facilitates stakeholder alignment through recurring prioritization forums and governance discussions.

Drive Platform Delivery

  • Leverages SQL and strong technical fluency to validate delivered solutions and ensure business requirements are met.
  • Partners with Governance and FinOps teams to manage platform consumption, forecast costs, and promote cost-effective platform growth.
  • Ensures the platform supports analytics, data science, and AI workloads through strong data quality, lineage, governance, semantic context, and performance management.
  • Establishes performance metrics, reporting, and documentation standards that support platform adoption, reliability, and continuous improvement.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Builds alignment across business, operations, technology, governance, security, privacy, and compliance stakeholders.
  • Ensures appropriate platform controls are implemented and maintained, including role-based access, masking policies, data classification, retention, lineage, and auditability.
  • Communicates platform strategy, releases, priorities, and performance through executive reporting, documentation, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Acts as a trusted advisor on data platform capabilities, governance requirements, and strategic opportunities.
  • Maintains awareness of emerging Snowflake capabilities and modern data architecture trends to inform platform strategy.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, or a related technical field required.
  • Advanced degree a plus.
  • Snowflake certification (e.g., SnowPro Core or SnowPro Advanced Architect) preferred.

Experience

  • Ten (10) or more years of experience in product management, data platform, data engineering, or data architecture roles, including at least five (5) years in technical product management for data platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with Snowflake, either as a technical practitioner or product owner of a Snowflake-based platform.
  • Strong experience with modern data architecture concepts including data warehousing, data mesh, dimensional modeling, layered (medallion) architecture, semantic modeling, and ELT pipelines.
  • Demonstrated success shaping data platform capabilities, influencing engineering direction, and partnering across business and technology teams.
  • Experience leading intake and prioritization processes for shared enterprise platforms serving multiple business units.

  • Experience with semantic layers, knowledge graphs, metadata management, entity resolution, master data management, or governed data-sharing solutions preferred.

Skills & Knowledge

jobs.description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We're looking for a Business Manager to own the outcomes of one of our credit programs, reporting to the Director, Portfolio Management. The Portfolio Management Team is responsible for owning the underwriting process throughout the lifetime of existing accounts, understanding customer lifetime value (LTV), and creating pathways to customer success and graduation, all while staying true to our mission. This includes our Credit Line Increase Program (CLIP).

The impact you'll make:

For a lot of our customers, getting their Mission Lane credit card is the first step toward building their credit. But what comes next is where the real progress happens: earning a higher credit line or a better rate, or qualifying for a second card.

As Business Manager, you own the program that decides these outcomes for existing customers. Your job is figuring out where that program needs to be a year from now, whether that means questioning if the current criteria still hold up, or finding room to approve more people while catching risk earlier. Nail that, and the program keeps getting better at finding the people ready for that next step.

Mission Lane is still young, but we've already built a solid foundation and are experiencing steady growth. There's never been a better time to help shape how we get this right.

As Business Manager, CLIP, you will:

  • Use AI-driven tools to speed up and sharpen your analysis
  • Adjust our approach as customer behavior and the market change
  • Turn financial data into clear recommendations that grow the business while managing risk responsibly
  • Run small tests in market, then use what you learn to decide where we invest next
  • Guide and mentor analysts working alongside you on the program
  • Develop actionable strategies based on data-driven insights and model the expected financial impacts to improve our underwriting & pricing strategies while ensuring customer success
  • Design and enhance the customer lifetime value (LTV) model to drive business growth
  • Present and communicate clear recommendations to senior leadership
  • Enable long-term growth by pushing forward our testing agenda to build insights into consumer behavior and invest in future growth
  • Collaborate with cross functional teams across product, data science, and engineering to bring strategies to market

You'll thrive in this role if:

  • You understand the whole card business system, from acquisition to risk to engagement, and you can trace how a change in one part ripples through the rest.
  • You're curious enough to dig into the reasoning behind a strategy, down to the assumptions it's built on, so you understand it at an elemental level.
  • You're comfortable defining the problem yourself when nobody's handed you one, and thinking in terms of the next year, not just the next task.
  • You take ownership of your work end to end, catching your own mistakes before they compound.
  • You can explain a business problem clearly enough that someone outside your immediate team could follow your thinking.

Minimum qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in a highly analytical role
  • A bachelor's or master's degree in economics, finance, engineering, mathematics, or a similarly quantitative field, with a strong academic record
  • A track record of leading complex, cross-functional analytical projects from start to finish
  • Experience guiding or mentoring other analysts
  • Comfort working in SQL, Python, or similar tools for data analysis
  • Ability to travel ~4+ times per year for high quality in-person collaboration

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience working with credit cards or other consumer lending products
  • Experience helping scale a business in a fast-moving startup environment
  • Strong SQL or Python skills
  • Experience using AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, etc.)

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $140,000-160,000

This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.

Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization: nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do.

In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

We have a great opportunity for an Operations Supervisor! The ideal candidate accomplishes company objectives by supervising the daily operations of a team of Customer Service Specialists and Medical Administrative Assistants.

The Integrated Kidney Care division of DaVita Kidney Care, is at the center of DaVita’s strategy for the future and our commitment to provide integrated care to one of the most medically complex patient populations in the US. Our more than 600 dedicated nurses, care coordinators, nurse practitioners (NPs) and business professionals integrate and manage care for more than 20,000 patients with late-stage chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end stage renal disease (ESRD) across the US each month.


We’ve proven that integrating care achieves the triple aim of improved patient quality of life, better outcomes and lower total cost of care. What sets VillageHealth apart is that we not only provide great care management but we start with our heart with our patients and each other. We focus on creating both a great experience for our patients and a special place to work for our teammates.

We’re on a mission to revolutionize kidney care, with a vision of making integrated care the standard of care for all renal patients. To help us achieve our vision, we’re investing extensively in developing both our model of care and our team.

· Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, paid time off, PTO cash out

· Support for you and your family: Family resources, EAP counseling sessions, access Headspace®, backup child and elder care, maternity/paternity leave and more

· Professional development programs: DaVita offers a variety of programs to help strong performers grow within their career and also offers on-demand virtual leadership and development courses through DaVita’s online training platform Star Learning.


At DaVita, we strive to be a community first and a company second. We want all teammates to experience DaVita as "a place where I belong." Our goal is to embed belonging into everything we do in our Village, so that it becomes part of who we are. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and comply with state and federal affirmative action requirements. Individuals are recruited, hired, assigned and promoted without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

This position will be open for a minimum of three days.

jobs.title: Channel Sales Manager
jobs.excerpt: CIQ OVERVIEWCIQ builds the enterprise infrastructure that powers the world's most demanding workloads.
jobs.description:
CIQ OVERVIEW

CIQ builds the enterprise infrastructure that powers the world's most demanding workloads. From the operating system layer through AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, and cloud-native orchestration, CIQ delivers the speed, security, scalability, and sovereignty that major enterprises, government agencies, and research institutions depend on.

CIQ is the founding support and services partner of Rocky Linux and the developer of the RLC Pro family of Enterprise Linux distributions, Fuzzball workload orchestration, Warewulf Pro cluster provisioning, and Ascender Pro automation. Our customers include some of the largest and most technically sophisticated organizations in the world, working across HPC, AI/ML, defense, and regulated industries.

We are a company of builders, operators, and open source practitioners. If you want to do work that matters, at a company that is genuinely changing how enterprise infrastructure gets built and run, we want to talk.

POSITION SUMMARY

As Senior Channel Manager, you will own CIQ’s channel-led revenue as an individual contributor, reporting directly to the company’s sales leadership. You will build and run CIQ’s partner motion across three fronts: recruiting new channel partners, developing and enabling existing partners, and managing distributor relationships. Every partner activity ties back to sourced and influenced revenue. Additional responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Identify, qualify, and recruit new channel partners (resellers, VARs, SIs, MSPs) whose customer base and technical focus align with Rocky Linux, RLC, and the broader CIQ portfolio; build the recruitment pipeline, run outreach, and close partner agreements directly.
  • Develop existing partners into producing partners through seller and SE enablement, joint business planning, co-marketing and demand-generation coordination, and accountability to mutually agreed targets; diagnose why partners are not selling and fix it.
  • Own distributor relationships and economics, including transactional flow, margin, and incentive structures, and using distributor reach to extend partner recruitment without CIQ carrying all the overhead.
  • Define and run the program mechanics: partner tiers, deal registration, the margin model, enablement, and the metrics that govern them.
  • Work cross-functionally with direct sales (to manage channel conflict and run co-sell), marketing (partner demand generation), and product (to feed partner and market signal back).
  • Carry and forecast a channel-sourced and influenced pipeline contribution.

NEEDED TO SUCCEED

Successful candidates will have:

  • A genuine self-starter mindset, comfortable operating with ambiguity, and a near-blank slate.
  • Strong commercial instincts, with the ability to negotiate partner economics and defend margin.
  • Credibility with both partner executives and partner field reps.
  • The discipline to run their book on numbers, not relationships alone.
  • A hands-on operator’s approach, doing the work directly (outreach, partner conversations, enablement sessions, negotiations) rather than delegating it.
  • A friendly, collaborative, humble, honest, and always striving to be better attitude.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience.
  • 8+ years of experience in channel, partner, or alliances sales, ideally in infrastructure, open source, or enterprise software.
  • A track record of personally building partner relationships that produced real revenue (not solely managing a team that did).
  • Experience standing up or materially growing partner program mechanics: tiering, deal registration, margin models, and enablement.

BENEFITS

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Flexible paid time off.

  • Employee stock options.

  • Remote work; no travel required for most positions.

jobs.description:
★ PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH ★

Head of GTM

Location: Remote – Latin America
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote
Employment Type: Full-Time
Industry: Digital Media / Performance Marketing / iGaming / Marketing Technology Compensation: $6,000 USD/month
Experience: 8+ Years in GTM, Revenue, or Growth Leadership
Schedule: Monday–Friday | U.S. Eastern Time (ET) Business Hours
English Proficiency: Advanced Professional English Required
Travel: Occasional travel to the United States

About the Company
Our client is a U.S.-based company operating at the intersection of digital media, performance marketing, marketing technology, and competitive entertainment.
The company provides marketing and customer acquisition services to businesses in sports betting, iGaming, and prediction markets, combining data analytics, attribution technology, media buying, and creator-driven distribution.
As the business grows, it is focused on strengthening its market positioning, building a scalable revenue engine, and leveraging AI-powered systems to accelerate commercial growth.
About the Role
We are seeking a strategic, hands-on Head of Go-to-Market (GTM) to lead the company's growth strategy, demand generation, and revenue operations.
Working closely with executive leadership, you will connect market positioning, pipeline generation, brand strategy, revenue operations, and AI automation into a unified GTM system.
A key priority is developing a strong top-of-funnel acquisition engine through owned media, newsletters, podcasts, thought leadership, and strategic content.
We are specifically looking for someone with experience leading GTM for service-based businesses, such as digital media agencies, performance marketing agencies, consulting firms, or similar professional services organizations.
This is not a traditional SaaS GTM position. The ideal candidate understands how to position, market, and sell services, generate qualified B2B opportunities, and build scalable commercial systems.

Why This Opportunity?
  • Own the GTM strategy of a growing U.S.-based services business.
  • Work directly with executive leadership on revenue growth and market positioning.
  • Build demand generation and owned media programs from the ground up.
  • Implement AI-powered systems with measurable commercial impact.
  • Shape the processes, technology, and team structure supporting future growth.
What You'll Do
GTM Strategy & Revenue Growth
  • Develop and execute GTM strategies specifically for service-based B2B businesses.
  • Define target segments, positioning, value propositions, and acquisition opportunities.
  • Build a full-funnel growth model connecting marketing activities to qualified pipeline and revenue.
  • Partner with revenue leadership on growth targets, forecasting, and performance metrics.
  • Monitor pipeline generation, conversion rates, customer acquisition costs, and revenue performance.
  • Identify opportunities to improve pricing, packaging, and commercial positioning.
Demand Generation, Brand & Owned Media
  • Build and lead a demand generation strategy focused on qualified B2B pipeline.
  • Develop owned media channels, including newsletters, podcasts, thought leadership, and strategic content.
  • Strengthen brand positioning and establish the company as an industry authority.
  • Turn customer results, market insights, and industry expertise into compelling commercial narratives.
  • Identify strategic partnerships, distribution opportunities, and industry events that support growth.
Revenue Operations & AI Automation
  • Own and optimize the GTM technology stack, including CRM, lead enrichment, sequencing, analytics, and reporting.
  • Establish reliable pipeline tracking, attribution, and revenue forecasting processes.
  • Personally design, build, and deploy AI agents or automated workflows supporting prospecting, research, outreach, content operations, and reporting.
  • Improve operational efficiency, data accuracy, and conversion performance.
  • Continuously evaluate and implement new technologies that support scalable growth.
Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Partner with executive and revenue leadership to align marketing, sales, and business objectives.
  • Establish clear reporting, performance reviews, and strategic planning processes.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives and coordinate internal and external resources.
  • Recommend hiring priorities, team structures, and process improvements as the company scales.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
  • Minimum 8+ years of experience in GTM, Growth, Revenue Operations, Demand Generation, or related leadership positions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading GTM strategies for service-based companies, such as digital media agencies, performance marketing agencies, consulting firms, or professional services businesses.
  • Proven responsibility for revenue targets, pipeline generation, or P&L performance.
  • Strong experience in B2B demand generation, market positioning, and customer acquisition.
  • Hands-on experience building or managing owned media programs, including newsletters, podcasts, or thought leadership.
  • Strong knowledge of CRM systems, revenue analytics, attribution, and forecasting.
  • Proven experience personally building and implementing AI-powered automations or agents in real business environments.
  • Ability to demonstrate previous AI projects, including workflows, business applications, and measurable results.
  • Experience leading teams, building processes, and scaling commercial operations.
  • Advanced professional English communication skills.
  • Availability to work during U.S. Eastern Time business hours and travel occasionally to the United States.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience in iGaming, sports betting, prediction markets, AdTech, or performance marketing.
  • Background in digital media agencies or consulting businesses serving B2B clients.
  • Experience with media attribution, creator-driven marketing, and performance-based acquisition.
  • Experience developing new market categories or industry thought leadership.
  • Experience working directly with founders, CEOs, or senior revenue executives.
How Success Is Measured
  • Growth in qualified pipeline and revenue contribution.
  • Development of a scalable GTM strategy for a services-based business.
  • Stronger market positioning and engagement through owned media and thought leadership.
  • Improved conversion rates, acquisition efficiency, and forecasting accuracy.
  • Successful implementation of AI-powered workflows with measurable business results.
  • Effective alignment between marketing, sales, and revenue operations.
Why Join Us?
  • $6,000 USD/month compensation.
  • Fully remote opportunity from Latin America.
  • 12 days of paid time off (PTO) annually.
  • U.S. holidays, following the company's holiday calendar.
  • 3% annual salary increase, according to the agreed compensation package.
  • Direct collaboration with executive leadership.
  • Significant ownership over GTM strategy, demand generation, and AI-driven commercial operations.
  • Opportunity to build scalable systems in an innovative, fast-growing industry.
Important Notes
This is a senior, hands-on GTM leadership role for a service-based business, not a traditional SaaS marketing or GTM position.
Candidates must demonstrate direct experience in services-led demand generation, revenue operations, and commercial growth.
Practical AI experience is essential. As part of the interview process, candidates will be expected to present real examples of AI-powered systems, process automations, or workflows they have personally built and implemented. Basic AI use for writing emails or generating content is not sufficient.
The interview process will involve the company's CEO and SVP of Revenue.
This position requires U.S. Eastern Time availability and occasional travel to the United States.
This is a remote/telecommute position.

  • Experience integrating and working with design systems, corporate component libraries, and Web Components.

  • Experience integrating REST APIs.

  • Proficiency with Git and repository management workflows, including branching strategies, pull requests, code reviews, and conflict resolution.

  • Strong experience with automated testing, including unit, integration, and component testing for services, components, and state management.

  • The opportunity to join a multicultural and international environment, collaborating with colleagues and teams across different countries.

jobs.description:
Our client, a leading Software, Information and Communication Technologies company, operates internationally (Athens, Brussels, Luxembourg, Copenhagen, Stockholm, London, Nicosia, Hong-Kong, Valetta, etc). Our client is a renowned supplier of IT services to government institutions, multinational corporations, public administrations and multinational companies, research and academic institutes.

Role Overview

Our client currently has a vacancy for a Scrum Master to offer his/her services as an expert remotely within the EU. In the context of the first assignment, the successful candidate will be integrated in the team of the company that will closely cooperate with a major client’s IT team on site.

Job Type: B2B Contract

Workplace: Remote

Requirements

  • University Degree and at least 8 years of IT professional experience;
  • Minimum of 3 of dedicated experience working as a Scrum Master at SM2 level or above;
  • Led at least 2 production teams through full sprint cycles (planning, review, retrospective, and refinement);
  • Implemented data-driven continuous improvement initiatives, such as increasing team velocity or reducing lead time;
  • Experience coordinating cross-team work via Scrum-of-Scrums or PI Planning events;
  • Deep knowledge of the Scrum Guide and Agile Manifesto principles and values;
  • Good knowledge of facilitation techniques (e.g., Fist of Five, participatory decision-making, Liberating Structures);
  • Good knowledge of systems-thinking and process tailoring to fit complex or evolving environments;
  • Good knowledge of team motivation and stakeholder engagement techniques (e.g., information radiators, team empowerment models);
  • Good knowledge of Agile metrics (velocity, cycle time, burn-up/down charts, cumulative flow diagrams) and the ability to build and interpret dashboards to support team performance and forecasting;
  • Tool proficiency in Azure DevOps (preferred) or Jira, particularly in backlog management, dashboards, and workflow configuration;
  • Possession of Scrum Master certifications: PSM II (or higher) and SAFe 5/6 Agilist;
  • Experience with one or more scaled Agile frameworks (SAFe, Nexus, LeSS, etc.) is considered as an asset;
  • Knowledge of integrating SAFe and Kanban approaches to optimize flow and delivery predictability is considered as an asset;
  • Excellent command of the English language.

Responsibilities

  • Organize and facilitate agile activities and ceremonies including daily stand-up meetings, sprint reviews, retrospectives, sprint and release planning, and product backlog refinement sessions;
  • Ensure that all meetings are positive, productive, stay on topic, and are kept within the timebox;
  • Collaborate closely with the product owner to manage the backlog;
  • Coach team and Product Owner on empiricism, value‑based backlog slicing, and incremental delivery;
  • Track and radiate flow metrics (velocity, sprint burndown, iteration burn rate) and guide the team in data‑driven improvement;
  • Champion and facilitate adoption of agile standards, tools, and best practices;
  • Proactively identify and resolve impediments to team progress;
  • Promote empowered, self‑organising teams, shared vision, psychological safety, collaborative decisions (e.g., Fist‑of‑Five);

What you'll do:

Grasshopper Bank is seeking a highly motivated Senior CRA Analyst to take ownership of the day-to-day execution and administration of the Bank’s Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) Program. In this role, you will apply your strong technical knowledge of CRA regulations to lead performance monitoring, manage data integrity, and coordinate regulatory reporting to ensure our digital commercial banking platform remains examination-ready.

As Grasshopper Bank actively prepares for and pursues a formal CRA Strategic Plan, this position will play a key role in preparing data baselines and establishing the tracking dashboards to monitor our progress against strategic goals.

In a shifting regulatory landscape, you will be expected to maintain up-to-date, forward-looking knowledge of the CRA environment, interagency regulatory updates, and modernizing rule changes.

Operating as a digital-first commercial bank, Grasshopper’s community development and lending initiatives focus strictly on the business and innovation economies. You will work cross-functionally with commercial underwriting, SBA lending, and treasury teams to ensure our commercial loans, SBA 7(a) and 504 originations, and qualified investments are accurately tracked, validated, and documented.

What You’ll Do
  • Own the end-to-end data collection, geocoding, and validation processes for commercial and Community Development (CD) loans, ensuring high-quality, audit-ready data.
  • Independently review, evaluate, and document qualified Community Development (CD) loans, investments, and service activities submitted by various business lines
  • Maintain the Bank’s CRA Public File and coordinate the compilation, scrubbing, and timely submission of annual small business loan registers under regulatory standards
  • Maintain records of the Bank’s qualified donations, sponsorships, and volunteer service hours targeting small business technical assistance and economic development
  • Lead the compilation of historical performance data, peer analyses, and baseline metrics to support the drafting, regulatory submission, and ongoing tracking of the Bank’s CRA Strategic Plan
  • Build and maintain performance dashboards to monitor Grasshopper’s progress against designated CRA Strategic Plan targets, proactively flagging areas of opportunity or risk
  • Actively track, analyze, and interpret the evolving CRA regulatory landscape, assessing the impact of new interagency modernization rules and advising on necessary adjustments to bank processes
  • Gather documentation, organizing technical request lists, and preparing data files for internal audits and OCC regulatory examinations

What you need:

  • 3–5 years of direct experience in CRA compliance, data analysis, or commercial loan compliance within a regulated financial institution
  • Advanced skills working with large datasets, geocoding tools, and reporting software to synthesize complex information into actionable compliance insights
  • Strong, up-to-date understanding of the Community Reinvestment Act, technical reporting requirements for small business loans, and upcoming regulatory modernization changes
  • Experience leveraging AI to document and package community development activities
  • Solid understanding of commercial loan files, SBA loan structures (7(a) and 504), and experience utilizing commercial loan systems (such as nCino)
  • Proven ability to manage data compliance projects independently, coordinate multi-departmental requests, and drive initiatives with minimal supervision
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, public policy, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., CRCM) are a plus

jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position. IT Support Engineer (L1/L2)Remote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Systems Engineer, System Administrator, Desktop Support Engineer, Service Desk Analyst Could you keep 425 people working from one Slack queue, and still say no to the wrong access request?
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

IT Support Engineer (L1/L2)Remote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Systems Engineer, System Administrator, Desktop Support Engineer, Service Desk Analyst

Could you keep 425 people working from one Slack queue, and still say no to the wrong access request?

On a typical day you might get a new tutor's Google Workspace, Slack and MFA live before their first class in the morning, work through a campus access point that keeps dropping with the MSP after lunch, and finish by turning today's fix into a knowledge base article the next person can follow.

About Contour

We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture.

Most people only notice IT when it stops working. This role is the reason they rarely do.

About This Role

You are the L1 and L2 support engineer for the whole company: the person staff message when something breaks, and the person who fixes most of it. You run the service desk, administer Google Workspace, Slack, HubSpot and the approved AI platforms, look after a fleet of macOS and Windows devices, and support the UniFi network, CCTV and door access across the Melbourne campuses with the local MSP on the ground. You report to the Senior Systems Engineer, who owns architecture, security policy, vendor contracts and any change to how a system is built. Everything at L1 and L2 is yours.

The standard here is different in two specific ways. First, security. Contour holds staff and student data, and most of what goes wrong in IT security goes wrong through a helpful support person granting access nobody checked. When a rushed request for broad access lands, the right move is to slow down and ask what the person needs to do, and you have to be able to do that with a senior manager on the other end. Second, repeat work. The third time you would do a task by hand, you propose the automation instead, and every fix gets written down, because a fix nobody can find is a fix you will do again.

This is a hands-on seat. You take the ticket, fix what you can, and hand up only what needs a senior pair of hands. You are the first dedicated support hire on the offshore technology team, working with that engineer and the Melbourne team, and the team grows around this seat as the company does.

Contour has grown to this size with technology support handled alongside other jobs. This role makes it someone's whole job. By the end of month three you will be working the queue to its response and resolution targets without escalating anything you could have fixed yourself, and running joiner, mover and leaver changes end to end including offboarding. You will have the most common fixes written up in the knowledge base and your first automation proposed. The runbooks you write in those months are the ones the team will still be following in three years.

Where the work lives

  • Slack, where the service desk lives:every request goes through the queue. Acknowledge there rather than in a DM, because the queue is the record and the report.

  • Google Workspace and the identity platform:accounts, groups, licences and MFA are set to match the role, so a joiner is working on day one and a mover carries nothing across that they should not.

  • macOS and Windows devices:enrolment and configuration follow the standard build, so a device is done when it matches the build.

  • UniFi:the controller tells you what the network is doing. Read it before you or the MSP touch anything.

  • The knowledge base:a fix is finished when it is written up so the next person can follow it without you.

  • The password manager:credentials live here and nowhere else.

What You Will Do

  • Work the queue.Acknowledge, triage and resolve L1 and L2 requests in the Slack service desk, and close the loop with the person who raised each one. Escalate what sits above L2.

  • Administer the workplace platforms.Google Workspace, Slack, HubSpot and the approved AI tools: accounts, groups, licences and permissions. Run joiner, mover and leaver access changes through the identity platform, including 2SV and MFA enrolment. Enrol, configure and fault-find macOS and Windows devices.

  • Keep the campuses connected.Support the UniFi stack across sites: access points, switches, guest and staff networks. Support CCTV and door access control, including adds, removes and fault escalation. Work campus network issues with the Melbourne MSP and hold them to what they committed to.

  • Support the systems other teams run on.Sales and go-to-market, finance, and the tools tutors use: access, configuration and first-line support.

  • Follow the process.Raise a change record before touching production, log incidents in full, and contribute to root cause analysis. Write and maintain knowledge base articles and how-to guides for the tech team and for end users, and keep system documentation current for what you touch.

  • Hold the line on access.Grant the least someone needs to do their job, and raise a request that looks broader than the role rather than granting it. Complete the offboarding checklist in order and in full. Report suspected phishing, unusual account activity and possible data exposure straight away: speed beats certainty here. Never share credentials outside the password manager, and pull people up when they ask you to.

  • Automate the repeat work.Propose the automation with the hours it saves and the tool you would use. Use the same AI tools in your own work and help staff use them well, including what must never be pasted into them.

If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.


Requirements

What You Need

  • 2 to 4 years in IT support, service desk or systems support, including L2 work where the fix was yours to own

  • Hands-on administration of Google Workspace or Microsoft 365: accounts, groups, licences and permissions, done by you. You support both macOS and Windows

  • Networking fundamentals in practice: IP addressing, VLANs and wireless, and the habit of reading a network issue rather than guessing at it

  • Identity and access basics: users, groups, roles, least privilege, MFA and 2SV

  • Time on a ticket queue measured on first response and time to fix

  • Clear written English. You explain fixes to non-technical people several times a day, and your write-up is what the next person follows, so clarity is part of the job

  • Comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference. The people you support are in Melbourne

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on UniFi, CCTV or door access control work

  • HubSpot, Rippling, Aircall or Notion administration

  • Light scripting or automation: Google Apps Script, Zapier or Make.com scenarios, or basic Python

  • Time in education or another environment that handles student or minor data

  • A diploma, degree or certification in the field: CompTIA A+ or Network+, Microsoft 365 Fundamentals, Google Workspace Administrator

The Kind of People Who Thrive Here

The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

What good looks like

  • Fast first, then thorough:every ticket gets a quick first response and a fix that holds, in that order.

  • Closed means confirmed:a ticket closes when the person who raised it says it works.

  • Escalations carry evidence:what you tried, what you saw, what you ruled out, so the senior engineer starts where you stopped.

  • Offboarding leaves nothing behind:a leaver's access is gone on the day, with a name against every step.

  • Repeat work shrinks:the queue gets lighter over the year because recurring tickets get automated or documented out of it.


Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India. No travel: the campus hardware is in Melbourne and you work it through the MSP and the onshore team. Compensation details shared early in the hiring process. You will hear from us within a week of applying, and the process is a written screen, a short video response, a practical task, and two conversations.

Apply with a CV and one paragraph on a request you slowed down, scoped down or refused because it was not safe, and what happened next.

Join ICF as a User Enablement Specialist supporting the ongoing operations and continuous improvement of GrantLens, a federal Salesforce grants management solution. You will provide dedicated solution-level user enablement support for GrantLens capabilities in production and help ensure users have the training, guidance, and support needed to effectively use the system.


As GrantLens evolves through new program onboarding, enhancements, and ongoing releases, you will translate product and process changes into practical user enablement. You will assess what changed, which personas and workflows are affected, what users need to understand or do differently, and what training, guidance, or support is required. The role provides continuity across onboarding, persona- and role-based training, release upskilling, self-service resources, instructional content, in-app guidance, and hypercare.


You will work closely with Product Owners, Business Analysts, Quality Assurance testers, developers, process and support teams, and federal stakeholders to keep user-facing resources aligned with current production functionality. The ideal candidate is a technically fluent enterprise application enablement professional who can independently learn complex functionality, operate comfortably within an Agile software delivery lifecycle, and translate evolving system behavior into clear guidance for non-technical users.


Job Location:

This position is fully remote within the U.S., with occasional travel to the client's Washington, D.C. office. Must support U.S. Eastern time zone working hours.


What You Will Do:

  • Develop, maintain, and deliver foundational, persona-specific, role-based, and ongoing training for programs and users transitioning onto or operating within GrantLens.
  • Perform user-impact analysis for enhancements and releases by reviewing requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, demonstrations, testing outcomes, and other release artifacts to determine affected personas, workflows, knowledge needs, and required enablement actions.
  • Translate complex system functionality, permissions, personas, sub-roles, and end-to-end workflows into clear training and guidance tailored to distinct user responsibilities.
  • Develop and maintain job aids, quick-reference guides, help and knowledge content, system demonstrations, instructional videos, FAQs, presentations, and other user-facing resources as the production solution evolves.
  • Develop and maintain instructional content for approved in-app guidance and digital adoption capabilities in coordination with O&M technical resources.
  • Participate in User Acceptance Testing (UAT), release readiness, demonstrations, and related software delivery activities as needed to understand functionality, validate user-facing workflows, identify enablement impacts, and prepare accurate production-aligned resources.
  • Support users following onboarding and releases through hypercare and targeted enablement; use recurring questions, user feedback, testing findings, support trends, and available adoption or usage data to identify knowledge gaps and prioritize enablement improvements.
  • Maintain content governance, version control, naming conventions, and lifecycle management for user-facing training and knowledge resources so users have access to current, production-aligned guidance.
  • Partner with Product, Business Analysis, Quality Assurance, development, process, and support teams to proactively identify enablement needs and maintain alignment between product changes and the user experience.
  • Develop user-facing digital learning and documentation with accessibility and Section 508 considerations appropriate to a federal technology environment.

Required Skills:
