  • 3+ years of experience performing user-impact or training-needs analysis for software changes and translating requirements, release information, workflows, or system behavior into targeted enablement actions.
  • 3+ years of experience designing and delivering persona-, role-, or workflow-based training for enterprise applications with differentiated permissions and user responsibilities.
  • 3+ years of experience developing and delivering instructor-led, virtual, self-paced, and release-based system training and upskilling.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience developing presentations, job aids, user guides, FAQs, knowledge articles, instructional videos, and system demonstrations.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with Jira and Confluence for requirements, release, issue, documentation, or knowledge-management workflows.
  • 2+ years of experience with screen capture, screen recording, video editing, PDF editing, and multimedia content-development tools used to create instructional resources.
  • Candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust.
  • Must be a United States (U.S.) Citizen or Green Card holder, and the work must be performed in the United States (U.S.), as this work is for a federal contract.
  • Candidate must have lived in the U.S. for three (3) full years out of the last five (5) years.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with Salesforce, particularly Salesforce-based enterprise or grants management solutions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, facilitation, cross-functional collaboration, systems thinking, creative problem-solving, adaptability, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, maintain accurate content across concurrent releases, and proactively identify user enablement needs in a fast-moving product environment.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and productivity tools, including presentation, document, spreadsheet, file-sharing, and collaboration applications.
  • Working knowledge of Agile software delivery and testing concepts, including requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, defects, UAT, releases, deployments, and production versus non-production environments.

Senior Software Engineer - Integrations

About the job

HeroDevs is hiring a Senior Software Engineer for our Shared Services team. We're the shared services team behind HeroDevs, the company that keeps critical open-source software secure long after it reaches end of life. We build and run the platforms, pipelines, and cloud infrastructure the rest of the company depends on. That includes the systems that deliver data and secure package releases to our integration partners. We care about doing things carefully, automating what shouldn't be manual, treating infrastructure as code, and building systems other engineers can trust and extend.

Position Summary

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer with deep infrastructure experience who also enjoys building the integrations that run on it. You'll own the design, reliability, and security of the cloud platform behind our partner integrations, and you'll build and evolve the pipelines that move data and package releases between our internal systems, our APIs, and our partners.

This is a high-ownership role. You'll shape technical direction, set the patterns other engineers follow and propose architecture decisions with the team. We're looking for someone who's comfortable with ambiguity, and thinks about failure modes before they happen.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate the cloud infrastructure that supports our integrations and shared platforms (compute, storage, networking, queues, scheduled workloads, and IAM)
  • Own infrastructure-as-code across environments
  • Architect and build reliable, secure data and package-delivery pipelines between internal systems, internal APIs, and integration partners
  • Lead technical design for new partner integrations, including data contracts, delivery mechanisms, validation, retries, and failure handling
  • Build and improve CI/CD with GitHub Actions, including build, test, release, and deployment automation for services and infrastructure
  • Establish observability practices (metrics, logging, tracing, alerting, and SLOs) so problems surface early and are easy to diagnose
  • Lead incident response and root-cause analysis for integration and infrastructure failures, and drive the follow-up work so they don't recur
  • Champion security across the platform, including use of secrets management, least-privilege access, supply chain integrity, and safe handling of partner data
  • Write services and tooling primarily using TypeScript/Node.js, packaged and deployed as containers
  • Review code and design documents

Required Qualifications

The bar is high: you need to zoom from annual content strategy to line-level copy review to prompting a new automation pipeline - and know which mode each situation calls for. We move in sprints, ship fast, and never let perfect be the enemy of good.

Tasks

  • Content quality and brand voice: Own the editorial standard across everything that goes out — LinkedIn posts, blog content, SEO copy, case studies, newsletter. You are the last human filter before anything is published. You can tell the difference between content that performs and content that just sounds like AI generated it, and you fix the latter.
  • AI content engine: Direct and maintain agentic pipelines that produce content at scale. You set direction, write the prompts, evaluate the output, and intervene when the machine gets it wrong. This is already partially built; you evolve and own it.
  • Account-based marketing support: Align the content calendar with live pipeline priorities. Brief assets for key accounts. Make sure sales has what it needs, when it needs it — not generic collateral.
  • SEO and inbound: Own organic growth. Blog strategy, keyword targeting, distribution playbook, conversion path optimisation.
  • Brand and thought leadership: Evolve the Retail Spotlight podcast into a content ecosystem. Ghostwrite and direct founder voice content across two distinct voices. Build refive's presence as the authoritative voice on in-store customer engagement in Europe.
  • Events and field: Project-manage event participation remotely — NRF, EuroShop, RTS London and similar. Own the full loop: logistics, pre-event content, on-site coordination with vendors and booth teams, lead capture workflows, post-event follow-up content. You run this independently; founders show up and present.
  • Partner co-marketing: Develop joint campaigns and launch materials with white-label and integration partners as the pipeline scales.
  • Metrics and reporting: Own the automated weekly marketing dashboard (GA4, HubSpot, LinkedIn). Know your numbers. Flag what is not working before anyone asks.

Requirements

  • 6-8 years of B2B SaaS or tech marketing experience, with real ownership - not just execution support.
  • You have run campaigns end to end and have results to show.
  • Fluent, flawless native spokend and written english
  • Agentic automation fluency. You have built or designed workflows using tools like Claude Code, n8n, Make, Zapier, or similar. You are comfortable prompting LLMs for structured outputs and wiring them into repeatable pipelines. This is not a nice-to-have it is how this role operates day to day.
  • Strategic range with execution instinct. You can write a marketing plan in the morning and review a CTA in the afternoon. You know when to go deep and when to move on.
  • Content quality instinct. You can tell the difference between AI-generated content that performs and content that just sounds like it was AI-generated. You write well yourself - sharp, no fluff, B2B-appropriate.
  • Modern mindset, not stuck in old-school playbooks. Curious about what new tools can do, comfortable with ambiguity, willing to try things that have no case study yet - but experienced enough to know what good looks like and push back when a shortcut will cost you later.
  • HubSpot and GA4 proficiency. You track what matters and use data to change direction, not validate decisions already made.
  • Retail or martech experience is a genuine plus — if you understand how brick-and-mortar retailers think about footfall, loyalty, and first-party data, you will ramp faster and produce better work.
  • One or more European language skills are a significant bonus given our primary market. But not a must have.

Benefits

We use heavy agentic automation across content, research, and reporting. This role is not about doing more with less, it is about designing systems that handle the repeatable work so human judgment goes where it actually matters. If that excites you, you will fit here. If you prefer full manual control over every deliverable, this is probably not the right environment.

To apply, send your CV plus responses to both tasks below. Please use the "Cover Letter" field for that. Applications without both tasks completed will not be reviewed.

  • Task 1: Editorial eye. jobs.description:
Product Development Owner

Buffalo Grove, IL

Monday – Friday 8:00 am – 5:00 pm

Remote

Do you want to build software that removes the manual work tax professionals dread every cycle?

CSC Corptax is looking for a Product Owner who pairs strong product fundamentals with a practical, hands-on approach to AI. You will own outcomes for a product area, work with your scrum team inside an agile delivery model, and find ways to eliminate the repetitive data preparation and validation work our clients do today. You will also use AI in your own daily work to move faster from client problem to shipped capability. Some of your work will extend an established product; some will mean shaping a new concept or rethinking an area from the ground up.

If you measure success by client outcomes, like taking apart a messy process to find what can be automated, and see AI as a tool to change how work gets done (not a buzzword), we want to talk with you.

Some of the things that you will be doing?

  • Own outcomes for your product area: Maintain a Now/Next/Later roadmap tied to system year and PI goals. Define success metrics before work starts, commit to “Now” scope you can deliver, and make clear trade-off decisions when priorities change, including when to cut, pivot, or stop work that evidence says will not deliver the outcome.
  • Shape new concepts and rethink existing areas: Take new products, features, and concepts from idea to adoption, and rebuild existing areas when the current approach no longer serves clients. Make scope decisions with incomplete information, adjust requirements as evidence comes in, and say no without stalling the team.
  • Eliminate manual preparation and validation work: Map how clients prepare, reconcile, and validate data today. Identify the repetitive, error-prone steps and design product capabilities (automation, rules-based checks, AI-assisted workflows) that remove them. Quantify the impact in hours saved, errors prevented, and cycle time reduced.
  • Apply AI responsibly in the product: Partner with engineering to identify where AI adds measurable client value. Define the guardrails a regulated tax environment requires: accuracy, auditability, explainability, data security, and clear points for human review. Before AI work starts, set accuracy thresholds, test datasets, and evaluation criteria with engineering so the team knows what “good enough to ship” means.
  • Use AI to work more efficiently: Use AI to draft and refine Features, user stories, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and release notes; analyze usage data and client feedback; and explore the codebase to understand current behavior before writing requirements.
  • Run the backlog in an agile framework: Write clear backlog items with testable acceptance criteria in Azure DevOps or Linear. Lead refinement, sprint planning, PI planning, and sprint demos. Identify and manage dependencies across teams.
  • Make insight-driven decisions: Use product analytics, support case trends, and client research to prioritize. Back major roadmap decisions with data, and define and review adoption KPIs within 90 days of each release.
  • Own the client experience end to end: Partner with the escalation owner assigned to your scrum team to understand what clients are reporting about your product, prioritize client issues, and write actionable work items for bugs and enhancements. Validate fixes through user acceptance testing, and apply Corptax UX standards so experiences stay consistent across products.
  • Drive awareness and adoption with go-to-market: Work closely with the go-to-market, Product Marketing, and Marketing teams from concept through launch. Use their view of pipeline strength, demo feedback from sales engineers, and account manager feedback on the product and adoption to shape priorities. Build awareness for new products, features, and concepts, and bring client and market feedback back into the backlog so every release is positioned, adopted, and measured.
  • Communicate with clarity: Present roadmap, progress, and risks to clients, sales, and executives. Review client-facing communication for accuracy and tone, and raise missed commitments early with a recovery plan.

What technical skills, experience and qualifications do you need?

  • 5+ years of recent product ownership or product management experience, or tax and accounting experience with direct involvement in software delivery
  • Undergraduate degree in Accounting, Finance, Computer Science, Information Systems, or equivalent experience
  • Hands-on use of AI tools in daily work, with concrete examples of a manual, repetitive process you automated or eliminated and the measured result
  • Ability to break a complex workflow into discrete steps, identify which steps can be automated or validated by rules, and write requirements for them
  • Experience taking a new product, feature, or concept from idea to adoption, or rethinking an existing area, with requirements that changed as evidence came in
  • Working knowledge of AI limitations (accuracy, hallucination, data privacy) and judgment on when human review is required
  • Working knowledge of agile methodologies and backlog tools such as Azure DevOps, Jira, or Linear
  • Comfort working with data: Excel, basic SQL, and product analytics tools
  • Effective communication with both technical and non-technical audiences, including clients and executives
  • Demonstrated ability to prioritize, manage time, and deliver on commitments, and to make the call to cut, pivot, or stop work when the evidence says so

Preferred:

  • Corporate tax experience (provision, US or international compliance, Pillar Two)
  • Experience with workflow and data automation tools such as Power Automate or Alteryx
  • Comfort reading code or navigating a repository (GitHub) to understand system behavior
  • Experience building reusable AI workflows, prompt libraries, or agents

What success looks like in your first year:

  • You own a Now/Next/Later roadmap for your product area with success metrics defined for every “Now” item
  • You have shipped at least one capability that removes a manual preparation or validation step for clients, with the time saved measured
  • You use AI to accelerate backlog creation: your “Now” backlog is refined and ready for the team to build, and you work ahead to shape “Next” and “Later” items into Features before each PI
  • Your team delivers at least 90% of committed “Now” items each PI, and you cut, pivot, or stop work early when evidence shows it will not deliver the client outcome

Proof is the world's first identity-assured transaction management platform and we are on a mission to digitize trust for all of life’s most critical transactions. Developed by the same market leaders and experts who brought notarization online with Notarize℠, Proof offers trust in a digital world by verifying identities and securing transactions to protect businesses and their customers. Proof operates identity infrastructure for high-consequence transactions. Built on a WebTrust-audited certificate authority and PKI-anchored verifiable credentials, Proof helps more than 8,000 businesses, from financial institutions and mortgage lenders to insurers and wealth managers, verify who is on the other side of a transaction. Having created the online notarization category, we're now extending into portable digital identity with our Verifiable Digital Credential (VDC) for banks, and into authorization for AI agents.

As Director of Product Marketing, you'll turn that technical foundation into positioning that a bank's Chief Risk Officer, head of digital, and compliance team all understand and act on. Day to day, you'll work across Product, Sales, and Marketing to shape messaging, lead launches, equip Sales to win, and make sure the market sees Proof as the trusted identity layer. You'll also lead and develop the product marketing function, starting with the Partner & Customer Marketing Manager.

  • Positioning and messaging: Own product and solution positioning and the messaging architecture (value propositions, proof points, and differentiation) across the VDC, identity verification, eSign/eNotary, and agentic authorization, tailored by segment (banking, mortgage, insurance, wealth) and buyer persona.
  • Launches and go-to-market: Run the launch process for new products and major features, from tiering and readiness through announcement, enablement, an post-launch measurement. Shape use-case plays such as account opening, high-value money movement, title and closing, and agent-initiated transactions with Revenue Marketing and Sales.

  • Product partnership: Partner with Product on pricing, packaging, and roadmap priorities. Track regulatory developments (CIP/KYC, digital identity, and eNotary legislation) and translate them into market opportunities and messaging.
  • Cross-functional content: Supply product and roadmap content for analyst briefings (e.g., Gartner, Forrester, Liminal, Celent, Datos Insights) with the Director of Communications, and product inputs for demand programs, content, and events.
  • Team leadership: Manage and develop the Partner & Customer Marketing Manager and grow the product marketing team over time, so that product, partner, and customer messaging stay aligned.

  • Experience marketing technical or API-driven products to regulated enterprise buyers, ideally financial institutions.
  • A record of creating positioning for a new or emerging category, with launches that measurably improved pipeline and win rates.

  • Experience with developer- or platform-led motions alongside enterprise sales.

Operating from six central hubs—Calgary, Mississauga, and Toronto in Canada, and Los Angeles, New York City, and San Antonio in the US—the team provides patients with an integrated, end-to-end healthcare experience.

We are proud to be ranked #2 on Deloitte’s 2024 list of Canada’s 50 fastest-growing tech companies and recognized as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures for two consecutive years. Permanent, full-time opportunity

PurposeMed's office is located on the unceded and traditional territories of the peoples of the Treaty 7 region in Southern Alberta, which includes the Blackfoot First Nation tribes of Siksika, the Piikuni, the Kainai, the Stoney Nakoda First Nations tribes of Chiniki, Bearspaw, and Wesley and the Tsuut’ina First Nation. The city of Calgary is also homeland to the historic Northwest Métis and to Métis Nation of Alberta, Region 3.

Who we hope to find:

PurposeMed is looking for a bilingual (English/Spanish) Client Solutions Specialist to join the team! This role will focus on supporting Freddie, the #1 rated PrEP provider in North America. As the first point of contact for PurposeMed's existing and prospective clients, you'll be responsible for delivering an amazing support experience. That means the bar does not just equal a resolved ticket; it is a patient who feels heard, who understands what happens next, and who leaves the interaction more confident in their care than when they arrived.

In this role, you’ll make an impact by:

Delivering Exceptional Patient and Stakeholder Support

  • Responding to incoming support tickets promptly and professionally, providing solutions or escalating issues as necessary
  • Speaking with patients and other key stakeholders over the phone to ensure a speedy resolution to their questions
  • Maintaining clear and friendly communication with patients and the Clinical team, ensuring a positive customer experience
  • Striving to achieve high customer satisfaction ratings through attentive and helpful experiences
  • Documenting Client Experience interactions and resolutions accurately, so the next person picking up that patient has what they need
  • Flagging friction you notice in the queue, so recurring patient pain points get surfaced rather than just resolved

Collaborating and Following Best Practices

  • Following established SOPs, along with privacy and healthcare compliance requirements, in every interaction
  • Communicating status and blockers clearly and on time, keeping your lead informed without being asked
  • Collaborating with team members to address common issues and share insights

Contributing Beyond the Support Queue

  • Taking on tasks such as writing and updating Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) or Help Center articles, refreshing macros and templates, or supporting a process change
  • Regularly contribute to team initiatives with direction, support, and guidance from your Team Lead
  • Participating in training sessions to enhance your knowledge of our products and services

We need someone who has:

  • Fluency in Spanish, both written and verbal
  • A high school diploma or equivalent, although a post-secondary degree or relevant certification is a plus
  • 1+ years of experience in customer service
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, to effectively interact with patients, the Clinical team, and team members
  • Excellent problem-solving abilities and a strong willingness to learn
  • The ability to work in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment
  • Availability to work additional shifts (including some statutory holidays and weekends) to provide necessary coverage for patient needs, with time-in-lieu offered once completed

It would also be great if you have:

  • A basic understanding of healthcare and technology concepts
  • Experience in technical support
  • Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment
  • Experience working in a distributed team environment

Compensation:

  • $52,000 - $56,000 CAD a year
  • The compensation listed above refers to a yearly base salary that may vary depending on a candidate's relevant qualifications, knowledge, competencies and work experience, and other factors including market conditions. Base pay is just one aspect of our total rewards at PurposeMed—see our other exciting benefits below!

Our Hiring Process:To best set you up for success, here’s what you canexpect after you apply

  • Application ReviewOur hiring team carefully reviews each application to understand how your skills and experience align with the role. We aim to respond within 14 days of receiving your application. In most cases, we’re much quicker—but as a small team that reviews every application personally, it can take a little longer when we’re hiring for high-volume roles.
  • Take-Home Assignment (1-2 hours)If your application aligns strongly with the role, you’ll be invited to complete a short take-home assignment that reflects the type of work you'd complete in this role. This helps us understand your approach to practical daily work and helps us assess certain skillsets early in the process. Please note: completing the assignment does not guarantee progression to the next stage of the process.
  • Initial Interview with a Recruiter (45 minutes)On our first call, you’ll meet with a member of our Talent Acquisition team for a high-level conversation about your background, interests, and alignment with the role and our mission. This also provides an opportunity for you to ask your initial questions about PurposeMed and the role.
  • Interview with the Hiring Manager and Team Lead (1 hour)In this conversation, we’ll dive deeper into the role and your relevant experience, while also exploring the core competencies needed for the position and how you could contribute to the team.

Do you think you could be our next Client Solutions Specialist? We look forward to seeing your application!

Why you should join us:

  • Be part of a team of great people who don’t take themselves too seriously. While we’re serious about the problems we solve, we believe in having fun along the way.
  • Make an impact, every single day. We’re providing compassionate, affirming care to many people who have never received the proper support before.
  • Be confident in bringing your whole self to work. Inclusivity is core to how we take care of our patients, our teammates, and ourselves. We create spaces that are safe and affirming.

What we’re offering (based on full-time, permanent roles in Canada & the USA):

Along with the benefits below, we offer additional programs and supports designed to help you feel your best—both at work and outside of it.

  • Work flexibly within a team that’s remote friendly; we believe that work should fit around your life*
  • 20 vacation days and a team that will remind you to use them!

  • Our unique People Potential program, in which you'll partner with your manager to identify opportunities to grow and achieve your full potential

If you are looking for a place that sparks your creativity, helps others, and will push you to be your best, then you’ll love PurposeMed.

PurposeMed is committed to being an equal-opportunity employer, and we highly encourage those from excluded and marginalized communities to apply. This includes groups such as (but not limited to): Indigenous, Black, and racialized communities, trans and non-binary, LGBTQ2S+, disabled, and HIV-positive people. jobs.title: Social Media Manager
jobs.excerpt: At Colibri Group, culture is at the heart of everything we do.
jobs.description:
At Colibri Group, culture is at the heart of everything we do. Our values Love, Joy, Boldness, Teamwork, and Curiosity guide how we work together, support our customers, and make a difference in the communities we serve.

Colibri Group is a leader in online professional education, serving more than one million learners each year across a family of trusted education brands. Within our Teacher Education Ecosystem, including Moreland University, we connect with aspiring and current educators, alumni, and school leaders to support their professional journeys. Social media helps us build authentic relationships with these audiences and connect them with valuable resources and opportunities.

Come Build What’s Next

We’re looking for a Social Media Manager to lead and grow the organic social media presence of Colibri Group’s Teacher Education Ecosystem. This person will shape how our brands show up across social channels, bring educator-focused stories and campaigns to life, build engaged communities, and use performance insights to support awareness, qualified traffic, leads, and applications.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role with meaningful ownership of social strategy, day-to-day content production, community engagement, social measurement, and the management of our existing influencer program. As a general guide, approximately 50% of the role is content creation, 25% is social strategy, and 25% spans analytics, reporting, and influencer-program work. The balance will shift with campaigns and business priorities.

We’re looking for someone who has managed social media on behalf of a company, organization, or agency client and understands what it means to collaborate with a marketing team and be accountable for KPIs. You should be equally comfortable developing a channel plan, filming and editing a short-form video, speaking on camera, tailoring content for different audiences, engaging with followers, and explaining what the performance data says to do next.

Important distinction: This is a professional social media management position, not an influencer, brand ambassador, or personal-content-creator opportunity. You will manage Moreland University's owned social channels and work with external influencers as partners; you will not be hired to promote our brands primarily through your own personal accounts.

What You’ll Do

  • Own organic social strategy and editorial planning: Build audience-specific strategies and content calendars across Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, and emerging channels. Prioritize Instagram and TikTok for educator audiences, tailor LinkedIn content for school leaders and alumni, and explore authentic, non-promotional participation in relevant Reddit communities. Translate wider Marketing initiatives into platform-native campaigns
  • Create content hands-on, with a strong emphasis on short-form video: Personally concept, script, film, edit, caption, and publish videos; appear confidently in talking-head content and social live events. Independently produce graphics, carousels, stories, and copy using tools such as Canva, collaborate with the Graphic Designer on brand consistency, and develop social assets to promote guides, events, and podcasts (without hosting the podcast)
  • Build and serve engaged communities: Manage organic social accounts day to day, including comments, DMs, tags, audience conversations, and admissions-related questions that need routing to the appropriate team. Proactively identify educator and school-leader stories and opportunities for meaningful engagement, not merely one-way posting
  • Measure performance and continually improve results: Monitor audience growth, reach, engagement, video performance, website traffic, leads, guide downloads, and applications attributable to organic social. Use reporting, experiments, and audience insights to refine creative decisions and channel priorities; demonstrate how social contributes to integrated marketing goals
  • Manage influencer partnerships and collaborate across Marketing: Oversee existing external creators, including briefs, content review, approvals, deliverables, renewals, payment coordination, budgets, and ROI. Recommend when to expand, adjust, or pause partnerships. Partner closely with content, design, and paid media colleagues; direct management of paid advertising is not part of this position. Occasionally support events and content opportunities requiring travel

What You’ll Bring

  • Professional organizational social media experience: Approximately 2–4 years managing organic social accounts for an employer, organization, or agency client, with personal ownership of deliverables and accountability for KPIs. Managing only your own personal influencer accounts does not meet this requirement; additional relevant professional experience is welcome
  • Proven creation and on-camera skills: Direct experience independently planning, filming, editing, and publishing compelling short-form video for a brand, plus the ability to appear on camera and support live social content. Strong social copywriting and hands-on Canva, Capcut, or comparable design skills are also expected
  • Demonstrated growth and analytical judgment: Evidence that you have grown audiences, not solely maintained existing accounts; ability to explain the KPIs you owned, results you achieved, and changes you made based on data. Familiarity with engagement, website traffic, lead or application attribution, and testing is valuable
  • Audience-focused collaboration and execution: Experience adapting tone, formats, and channels for distinct audiences; engaging communities through comments and DMs; and working within a marketing team to manage a busy editorial calendar, multiple priorities, and cross-functional projects
  • Required professional portfolio: Include an accessible portfolio link or relevant work samples showing organizational/client accounts, short-form videos you personally produced, and ideally measurable outcomes. Redacted or anonymized case studies are welcome for confidential work. Education/edtech experience, previous influencer-program coordination, Reddit knowledge, a related bachelor's degree, and familiarity with tools such as Sprout Social or ClickUp are helpful but not required. Occasional travel may be necessary

Tools, Platforms, and Methodologies You May Use

Experience with every tool below is not required. We care more about your ability to create strong work, manage the process, and make decisions from results than about checking specific software boxes.

  • Social channels: Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube, and Reddit or other educator communities
  • Video creation: CapCut or comparable filming and editing workflows. The team is open to effective tools you already know and use
  • Design and production: Canva, Capcut, and brand templates or design review with an in-house Graphic Designer
  • Scheduling, analytics, and collaboration: Sprout Social or comparable social management and native analytics tools; ClickUp or similar project-management platforms
  • Measurement and improvement: Reporting dashboards, campaign tracking, tests, performance reviews, and thoughtful use of AI for ideation, research, repurposing, or productivity while maintaining originality and brand standards

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • Own the organic social presence of a mission-driven education ecosystem and shape how our brands show up online
  • Create original, video-first content and tell relevant stories for teachers, future educators, alumni, and school leaders
  • Grow priority channels such as Instagram and TikTok while testing thoughtful community opportunities, including Reddit
  • Collaborate with content, design, and marketing colleagues while retaining autonomy over day-to-day creative execution
  • Connect creative work to measurable engagement, leads, and applications while helping evolve an established influencer-partnership program

We Encourage You to Apply

You may not check every preferred box, and that is okay! We welcome applicants with relevant experience in education, edtech, consumer brands, nonprofit or mission-driven organizations, agencies, and other environments where they have managed professional social channels, served distinct audiences, and delivered measurable results.

However, this position does require professional responsibility for an organization’s or client’s social presence, hands-on short-form video creation, comfort contributing on camera, and the ability to assess performance against KPIs. If your experience has primarily been creating content for your own personal influencer accounts, without managing an organization’s or client’s channels and results, this role is unlikely to be the right match.

A professional social media portfolio or relevant work samples must be included with your application to be considered. Please share a working link to campaigns, social accounts, video examples, or case studies that demonstrate your direct work and impact. If your work is confidential, you may submit redacted or anonymized case studies and examples that respect client or employer requirements.

If you enjoy creating content yourself, collaborating within a marketing team, using data to make it better, and helping real communities connect with an education brand, we would love to hear from you.

What You Can Expect From Our Hiring Process

We want our interview process to give you a clear picture of the role, the team, and what it’s like to work at Colibri while giving us the opportunity to understand your experience, how you approach your work, and what you’re looking for next. We do not use AI to review applications; your application is reviewed by a human on the Talent Acquisition team. While the exact process may vary slightly by role, you can generally expect:

1. Recruiter Conversation: An introductory conversation with Talent Acquisition about your professional social media background, interests, expectations, and fit for this position

2. Hiring Manager Conversation: A deeper conversation with the Senior Director of Marketing, including review of your work, approach to short-form video, audience segmentation, strategy, and results

3. Team / Cross-Functional Conversation: A conversation with team members, focused on collaboration and the capabilities relevant to day-to-day success in this role

4. Final Conversation and Decision: A final conversation with the team. For finalists, there may be an optional opportunity to connect with additional content teammates. Talent Acquisition will share details and preparation expectations throughout the process.

Application deadline: Tuesday, October 20th, 2026.

Our goal is to make the experience thoughtful, respectful, and transparent. We encourage you to ask questions throughout the process—we’re evaluating the opportunity together.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Colibri Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels welcome, respected, and empowered to do their best work. We encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds, experiences, and career paths to apply.

We are seeking an experienced Embedded Software Engineer to design, develop, and optimize firmware and embedded software for next-generation connected devices, industrial automation systems, automotive platforms, medical devices, and IoT products. This role focuses on developing high-performance, real-time embedded applications that interact directly with hardware components while ensuring reliability, security, and compliance with industry standards.
You will collaborate closely with hardware engineers, systems architects, electrical engineers, QA teams, and product managers to build embedded software solutions supporting mission-critical products deployed across enterprise and industrial environments. The ideal candidate possesses strong expertise in embedded C/C++, RTOS development, device drivers, communication protocols, and hardware-software integration.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design, develop, and maintain embedded software and firmware for microcontroller and microprocessor-based systems.
  • Develop low-level device drivers, Board Support Packages (BSP), bootloaders, and hardware abstraction layers (HAL).
  • Build real-time applications using RTOS platforms including FreeRTOS, VxWorks, ThreadX, Zephyr, or Embedded Linux.
  • Develop firmware supporting communication interfaces including UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, USB, Ethernet, BLE, and MQTT.
  • Collaborate with hardware engineers during board bring-up, hardware validation, and system integration activities.
  • Optimize embedded applications for CPU utilization, memory footprint, power consumption, and boot time.
  • Implement secure firmware update mechanisms, secure boot, encryption, and hardware-based security features.
  • Develop software supporting sensors, actuators, wireless modules, and peripheral devices.
  • Debug hardware-software integration issues using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG debuggers, and protocol analyzers.
  • Write unit tests, integration tests, and automated validation scripts to ensure firmware quality.
  • Participate in architecture reviews, code reviews, technical design discussions, and Agile development activities.
  • Support production deployments, field diagnostics, root cause analysis, and firmware maintenance.

Required Skills
  • Six or more years of professional embedded software development experience.
  • Strong proficiency in Embedded C and Modern C++ for firmware development.
  • Extensive experience developing software for ARM Cortex-M, ARM Cortex-A, STM32, NXP, Renesas, Texas Instruments, or Microchip microcontrollers.
  • Strong understanding of embedded systems architecture, memory management, interrupts, DMA, timers, and peripheral programming.
  • Hands-on experience with RTOS platforms including FreeRTOS, Zephyr, ThreadX, Embedded Linux, or VxWorks.
  • Experience developing device drivers and low-level hardware interfaces.
  • Strong knowledge of communication protocols including UART, SPI, I2C, CAN/CAN FD, Ethernet, USB, Modbus, MQTT, BLE, and TCP/IP.
  • Experience with Embedded Linux development, kernel configuration, and driver development is highly desirable.
  • Familiarity with hardware debugging tools including JTAG, SWD, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and serial protocol analyzers.
  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated firmware builds, and version control systems.
  • Strong understanding of software debugging, profiling, and optimization techniques.
  • Experience using build systems such as CMake, Makefiles, or Bazel.
  • Knowledge of secure coding practices for embedded systems.
  • Experience working in Agile Scrum development environments.

Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience developing software for automotive, aerospace, medical devices, industrial automation, robotics, or IoT platforms.
  • Familiarity with AUTOSAR, MISRA C/C++, ISO 26262, IEC 61508, DO-178C, IEC 62304, or other industry safety standards.
  • Experience with Yocto Project, Buildroot, or custom Embedded Linux distributions.
  • Knowledge of wireless communication technologies including Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Zigbee, LoRaWAN, or Cellular IoT.
  • Experience implementing secure boot, TPM integration, Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), and firmware signing.
  • Familiarity with FPGA integration and hardware acceleration.
  • Experience using Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or GitLab CI for firmware automation.
  • Knowledge of Python or Shell scripting for test automation and manufacturing support.
  • Experience with cloud-connected IoT platforms including AWS IoT Core, Azure IoT Hub, or Google Cloud IoT.
  • Embedded systems certifications or contributions to open-source embedded projects are highly desirable.

Project Environment
You will be joining an embedded engineering team developing next-generation intelligent devices and connected systems supporting enterprise and industrial customers. Current initiatives include:
  • Industrial IoT gateways and edge computing platforms
  • Smart manufacturing and factory automation controllers
  • Automotive electronic control units (ECUs)
  • Medical monitoring and diagnostic devices
  • Connected consumer electronics and smart home devices
  • Wireless sensor networks and edge AI platforms
  • Embedded Linux networking appliances
  • Secure firmware platforms supporting OTA (Over-the-Air) software updates

This is a hands-on engineering role where you will contribute to firmware architecture, embedded software development, hardware integration, system validation, performance optimization, and long-term product reliability for enterprise-grade embedded solutions.

jobs.title: Financial Analyst, India
jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position. Financial Analyst, IndiaRemote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Finance Analyst, FP&A Analyst, MIS Analyst, Business Analyst What would you tell a leadership team about their own business that they have not thought to ask?
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Financial Analyst, IndiaRemote (India) | Full-Time

Also searched as: Finance Analyst, FP&A Analyst, MIS Analyst, Business Analyst

What would you tell a leadership team about their own business that they have not thought to ask?

On a typical day you might reconcile the weekly scorecard numbers back to Xero and HubSpot before the leadership review in the morning, work through month-end variances with the Financial Controller and draft the commentary after lunch, and send a short written note on why a revenue line moved and what you would do about it before the end of day.

About Contour

We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture, and this role sits with the group finance function.

A company growing this fast is steered by the numbers someone puts in front of it each week. This is that seat.

About This Role

You're Contour's first Financial Analyst, and the senior of the first two India-based seats in group finance, alongside an Accountant who runs the transactional side. You own the analytical layer: the monthly reporting leadership reads, the weekly scorecard the business runs on, budget vs actual tracking, and the analysis behind decisions. You report to the Financial Controller, who owns the budgeting and forecasting, statutory reporting, management reporting, tax, and final sign-off of all financial data. Leadership decides which metrics matter; you make them measurable and reconciled, with the explanation attached.

Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you're proactive by instinct: when a number moves, you find out why, form a view, and put a recommendation in front of the people who can act on it. You don't stop at what happened, you push to why it happened and what should happen next. Second, you build reporting to run itself, so your hours go into analysis, not copy-paste.

This analytical work has so far been carried alongside other jobs, not owned by one person. You change that: the weekly and monthly rhythm leadership runs on is being set up now, and you build it.

By month three, you own the monthly reporting cycle, the weekly leadership scorecard is live with agreed definitions and targets vs budget, budget vs actual reporting is standing, and at least one of your recommendations has been acted on. What you build here becomes how Contour reads its numbers as it scales.

Where the work lives

  • Xero: actuals live here, so your reporting starts from, and ties back to, the ledger.

  • Google Sheets: the working medium for models, budgets, and reporting packs, so clean structure and formulas someone else can follow are the baseline.

  • HubSpot and Stripe: enrolment and payment data live here, so revenue analysis means joining what the CRM says with what actually settled.

  • AI tools: Claude and similar are part of how this team works, so using them to build, draft, and check analysis is expected here, not a novelty.

  • monday.com: task status moves here, and keeping yours current is how a remote team sees progress without having to ask.

What You Will Do

  • Own the monthly management reporting pack.Build it, run it on a predictable cycle, and make it the version leadership trusts: actuals from Xero, enrolment and revenue from HubSpot and Stripe, with commentary on what changed and why.

  • Run the weekly leadership scorecard.One set of numbers, agreed definitions, one source of truth, red-amber-green against targets. You keep definitions tight and figures reconciled so nobody argues whose number is right.

  • Track the business against budget.The Financial Controller owns the budget; you own how we track against it. Build the reporting, explain variances, flag material ones early with a view on what to do.

  • Analyse enrolments and revenue across the three brands.Volumes, movements, and the drivers across Contour Education, TestPrep, and MedPrep, turned into findings a non-finance leader can act on.

  • Answer the questions behind decisions.Sizing an offering, checking if a cost line earns its keep, testing an assumption in the forecast: these land with you and your recommendations go into the weekly review.

  • Automate the grunt work.Use Sheets, AI tools, and the BI layer to make recurring reports assemble themselves. The dashboarding toolkit is still being chosen; you will have a real say in it.

  • Partner for clean inputs.The Accountant keeps the ledger tight and the data team owns the sources of truth; you work with both so your numbers agree everywhere they appear.

If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.


Requirements

What You Need

  • 3 to 6 years in an FP&A, finance analyst, MIS, or business analyst role, including management reporting you built or ran yourself rather than inherited.

  • Advanced Google Sheets or Excel: you can build a model, a variance analysis, and a clean reporting layout from a blank sheet

  • Comfort pulling data out of the systems it lives in (an accounting platform, a CRM, a payments platform) and joining it into one picture that agrees with itself.

  • AI tools as a working habit: you already use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or similar to speed up analysis and build reporting, and can show how.

  • Sharp written English. Much of your work with the Financial Controller and leadership is asynchronous, so a variance commentary or a recommendation has to land right the first time, in writing.

  • Comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference.

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on Xero, or another cloud accounting platform, on the reporting side

  • Dashboards you built in Power BI or Looker Studio that other people actually used

  • EdTech, education services, or another B2C business with recurring or instalment revenue

The Kind of People Who Thrive Here
The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

What good looks like

  • One version of the truth:any number you publish agrees with the ledger and everywhere else it appears.

  • Reports run themselves:the recurring pack lands on schedule without heroics, because you automated the assembly.
  • Ahead of the question:leadership hears why a number moved from you, before they ask.

Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India. Compensation is competitive and benchmarked to the role and your experience, and we discuss it openly early in the process. From application to offer: a short screen, a technical assessment, a culture conversation with our People team, and a final interview with the Financial Controller, in about four weeks.

Apply with a CV and one short paragraph on an insight you found in data that changed a decision: what you noticed, and what happened next.

jobs.excerpt: Who We AreYellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Yellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries. From Stablecoin payment infrastructure to fiat settlement rails, wallet services, and custom local Stablecoin issuance, Yellow Card provides the complete infrastructure businesses need to manage Stablecoins, payments, and operations across 50 emerging markets.

Yellow Card operates with a substantial global team spanning 24 countries. This workforce is characterized by its linguistic diversity, with collective speaking of over 25 languages, underscoring the company’s extensive international reach.

The Security Operations Engineer is the operational backbone of the Security Operations Centre (SOC). It is a fully remote, hands-on, technical role that owns three tightly integrated domains: security alert design, triaging, and automated response; cloud security posture management across EKS and AWS environments; and posture tracking and reporting.

Reporting to the Associate Director, Product & Infrastructure Security, the engineer works alongside a mature Application Security team and collaborates closely with DevOps, Engineering, and Security GRC functions. The role sits within the First Line of Defense and is expected to progressively drive down manual effort through detection-as-code and SOAR automation.

This is not a perimeter-security or scan-and-report role. The right candidate must be comfortable writing detection logic, triaging cloud misconfigurations at the infrastructure level, and owning end-to-end vulnerability remediation cycles in containerised environments.

What You'll Do

1. Security Operations

The engineer owns the full lifecycle of security detection and response inside the SOC, from signal design through to automated containment. This is the primary domain of the role.

Alert design and coverage

  • Design and maintain SIEM detection rules covering cloud, container, identity, and application layers, using both signature-based and behavioural logic
  • Map detection coverage against the MITRE ATT&CK framework and identify gaps relevant to the organisation's AWS and EKS attack surface
  • Integrate threat intelligence feeds to refresh rule logic for emerging threats and TTPs
  • Maintain a detection backlog, prioritised by risk, with defined review cadences

Alert triage

  • Daily SIEM alert triage following defined response timing standard
  • Classify, investigate, and resolve security signals;
  • Reduce false-positive rates through structured tuning cycles, with documented rationale for rule changes
  • Maintain triage runbooks for key production detection rules

Automated response workflows (SOAR)

  • Build and maintain SOAR playbooks for common alert types including IAM anomalies, misconfiguration alerts, exposed secrets, and container runtime events
  • Automate enrichment steps (asset lookup, threat intel correlation, ownership resolution) to reduce analyst time-to-context
  • Document automation logic and maintain version control for all playbooks
  • Measure and report automation coverage rate as a standing KRI

2. Cloud Security Posture Management

Cloud posture management is the infrastructure-facing domain of the role, covering vulnerability management, identity governance, and configuration and change control. AWS EKS and Serverless resources are the primary environments.

Vulnerability management

  • Own the end-to-end vulnerability triage process for cloud and container environments, prioritising findings by business impact using CVSS scoring, asset criticality, and exploitability context
  • Manage EKS-specific vulnerability coverage: base image currency, workload scanning results, pod security standards compliance, and node group patching cadence
  • Coordinate remediation with engineering teams by opening well-scoped tickets, tracking progress, and escalating SLA breaches
  • Maintain MTTR and SLA compliance data by severity tier
  • Oversee CSPM posture score targets; triage new Critical findings within defined SLA windows

Identity and access governance

  • Review and approve IAM policy changes, enforcing least-privilege and flagging over-permissioned roles or service accounts
  • Execute scheduled IAM hygiene reviews: unused credentials, stale access keys, overly broad policies, and cross-account trust boundaries
  • Govern workload identity configurations in EKS, ensuring service accounts carry only the permissions required
  • Support the secrets rotation program and enforce zero hardcoded credentials across the estate

Configuration and change management

  • Review and approve cloud network security changes: security group modifications, network ACL changes, and routing updates
  • Own container image security: base image update cadence, scanning results review, and image ownership classification
  • Investigate and remediate misconfiguration alerts surfaced by CSPM tooling within defined SLA windows
  • Maintain a configuration baseline for critical cloud resources and flag drift

3. Posture Tracking and Reporting

The engineer is the primary data owner for security posture metrics across both SOC and cloud domains. Reporting outputs feed executive dashboards, GRC compliance evidence, and quarterly risk reviews.

KRI data collection

  • Collect and maintain Key Risk Indicator data across all three KRA domains on defined cadences
  • SOC KRIs: MTTA (Mean Time to Acknowledge), MTTR, false-positive rate, automation coverage rate, detection coverage score
  • VM KRIs: Critical/High finding counts, SLA compliance rate by severity, MTTR by tier, overdue remediation count
  • Posture KRIs: CSPM score, under-protected asset count, misconfiguration closure rate, IAM hygiene score, log source coverage

Recurring control reviews

  • Execute infrastructure security control checks on weekly (CSPM critical findings), monthly (IAM hygiene, secrets rotation status), and quarterly (posture benchmark, detection coverage review) cadences
  • Produce structured findings reports for each review cycle, flagging control failures for escalation

Reporting

  • Provide SOC and cloud posture metrics, including trends, at the required reporting cycles
  • Support external audit and due diligence processes by providing evidence artefacts

4. Others

  • Co-own the shared vulnerability backlog (infrastructure side) with the Application Security team, ensuring consistent prioritisation methodology across domains
  • Serve as the infrastructure and identity SME for the AppSec team during application security assessments and architecture reviews
  • Own infrastructure containment during incidents that span application and infrastructure layers, working alongside AppSec for root cause analysis
  • Provide infrastructure, identity, and network security review for new third-party integrations prior to deployment
  • Collaborate with the Security GRC function on control evidence and compliance mapping, particularly for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR requirements

What You'll Bring

  • Fluency in English, both written and verbal
  • Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and across different time zones
  • 3 to 5 years of experience in security operations, cloud security, or infrastructure security engineering
  • Hands-on AWS security experience: IAM policy design, virtual network architecture, cloud-native security services, CloudTrail, GuardDuty
  • Kubernetes and EKS security experience: pod security standards, network policy enforcement, workload identity, image scanning
  • SIEM operations: alert triage, detection rule authoring (signature-based and behavioural), log analysis and correlation
  • Vulnerability management: CSPM tooling, risk-based prioritisation, CVSS scoring, SLA framework operation
  • IaC security: ability to read and review Terraform or CloudFormation for misconfigurations
  • Incident response: investigation, containment, and post-incident reporting
  • Experience in a regulated environment (FinTech, payments, banking, or crypto preferred)
  • Ability to author and tune detection rules without relying on vendor-supplied defaults
  • Structured written communication for triage reports, post-incident write-ups, and stakeholder metrics
  • Ability to coordinate remediation across engineering teams without direct authority
  • Comfort operating in a lean team where domain boundaries are broader than in large enterprise security functions
  • Professional certifications: AWS Security Specialty (highly valued)
  • Experience with CSPM and SIEM platforms: Datadog, Wiz, Orca Security
  • Experience with secrets management platforms: AWS Secrets Manager
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks: SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, DORA
  • Scripting ability in Python or Bash for detection-as-code and operational automation
  • Experience with SOAR or workflow automation platforms
  • Understanding of cryptocurrency or blockchain security considerations
  • Experience in a startup or scale-up environment
  • AI tooling familiarity and interest in applying AI to operational workflows

What We Offer

  • Compensation & Benefits: We offer competitive compensation and meaningful health coverage, and all full-time employees are participants in our stock option plan.
  • Learning & Development: Access to resources, support, and autonomy to grow professionally.
  • Remote-First Flexibility: We embrace a fully remote work environment.
  • Regulated, multi-geography environment with real-world impact on financial inclusion
  • Mental Health Support Services: Your mental well-being matters to us.
  • Ownership of the SOC and cloud security posture function from day one, in a high-growth FinTech environment
  • Broad domain exposure: detection engineering, cloud security, container security, incident response, and compliance
  • Collaborative team culture with a mature AppSec function and strong leadership support

Ready to Join Us?

Job Summary:

Health information coding is the transformation of verbal descriptions of diseases, injuries, and procedures into numeric or alphanumeric designations. The coding process reviews and analyzes health records to identify relevant diagnoses and procedures for distinct patient encounters. Coders are responsible for translating diagnostic and procedural phrases utilized by healthcare providers into coded form procedure codes that can be utilized for submitting claims to payers for reimbursement. A joint effort between the healthcare provider and the coder is essential to achieve complete and accurate documentation, code assignment, and reporting of diagnoses and procedures.

Job Duties:

  • Reviews the content of the medical record for hospital and professional inpatient or outpatient records to identify principal diagnosis, secondary diagnoses and procedures performed that explain the reason for service being provided or the admission and patient severity and comply with standard provider coding regulations.
  • Carefully details review of documents such as laboratory findings, radiology reports, various scan reports, discharge summary, history and physical, consultations, orders, progress notes and other ancillary services treatment records needed to ensure all pertinent diagnoses and procedures are recorded.
  • Translates all diagnostic and procedural phrases utilized by healthcare providers into coded form using procedure codes as required.
  • Using the Encoder software program, determines the codes for all diagnoses and procedures.
  • Determines their sequencing to legally maximize reimbursement.
  • Assigns the appropriate DRG.
  • Assigns codes based on hospital and professional coding guidelines, Coding Clinic directives, federal regulations, CCI coding initiatives, CPT Assistant or other standard coding guidelines Queries physicians as needed to clarify documentation within the patient’s record to facilitate complete and accurate coding.
  • Reviews coding guidelines on an annual basis and makes recommendations for change to improve coding and data management.
  • Communicates to Coding Quality and Professional Manager any new diagnoses, procedures, technologies, etc. documented within patient records to ensure that appropriate diagnosis and procedure codes are selected and incorporated into hospital and professional coding guidelines.
  • Updates and corrects historical file data by completing and submitting claim action reports per the PHC4 quarterly report.

Work is typically performed in an office environment. Accountable for satisfying all job specific obligations and complying with all organization policies and procedures. The specific statements in this profile are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements considered necessary to successfully perform the job.

  • Participates in customer meetings, discussions and decisions. Identifies and proposes improvements to security policies, standards and procedures, and risk mitigation/remediation activities.
  • Supports product development discovery efforts, security architecture design and control evaluation
  • Shares best practices and technical knowledge among multiple teams/portfolios.

Required:

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience with DoD network engineering/management
  • Minimum 3 years specified work in Cyber Security
  • MUST hold at a minimum DoD 8140/8570 certification level: IAT II or IAT III
  • MUST hold at least ONE of the following certifications: CASP+, AWS Security, CCSP, CSSLP (or Associate of ISC2), or equivalent technical security certification or demonstrated experience directly related to the problem domain
  • Specific knowledge that may include, but is not limited to: Unix, DevSecOps, web application security, web application modernization, AWS cloud security, DoD/U.S. Air Force Risk Management Framework and related security policies and practices

The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) is a not-for-profit international regulatory authority whose mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid. NERC’s area of responsibility spans the continental United States, Canada, and the northern portion of Baja California, Mexico. NERC is the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO) for North America, subject to oversight by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and provincial authorities in Canada. NERC’s jurisdiction includes users, owners, and operators of the BPS, which serves nearly 400 million people.

Our Mission

The vision for the ERO Enterprise, which is comprised of NERC and the six Regional Entities, is a highly reliable and secure North American BPS. Our mission is to assure the effective and efficient reduction of risks to the reliability and security of the grid.

  • Experience with the operation, design, or analysis of AC and DC electric power systems.

  • Hands-on experience with SCADA, DAS, telemetry, and operational datasets for power plant performance assessment.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

Nice-to-have

jobs.description:
The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

Compensation:

For this senior role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD based on experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work.

About the Role:

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through.

This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery.

You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with.

At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones.
  • Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it.
  • Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering.
  • Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery.
  • Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt.
  • Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations.
  • Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own.

What We Look For:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience.
  • Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days.
  • Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus.
  • Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring.
  • Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate.
  • Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills:

  • Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope.
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence.
  • Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA).
  • Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer.
  • Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right.
  • Experience with threat modeling at a system level.

About You:

  • You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better.
  • You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it.
  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting.
    You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

Sezzle’s Technology Stack:

  • Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python
  • Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native
  • Backend: Golang
  • Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
  • DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
  • Version Control: Git
  • CI/CD: Gitlab
  • Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests
  • Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

The CISO is responsible for establishing and leading the organization's cybersecurity strategy, protecting information assets, systems, and infrastructure from evolving threats.
