jobs.title: Senior People Ops Manager - Payroll & Systems
jobs.excerpt: About Convergent ResearchConvergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO).
jobs.description:
About Convergent Research

Convergent Research is a nonprofit science studio best known for pioneering the Focused Research Organization (FRO). We architect critical infrastructure that removes bottlenecks to breakthrough scientific research.

FROs are mission-driven, time-bound organizations built to solve important scientific and engineering bottlenecks. Convergent secures funding and provides the operational backbone that allows scientists and engineers to move quickly, from legal formation and governance to hiring, finance, communications, and operational systems. We’ve taken 14 FROs from idea to operating entity, including four launches in 2026.

About the Role

Payroll probably isn’t the first thing that comes to mind when you think about breakthrough science. But scientists can’t do their best work if they aren’t paid correctly, benefits aren’t working, or their organization isn’t set up to employ them.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Senior People Ops Manager - Payroll & Systems to own the people ops infrastructure that keeps Convergent and our FROs running smoothly. You’ll make sure our employees get paid accurately and on time, our policies and systems keep pace with our growth, new FROs become functioning employers, and organizations completing their missions can wind down responsibly.

This is a senior, hands-on expert role. We’re looking for someone who knows parts of this work better than we do. Someone who doesn’t just identify problems but brings recommendations, builds solutions, and sets the standard for how we operate. You’ll have significant autonomy to make decisions within your domain, with the Head of People providing final approval on decisions that impact company-wide strategy or multiple teams.

You’ll report to our Head of People and work closely with our People Ops Manager – Employee Experience, who owns recruiting, onboarding, and internal communications, and our Sr. HRBP, who serves as the primary point of contact for FRO employees. You’ll also partner with our Launch team, which coordinates the many moving pieces involved in getting a new FRO off the ground or winding one down. As we grow, there may be an opportunity to add a coordinator to support routine administrative work.

A quick note on payroll: We use TriNet as our US PEO and Rippling for UK payroll. Our providers handle tax calculations and filings, but that doesn’t mean we’ve outsourced accountability. You’ll own the accuracy of the inputs, review the outputs, and make sure issues get resolved. A second member of People Ops will provide an independent pre-run review.

This role will initially be approximately 60% hands-on execution and 40% policy development, infrastructure building, and continuous improvement. We need someone who enjoys both.

You Will (Duties)

  • Own payroll and make it bulletproof. You'll manage US and UK payroll end to end, including timesheets, payroll changes, initial review, and accuracy. We use TriNet (US) and Rippling (UK), so providers handle tax calculations and filings, but accountability stays with you. You'll build and maintain controls for input validation, independent pre-run review by another People Ops team member, pre- and post-run reconciliation, change approvals, and audit trails. You'll document processes so someone else can run payroll safely and push providers to fix gaps when needed.
  • Keep benefits, retirement, and leave running smoothly. You'll own benefits administration, COBRA, open enrollment, US 401(k) and UK pension administration, including contributions, records, and provider coordination. You'll also manage leave administration in our HRIS and workers' compensation, partnering with the Sr. HRBP when accommodations or employee-specific issues arise.
  • Make our people systems work for us. You'll own our HRIS architecture, configuration, integrations, data integrity, governance, and reporting, including source-of-truth rules, field ownership, and auditing. You'll troubleshoot escalated issues, manage vendor relationships and platform performance, and recommend when to build, buy, change, or simplify systems, with costs and risks clearly laid out.
  • Keep our policies and compliance ahead of our growth. You'll partner with the Head of People to write and maintain compliant policies across US federal and state jurisdictions, the UK, and EOR-covered countries, with a jurisdictional compliance matrix, version control, and review dates. You'll also own the people compliance calendar, covering filings, renewals, notices, audits, and policy reviews, with clear owners and lead times. You'll know when to involve outside counsel, while the Head of People retains final statutory policy approval and decisions with company-wide strategic implications.
  • Coordinate immigration and compensation processes. You'll facilitate FRO introductions to immigration counsel, coordinate vendors, track timelines, and provide HRIS documentation (not manage substantive immigration cases). You'll support reporting for compensation reviews, while the Head of People owns compensation strategy.
  • Help new FROs become functioning employers. You'll stand up the people infrastructure for each new FRO, including entity and EOR setup, payroll and benefits activation, policies, and a usable Notion workspace. You'll coordinate the people workstream within the broader plan owned by the Program Launch Manager, managing dependencies such as TriNet and Rippling onboarding timelines and flagging risks early.
  • Help FROs wind down responsibly. Because FROs are designed to be time-bound, finishing well matters. You'll own the operational side of wind-downs, including individual terminations, jurisdiction-specific final pay, benefits termination, platform and entity closure mechanics, and records retention. You'll partner with the Sr. HRBP on transition planning and employee communications, and with the Head of People on severance and counsel-involved matters.

In Six Months, You Will Have (6-Month Goals)

  • Taken full ownership of US and UK payroll, and pension/401k administration, with documentation detailed enough for someone else to run these processes safely.
  • Audited and updated our source-of-truth salary data.
  • Created a process for managing timecards and hourly payroll in Rippling, even though we don’t currently have hourly employees in the UK.
  • Built a 12-month roadmap with OKRs and success criteria, agreed upon with the Head of People, covering SOPs, controls, and infrastructure improvements, and completed 2-3 of the highest-priority initiatives.
  • Designed and implemented a payroll controls framework and people compliance calendar, with clear ownership, review processes, and accountability.
  • Completed a gap assessment of our policies by jurisdiction and closed the highest-risk gaps.
  • Supported at least one new FRO launch and one FRO wind-down from start to finish on the people operations side, assuming project timelines permit.

You Are (Skills)

  • A seasoned people ops expert who enjoys doing the work. You’ve owned payroll and people systems before. You’re comfortable being the person everyone turns to for answers, and you’re equally comfortable getting into the weeds. When we have something wrong, you’ll tell us and bring a better solution.
  • Detail-oriented. You sweat the details where it matters (ie payroll and compliance), but you also know when to not let perfect get in the way of done.
  • A builder of repeatable processes. You see a one-off problem and start thinking about how to prevent it from happening again. You create playbooks, templates, controls, and documentation that make our systems easier to run and safer to scale. You also protect the time needed to improve those systems, even when things get busy.
  • An owner of new and hard things. You’ve helped stand up operations for a new entity, location, or country. You’re comfortable starting with a blank page, identifying dependencies, and turning a complicated problem into an actionable plan without waiting for someone else to make the checklist.
  • A confident recommender and decision-maker. You bring options, explain the risks, and have a point of view. You know which decisions are yours to make and which need to go to the Head of People. We value expertise and thoughtful pushback, not just agreement.
  • Fluent in systems and providers. You’re comfortable working with HRIS platforms, payroll providers, PEOs, and external partners. You know what our vendors are responsible for, what remains our responsibility, and how to hold them accountable when things aren’t working.
  • A great juggler. Some months involve routine payroll and benefits admin. Others involve a new FRO launch, open enrollment, or a wind-down. Sometimes things happen all at once. You’re able to prioritize, anticipate collisions, and keep things moving without dropping the important details.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You’ve worked somewhere the process didn’t exist yet, or where version one left plenty of room for improvement. You bring structure to messy situations without assuming there’s always a standard answer.
  • Curious and questioning. You want to understand why something works the way it does, not just learn how to repeat it. You’re constantly looking for better tools, smarter processes, and ways to make the organization more effective.
  • A kind, low-ego teammate. You assume positive intent, communicate clearly, and treat people with respect. We don’t tolerate jerks, even exceptionally competent ones.

Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience in HR ops, payroll administration, or a closely related field (or 8+ years with a directly relevant master’s degree).
  • 5+ years of direct, accountable ownership of payroll administration across multiple jurisdictions, including California.
  • Experience standing up or substantially building people operations processes for a new entity, location, or country.
  • Hands-on experience administering benefits, including coordinating at least one open enrollment cycle.
  • Experience owning an HRIS, including configuration, integrations, data integrity, data governance, and reporting.
  • Experience developing complete, compliant policy suites across multiple states or countries, including knowing when to engage legal counsel.
  • Strong documentation and process-building skills, with examples of playbooks, controls, or operational systems you’ve created.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled tools for documentation, reporting, and workflow automation.

Nice to Have

  • UK payroll experience, including PAYE, RTI, and pension administration.
  • Experience working in a PEO environment, ideally with TriNet, and with Rippling or a comparable international payroll platform.
  • Experience with international employer of record (EOR) arrangements.
  • Experience in a nonprofit, startup, research organization, or other fast-moving, mission-driven environment.
  • Experience supporting multiple legal entities.

We Offer (Amazing Benefits):

  • A rare chance to build institutional architecture for frontier science and work with some of the smartest and most talented experts from different fields
  • Competitive Salary: The salary range for this role is $165,000 - 175,000. Convergent uses a consistent compensation philosophy across all roles, and we offer a 5-10% premium for those working from especially high cost of labor locations (e.g. NYC, San Francisco) or from our NYC office. This structure helps us keep pay transparent, consistent, and equitable.
  • Up to a 6% 401k match because future-you deserves comfort
  • Top-tier medical, dental, and vision insurance—majority of options are fully covered for you and your dependents. Stay healthy, my friend
  • Company-paid life insurance, AD&D, long- and short-term disability insurance, as well as voluntary supplemental insurance options
  • 19 holidays (including a full week off at the end of the year—yes, we enforce it)
  • 3 weeks PTO with tenure increases, with separate allotments for sick and parental leave
  • Generous fertility benefits and childcare reimbursement—because tiny humans are a big deal
  • Education and professional development benefits
  • Wellness allowance for fitness and wellness activities (treat yourself to climbing shoes or —no judgment)
  • Quarterly offsite team retreats and additional opportunities to meet your teammates in person
At Convergent Research, we are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. We believe in hiring individuals based on their unique talents, not on race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or our company policies. We are more than a proud Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Our goal is to foster a healthy, safe, and respectful environment where all employees are valued and treated with dignity. Harassment of any kind is not tolerated here.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As an Installation Coordinator, you’ll be responsible for orchestrating and monitoring Samsara hardware installations across customer fleets. You will ensure that each deployment is carried out according to technical and operational standards, working closely with Implementation consultants, Account Executives, Partners, and Internal stakeholders to guarantee a successful customer experience from the start.

This is a critical and detail-oriented role that blends project coordination, field operations knowledge, and customer success. Your work ensures our customers’ first touchpoint with Samsara’s technology is smooth, impactful, and aligned with our quality and safety standards.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in Mexico.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

  • Coordinate pre-installation logistics with partners.
  • Validate customer and site readiness, including cable availability and configuration.
  • Ensure the Statement of Work (SOW) is fully understood and achievable before kickoff.
  • Track real-time installation progress, ensuring adherence to the project plan.
  • Identify deviations from expected timelines or specifications and define/remediate action plans.
  • Drive weekly installation reporting cadence and provide updates to internal teams.
  • Maintain installation evidence and ensure proper documentation is stored and accessible.
  • Serve as a point of contact for escalations and troubleshooting during install phases.
  • Work cross-functionally with Sales, Implementation, and Support to ensure alignment.
  • Ensure installation partners are trained and follow Samsara standards.
  • Monitor CSAT related to installation events and resolve root causes of dissatisfaction.
  • Provide proactive communication and transparency with customers during install projects.
  • Define and continuously improve the installation coordination process using AI and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) tools to enhance efficiency and scale globally.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Experience in field operations coordination, customer implementation, or technical deployment.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple installs in parallel.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Fluent in Spanish and English (verbal and written).
  • Comfortable in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with cross-functional collaboration.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Has strong bias for standardization, automation and AI, the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards.
  • Thrives in a fast-paced and change-heavy environment.
  • Possesses strong problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Has familiarity or hands-on experience with AI and RPA tools to drive operational efficiency.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. Turno Source CODE

C - Customer Obsessed

O - Outcome Focused

D - Data Driven

Role Overview

As Senior Product Manager for our Core Experience, you'll own the essential workflows hosts and service providers use every day to run short-term rental operations. This includes how work gets planned, scheduled, communicated, completed, verified, and resolved across features such as task management, checklists, problem reporting, notifications, and operational workflows.

You'll spend time understanding how hosts and service providers actually work, identifying friction in their day-to-day routines, and turning those problems into intuitive product experiences.

This is a customer-facing product role. You should be comfortable working with technical systems and integrations, but your primary focus will be owning and improving the product experiences our customers depend on to get work done.

You'll work daily with Engineering, Design, Operations, Support, and other Product teams, and you'll be accountable for customer and business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Own the core operational experience

  • Own critical host and service provider workflows end to end. Set the strategy, roadmap, and execution for the experiences hosts and contractors use to manage work across their properties and projects.

  • Make daily operations simpler. Simplify multi-step and exception-heavy workflows without losing the flexibility customers need to operate their businesses.

  • Balance supply and demand. Make trade-offs that keep the marketplace healthy for everyone. A win for hosts that hurts cleaner retention (or the reverse) is not a win.

  • Design for the edge case as if it were the happy path. Substitutions, late arrivals, no-shows, damage reports, and engagement notifications get the same rigor as the primary flow, with workflows Operations can actually run.

  • Create consistency across the product. Help ensure Turno feels like one coherent system as we add new products, services, and markets.

Product strategy, discovery & execution

  • Lead continuous discovery. Translate customer behavior, qualitative research, support insights, and product data into clear problem statements, hypotheses, and opportunities.

  • Prioritize based on customer and business impact. Balance usability improvements, product growth, operational efficiency, reliability, and longer-term platform needs.

Systems & technical fluency

  • Think in connected systems. Understand how shared concepts such as properties, projects, users, schedules, tasks, payments, and communications interact across Turno.

Qualifications

  • Experience: 6+ years of product management in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, operations software, or products with complex customer journeys and multi-sided interactions (supply and demand, buyers and sellers).

  • Product sense and curiosity: Strong instincts grounded in real user understanding. You keep asking "why" until the root problem is clear.

  • Data fluency: Experience defining KPIs, building instrumentation, and using BI tools to make decisions.

  • AI experience: You leverage AI throughout your entire product tasks and planning.

  • Communication: Ability to explain complex customer, technical, and operational problems clearly and make thoughtful trade-offs visible.

﻿

About the Role

We are seeking an elite-level Senior Performance Media Buyer with proven experience scaling DTC fashion and eCommerce brands through high-budget paid advertising.

This position is designed for a highly experienced operator who has personally managed 300,000- 500,000+ USD in monthly advertising spend and understands how to scale aggressively without sacrificing profitability.

We are not looking for someone who simply launches campaigns, adjusts budgets, and reports ROAS.

We need someone who understands the entire paid acquisition ecosystem, from advanced bidding strategies and attribution to creative performance, customer acquisition economics, and full-funnel growth.

You will take ownership of paid media performance across multiple DTC brands, working closely with our Creative Strategist and leadership team to identify opportunities, develop scaling strategies, and drive profitable revenue growth.

A dedicated support resource will assist with campaign uploads and execution, allowing you to focus on high-level strategy, analysis, testing, and optimisation.

  • Scale winning campaigns to $10,000+ in daily spend while maintaining acquisition efficiency and profitability.
  • Analyze performance across Meta Ads Manager, Shopify, Google Ads, and Triple Whale to guide scaling and budget allocation decisions.
  • Monitor key performance metrics, including CPA, ROAS, MER, CAC, LTV, AOV, and contribution margin.
  • Evaluate attribution, tracking, and conversion data to distinguish profitable growth from platform-reported results.
  • Collaborate with the Creative Strategist to analyze creative performance, identify winning concepts, and guide testing priorities.
  • Identify creative fatigue, declining efficiency, and opportunities to improve campaign performance.
  • Optimize campaigns based on marginal returns, customer acquisition economics, and overall business profitability.
  • Leverage AI-powered tools, automation, and reporting systems to improve performance and operational efficiency.
  • Delegate routine campaign execution to support resources and communicate actionable performance insights to leadership.
  • Explore and support additional channels, including TikTok, Pinterest, Google Ads, and Axon (AppLovin), as relevant to the brands.

Qualifications

  • 3–5+ years of hands-on performance media buying experience, preferably with DTC fashion and eCommerce brands.
  • Proven experience personally managing and scaling $300,000–$500,000+ in monthly advertising spend.
  • Advanced expertise in Meta Ads, including cost caps, bid caps, minimum ROAS, and advanced scaling strategies.
  • Demonstrated experience scaling campaigns to $10,000+ in daily spend.
  • Deep understanding of eCommerce unit economics, including CPA, CAC, ROAS, MER, LTV, break-even points, and contribution margins.
  • Experience with TripleWhale.
  • Advanced analytical skills and proficiency in Excel and Google Sheets.
  • Strong understanding of pixels, conversion signals, attribution windows, and server-side tracking.
  • Experience with TikTok, Pinterest, and Axon (AppLovin), or the ability to ramp up quickly.
  • Ability to translate performance data into actionable creative insights and collaborate effectively with creative teams.
  • Strong communication skills, commercial awareness, and the ability to make data-driven decisions under pressure.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • Highly analytical and confident working with large volumes of performance data.
  • Takes ownership of results and operates with a strong commercial mindset.
  • Disciplined in testing, scaling winners quickly, and cutting underperforming campaigns.
  • Focused on profitable growth rather than vanity metrics.
  • Proactive, accountable, and consistent under pressure.
  • Collaborative, low-ego, and results-oriented.

Offer Details

  • Compensation: USD $4,500 per month, plus performance-based bonuses.
  • Employment Type: Full-time, B2B freelance contract.
  • Location: Fully remote, open to candidates worldwide.
  • Working Hours: 8 hours per day, with some overlap with the Australian time zone required for streamlined communication.
  • Paid Leave: 20 days of paid annual leave and 10 days of paid sick leave.

Hiring Steps

  1. Initial Zabota Screening – An introductory interview to assess experience, technical expertise, and alignment with the role.
  2. Client Interview – A discussion with the client to evaluate media buying experience, scaling strategies, and commercial understanding.
  3. Practical Task or Second Stage Interview – An additional interview or practical assessment, if required.
  4. Offer – Successful candidates receive a final decision and an official offer.

jobs.excerpt: Apple Client Platform Engineer (Remote, US)About AlectronaCustomer experience is more than meeting an SLA.
jobs.description:
Apple Client Platform Engineer (Remote, US)

About Alectrona

Customer experience is more than meeting an SLA.

Our team is passionate about making Apple “just work” for our clients, because we want you to experience the delight of a truly functional technology environment, without the friction of IT getting in the way. We get excited about what we do, and we love sharing that passion with our partners.

Enterprise IT becomes enjoyable again.

We actually love what we do, we take a lot of pride in the quality of our work, and for us, customer experience is paramount. The SLA is not the only metric that drives us. We get deeply invested in finding ways to keep our clients as excited as we are. In an industry that hasn’t changed much in over a decade, we are actively reimagining what clients should expect from technology vendors. So we want to show off what’s possible -- not just what’s been promised.

We treat all people as if they’re smart and know what's best.

...because our clients are smart, and they do know. We work with clients that inspire us, and whose missions we want to support. That mutual respect results in trusting relationships and productive communication about business pain points and solutions. We won’t hide behind intimidating security-speak and IT jargon. We say what we mean, and mean for clients to understand what we say.

Our clients put their people first - and so do we.

Happy employees create happy customers. Downtime is expensive, and top talent shouldn’t spend entire days downloading apps and setting up workstations. Our clients understand this, and demand the best for their people as a matter of business strategy. We bring a matching sense of purpose and excitement to every client engagement.

What you’ll do at Alectrona

You will lead professional services engagements for organizations running Apple at scale. That means designing the management platform, building the parts that do not exist yet, and telling the customer the truth about what will and will not work.

  • We're a fully remote team across multiple time zones, and we expect you to work well in that environment and be willing to meet in person a few times per year, present at conferences, and be an active member of the team.
  • Design, deploy, and hand over Apple management platforms: MDM, identity, patching, security tooling, and the integrations that tie them together.
  • Own services engagements end to end in accordance with our company values. You scope the work, plan it, run it, document it, and close it out. We expect you to be able to effectively manage your own time and projects. Our team enjoys this flexibility and autonomy and the responsibility that comes with it.
  • Solve the problems that get escalated after everyone else has tried. Packet captures, log spelunking, protocol-level MDM debugging, troubleshooting undocumented behavior in macOS.
  • Understand software development concepts: automations, integrations against vendor APIs, custom agents, deployment tooling. We don't expect you to write apps, but it is important to understand the code you're deploying and know how to fix stuff that isn't working.
  • Challenge customers when their plan will not survive production. Arguing for a better approach is part of the job, and you have to do it well enough to keep the relationship.
  • Run scoping calls. Uncover the business driver behind the request, and then explain what the work will take in plain language.
  • Support our small and medium business managed services customers alongside the rest of the Alectrona team.
  • Provide technical support and guidance to our managed services customers, including properly recording notes, updating documentation, and resolving tickets within SLA targets.
  • Mentor other engineers and colleagues to raise the standards and help everyone learn.
  • Shape new products and services. Alectrona builds its own software, and the ideas come from the field.
  • Perform all job responsibilities in alignment with the core values, mission and purpose of the organization.
  • Adhere to the highest moral, ethical and legal standards to deliver an environment that promotes respect, innovation and creativity.
  • Support and promote a positive, inclusive workplace where the talents and strengths of our increasingly diverse workforce are welcomed, further developed, and expressed in our work.

What we’re looking for

This is a high mid-level to senior role. We are looking for an engineer who is an expert in Apple management and knows the rest of IT well enough to work across the whole stack a customer runs. You will be supporting a variety of customer types, from end users to IT managers.

Apple and endpoint management

  • Deep experience managing Apple devices in a variety of types of environments. This means complex management beyond help desk support and basic engineering
  • Solid hands-on expertise in at least two enterprise Apple device management platforms, and the ability to pick up the others fast. Our work spans Jamf Pro, Microsoft Intune, Omnissa Workspace ONE, Fleet, Iru (formerly Kandji), Addigy and Mosyle.
  • Command of the Apple management stack itself, not just one vendor’s console: this includes an understanding of the MDM protocol, Declarative Device Management, Automated Device Enrollment and Apple Business, APNs, configuration profiles, TCC and PPPC, FileVault, code signing and notarization, Platform SSO, etc.
  • Experience migrating fleets between platforms, and a solid understanding of what each vendor does well and where another solution might be stronger.

Software/DevOps skills for managing endpoints

  • You are familiar with more than just using basic shell scripts. Confidence in writing your own Shell scripts and troubleshooting code at a minimum. Swift, Python, Go or other experience is a plus.
  • Use AI to accelerate and complement your code, not as a wholesale replacement. We want efficiency, productivity, and anti-slop creativity. At Alectrona, we view AI not as a replacement for human expertise, but as a multiplier for your existing skills.
  • Using git, participating in code review, leveraging CI, and testing and packaging are part of how you work, not something another team does for you.
  • You leverage APIs, webhooks, and automation workflows to complete tasks and build processes that scale.

The rest of IT

  • IP networking: familiar with TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, 802.1X, VPN, proxies and TLS inspection.
  • Server and identity administration: supporting Platform SSO, WebAuthn, Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Active Directory, SAML, OIDC, SCIM, Kerberos, and certificate authorities.
  • Security and compliance: CIS Benchmarks, NIST 800-53, SOC 2, ISO 27001, endpoint detection tooling, vulnerability management, and how each of these applies to securing Macs in production.

Working with customers

  • Experience and confidence delivering paid professional services or consulting to external customers.
  • You are comfortable actively leading and training customers on implementing configuration changes when we aren't provided direct access to systems.
  • Experience and confidence in supporting end users and small businesses in our managed services operation.
  • You explain complex technical work to people who do not share your background, in writing and out loud.
  • You participate in discovery, kickoff, and project scoping calls as the engineering voice; ask good questions and translate client context into technical decisions.
  • You have the confidence to stand up for what's right, whether it's about a technical best practice or just common sense. You challenge your customer to think differently and maintain trust in our recommendations.
  • You stay steady when a project goes sideways, the workload swings, or a customer is unhappy.
  • Fluent English language proficiency (required).

Education and certifications

  • Four-year degree, or the equivalent in experience and knowledge. We understand these skills don't come from higher education alone.
  • Appreciated, but not required; however, you should have the skill to obtain any or all of these certifications quickly: Apple Certified IT Professional, Jamf Certified Expert (400), Microsoft MD-102, CompTIA Network+ and Security+, CISSP. If you don't have certs, you will be expected to obtain them in the first few months of employment.

You’re the right fit for Alectrona if

You enjoy your work and enjoy helping the people around you without being asked. You seek out perspectives that are not your own. You are curious and resourceful; you dig into the parts nobody else wants, and you improve on your own work. New challenges excite you rather than worry you. You take calculated risks and share your mistakes with the team so we can all improve. You approach hard conversations with empathy. Like us, you enjoy solving the really hard problems as a team and hearing how we've significantly improved our clients' working environment. We're serious about building a great place to work where we all get to enjoy what we do together.

Pay and benefits

The approximate annual compensation range for this role is $95,000 to $165,000, including base salary and any related bonuses or commissions. In addition, Alectrona provides benefits, including 401(k) (6% non-elective company contribution), group medical, dental, vision insurance (99% paid by Alectrona), and an unlimited vacation policy.

Salary: $95,000 – $165,000 / year

Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, United States of America, Raynham, Massachusetts, United States of America, Remote (US), Warsaw, Indiana, United States of America, Washington, District of Columbia, United States of America, West Chester, Pennsylvania, United States of America

Job Description:

We are searching for the best talent for a Manager, Reimbursement and Payment Policy to join our Orthopaedics team. The role will ideally be located in Palm Beach Gardens, FL, Raynham, MA, Warsaw, IN, Washington, D.C. or West Chester, PA however remote work options may be considered on a case-by-case basis and if approved by the Company.


Purpose:

This role is designed for a professional with 5–10 years of professional experience in coding, coverage, and payment policy within the MedTech sector who can work independently and manage programs and vendors. The Manager will partner with cross-functional teams to deliver reliable reimbursement support, policy monitoring, and field enablement initiatives that drive market access for innovative orthopaedic technologies. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.


You will be responsible for:

CMS Payment Policy Support

  • Support the Director in developing and executing payment policy strategy for the Orthopaedics portfolio across Medicare payment systems, including IPPS/MS-DRGs, OPPS/ASC, and the Physician Fee Schedule.
  • Conduct research and analysis to inform coding, coverage, and payment positioning for both pipeline and in-line products, including DRG, APC, and code assignment questions.
  • Assist in the preparation of reimbursement assessments for new product launches and lifecycle management.

Policy Monitoring & Analysis

  • Monitor and analyze CMS proposed and final rules, along with Medicaid and commercial payer policy updates, and summarize implications for internal stakeholders.
  • Track changes in DRG, CPT/HCPCS coding, ASC/HOPD payment systems, and emerging reimbursement trends.
  • Develop concise summaries, executive alerts, and briefs that translate policy updates into actionable insights.
  • Manage multiple projects and deadlines tied to the CMS rulemaking calendar and annual coding cycles, and communicate status and risks to leadership.

Reimbursement Hotline & Vendor Management

  • Own day-to-day management of the Orthopaedics Reimbursement Hotline (phone and email), including vendor oversight, service levels, response quality, and escalation handling.
  • Manage the end-to-end hotline vendor relationship, including performance review and contract and scope management.
  • Ensure hotline operations comply with applicable healthcare compliance, privacy, and company policies, in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and Privacy.
  • Analyze inquiry logs to identify trends in customer needs, coding questions, and payer issues, and report insights and recommendations to HEMA and Commercial leadership.
  • Promote awareness of hotline services with field teams and customers, and set metrics to measure utilization and customer satisfaction.

Coding Guides, Reimbursement Tools & Field Education

  • Lead the annual update and lifecycle management of coding and reimbursement guides, FAQs, and customer-facing resources across joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports medicine, and related portfolios.
  • Ensure all guides reflect current CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS, MS-DRG, and APC information, as well as CMS payment rates and rule changes, and are accurate, compliant, and timely.
  • Manage the content review and approval process with Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance, and maintain version control and a publication calendar.
  • Design and deliver training for sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams on coding, coverage, and payment, and translate policy updates into practical field guidance.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to keep reimbursement websites and resource libraries current and easy to navigate.

External Engagement & Advocacy Support

  • Assist the Director in drafting comment letters and background materials for CMS and other stakeholder engagements.
  • Support preparation for interactions with external stakeholders (e.g., specialty societies, trade associations, payer groups).
  • Conduct landscape assessments to support advocacy positions and policy strategy development.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Evidence Integration

  • Partner with Health Economics and Epidemiology teams to support development of evidence strategy to facilitate reimbursement and access.
  • Provide reimbursement inputs for Target Product Profiles (TPPs) and early-stage pipeline discussions.
  • Synthesize clinical, economic, and real-world evidence to inform coverage strategies.
  • Collaborate with Commercial, Regulatory, Legal, and Compliance to ensure reimbursement information and programs meet company and regulatory standards.

Education and Experience:


Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Health Policy, Health Economics, Public Health, Business, or a related field.
  • 5–10 years of relevant experience in reimbursement, health policy, market access, or healthcare consulting, preferably in the medical device or life sciences industry.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. reimbursement systems, including Medicare payment structures (IPPS/MS-DRG, OPPS/ASC, Physician Fee Schedule) and coding frameworks (CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10-CM/PCS).
  • Experience interpreting CMS regulations and translating them into business implications and written materials such as comment letters or executive briefs.
  • Experience managing vendors, programs, or customer support operations, including performance metrics and compliance requirements.
  • Strong analytical, research, project management, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex policy to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams in a matrixed environment.

Preferred

  • Advanced degree (e.g., MPH, MPP, MBA).
  • Experience in MedTech, orthopaedics, or surgical technologies.
  • Familiarity with CPT/HCPCS coding, CMS rulemaking, and payer policy development processes.
  • Experience with reimbursement hotlines, field reimbursement, or coding and reimbursement education.
  • Coding credential (e.g., CPC, CCS) or equivalent practical coding expertise.

Fueled by innovation at the intersection of biology and technology, we’re developing the next generation of smarter, less invasive, more personalized treatments.

Are you passionate about improving and expanding the possibilities of Orthopaedics? Ready to join a team that’s reimagining how we heal? Our Orthopaedics teams help keep more than 6 million people moving each year while delivering clinical and economic value to surgeons and healthcare systems. Our teams build solutions for joint reconstruction; trauma and craniomaxillofacial; sports, extremities, and elective foot and ankle; spine; and robotics and digital surgery.

Your unique talents will help patients on their journey to wellness. Learn more at

jobs.title: M&E Associate - Rapid Experimentation
jobs.excerpt: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011.
jobs.description:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Priority Application Deadline: May 15, 2026

About this role

The Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Associate for Rapid Experimentation will support the execution and analysis of A/B tests across GiveDirectly’s programs, contributing to the use of data to inform program and product decisions. This role is fast-paced and iterative - the team runs frequent, lightweight experiments designed to generate actionable answers quickly, and then uses those learnings to refine and improve programs in real time. This includes:

  • Supporting the execution and analysis of rapid A/B tests across GiveDirectly projects, ensuring that experiments are implemented effectively and contribute to learning within and across projects
  • Ensuring experiments are implemented correctly, measured reliably, and analyzed to produce clear and credible results, working closely with Programs, Product, Research teams, and external academic partners to align experimental design with program delivery, data collection, and operational realities
  • Translating findings into actionable insights and well-structured learning products that serve multiple audiences - internal program and product teams, and external academic partners, ensuring results inform both immediate decisions and longer-term program direction

In practice, this role is about managing a high volume of rapid experiments and turning results into clear, credible evidence that continuously shapes how GiveDirectly’s programs are refined and improved.

Reports to: Senior Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation

Level: Associate

Travel Requirement: This role is based in Rwanda. Travel within East Africa is a regular part of the role, estimated at up to 25% of the time, to support field operations across country programs.Additional international travel may occur for trainings or team convenings, as needed (estimated up to 10%)

What you’ll do:

Execute and manage A/B tests across programs

  • Conduct power calculations to ensure experiments are both statistically rigorous and feasible to implement within program constraints
  • Set up pre-specified experimental designs, applying defined experimental groups, outcome measures, and measurement timelines
  • Review experiment setups prior to launch and flag execution and measurement risks that may affect interpretability
  • Ensure experiments are well-coordinated and executed as designed, aligning implementation with research plans and integrating smoothly into program delivery across Programs and Product teams
  • Work at a fast pace across a portfolio of 2–3 live A/B tests at any given time, designed to generate actionable answers quickly and feed rapid iteration of programs and products

Ensure accurate measurement and high-quality data for experiments

  • Collaborate with external Principal Investigators (PIs) to ensure measurement approaches and data collection are aligned with research design and implementation realities
  • Ensure experimental outcomes are captured accurately and consistently by applying established indicator and measurement approaches
  • Prepare and manage datasets that are clean, well-structured, and ready for analysis using survey, administrative, and product data
  • Identify and flag data quality risks (e.g., missingness, inconsistencies, measurement error) that could affect the validity of experimental conclusions
  • Conduct targeted literature reviews to ensure measurement approaches are grounded in evidence and aligned with best practices

Analyze experimental data and interpret results to inform decisions

  • Generate reliable and decision-ready analyses of experimental data from A/B tests
  • Assess the magnitude and direction of effects and highlight what the results do and do not suggest, noting key limitations
  • Ensure results are clearly understood and appropriately interpreted, given data quality, sample size, and implementation considerations

Translate results into actionable insights and learning across experiments

  • Translate experimental results into clear, actionable recommendations to guide program and product decisions for individual country programs, and for the direction of GiveDirectly’s programming as a whole
  • Structure results and key learnings so they can be reused to inform future experiments and program design
  • Prepare concise learning products (e.g., memos, summaries) that serve multiple audiences, including internal Programs and Product teams, and external academic partners, ensuring findings are clearly communicated for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Prepare and clean de-identified datasets for sharing with external PIs and academic partners, ensuring data is structured, well-documented, and ready for independent analysis
  • Contribute to cross-country discussions to ensure learnings from experiments are shared and applied across contexts, and maintain clear documentation so experiments are easy to track, understand, and build on over time

What you’ll bring:

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem-solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, or a related quantitative field
  • 2–4 years of experience working with data in applied settings (e.g., experimentation, evaluation, analytics, or program learning), ideally in development, tech, or operations-focused roles
  • Solid understanding of experimental design and causal inference concepts (e.g., randomization, treatment/control groups, units of randomization, statistical power, bias) and how to apply them in real-world program contexts
  • Experience using R, Python, or Stata to clean, manipulate, and analyze data, including working with multiple data sources (e.g., survey or administrative data)
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (e.g., programs/operations, product, or research) and external partners to implement projects and solve problems
  • Fluency in English required
  • Comfort working at pace - able to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously, make progress with imperfect data, and iterate quickly based on emerging findings
  • Ability to interpret results beyond statistical significance and communicate clear, actionable insights to both technical and non-technical audiences

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

Kenya

  • Base Salary: $42,000
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$4,200, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization's current performance multiplier, this amount would be $4,914 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $46,200+

Rwanda

  • Base Salary: $37,600
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 10% (~$3,760, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization's current performance multiplier, this amount would be $4,399 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $41,360+

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in Kenya or Rwanda, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

  • A supportive team that works hard and cares hard
  • A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country)

  • Continuously evaluate and implement new technologies that support scalable growth.
Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Partner with executive and revenue leadership to align marketing, sales, and business objectives.

jobs.excerpt: About RidgelineRidgeline is the first front-to-back system of record for investment managers.
jobs.description:
About Ridgeline

Ridgeline is the first front-to-back system of record for investment managers. Founded by visionary entrepreneur Dave Duffield (co-founder of both PeopleSoft and Workday), the company was created to modernize an industry held back by outdated, disconnected technology. Powered by a single, real-time data set and embedded AI, Ridgeline helps firms automate complexity, accelerate collaboration, and deliver tailored client experiences at scale, without added headcount or risk. Ridgeline is headquartered in Lake Tahoe, with offices in New York, Reno, and the Bay Area, and is recognized by Fast Company as a “Best Workplace for Innovators,” by Frost & Sullivan as a “Technology Innovation Leader,” and by The Software Report as a “Top 100 Software Company.”

Why this role exists

As the number of concurrent customer implementations at Ridgeline grows, our Technical Consulting team is changing how it builds, deploys, and supports third-party integrations. This role is split roughly evenly between delivering integrations for new customers and helping launch a new managed integration services capability within consulting. You will help bring integration code into a single source of truth, define repeatable deployment and operating models, and make every new build faster and more consistent than the last. As a founding member of this effort, you will work closely with Technical Consulting leadership and Platform Engineering, and you will have the chance to shape how Ridgeline supports customers long after go-live.

What success looks like

Within six months, you will have completed training, shadowed experienced consultants, and built integrations with guided support. You will have led the integration workstream for a customer implementation and become familiar with Ridgeline APIs, Workato connectors, and common third-party vendors. Within a year, you will have a holistic understanding of our implementation methodology and of the customer and vendor landscape, and you will have made meaningful progress with Platform Engineering on reusable, centrally managed integration assets.

What you'll do

  • Lead and project manage integration workstream
  • Conduct discovery sessions to develop and document a thorough understanding of customers’ integration needs
  • Build and deploy integrations that are reusable, well documented, and maintainable across customers.
  • Partner with Platform Engineering to move integration code into a single source of truth with consistent deployment practices.
  • Improve our implementation methodology and consulting efficiency, with a focus on reducing technical debt and the hours required for repeat builds.
  • Help define the operating model for managed integration services that supports customers after go-live.
  • Engage directly with customers and vendors to scope, build, and troubleshoot integrations.

What we look for

  • 3–5 years of professional experience delivering technical solutions for customer or internal stakeholders in a software, consulting or complex technology environment.
  • Experience working in a complex technology organization, ideally a microservices environment, with a demonstrated understanding of how to deploy a service.
  • Practical software development or systems engineering experience beyond configuration, including building, deploying, and maintaining technical solutions.
  • Experience owning the resolution of a complex, high-impact technical challenge within a multi-system or microservices environment.
  • Comfort working directly with customers and vendors, and the ability to learn new technologies and domains quickly.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in financial services or investment management (not required; we welcome backgrounds from other industries).
  • Experience championing and driving adoption of source control, testing, deployment, and monitoring practices for a team.
  • Hands-on experience with Workato or another Integration-Platform-as-a-Service solution (Workday Studio, Mulesoft, Boomi, or Similar)
  • Have explored and developed initial ideas about agentic operations: agentic code review, continuous deployment, end-to-end integration tests, observability tooling, LLM gateway, and other related areas
  • Strong opinions about different models and when to use them is a plus!

Compensation and Benefits

The cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $114,000 - $143,000 OTE. Final compensation amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amount listed above.

As an employee at Ridgeline, you’ll have many opportunities for advancement in your career and can make a true impact on the product.

In addition to the base salary, Ridgeline employees can participate in our Company Stock Plan subject to the applicable Stock Option Agreement. We also offer rich benefits that reflect the kind of organization we want to be: one in which our employees feel valued and are inspired to bring their best selves to work. These include unlimited vacation, educational and wellness reimbursements, and $0 cost employee insurance plans. Please check out our Careers page for a more comprehensive overview of our perks and benefits.

Flow Studio has built a strong customer base through product-led growth. Creators and studios are already using it every day, and the product has matured to the point where it delivers serious value for larger creators and companies. Second, you will run targeted outbound into existing Autodesk customers who would be well served by Flow Studio, partnering closely with the Autodesk Account Executives and account reps who own those relationships. You will run fast, consultative sales cycles over phone and Zoom, from first conversation to close.


This is a startup inside Autodesk, and it is not starting from zero. The product, the customer base, and the executive backing are in place. What is new is the team and the motion. You will help write the first plays, test what works, kill what does not, and shape how Flow Studio scales from self-serve to sales-led.


You will work alongside a cross-functional growth team from Marketing, Product, Strategy, and Analytics, and learn from peers on the Fusion sales team, who have spent eight years scaling a similar business in manufacturing. Autodesk's culture emphasizes curiosity, rapid innovation, and ownership. We believe in reimagining what is possible, taking smart risks, and pursuing results with urgency. If you want to be on the ground floor of an AI product with real momentum and help build the team that scales it, this is the role.

  • Ability to partner with account owners and other sellers in a collaborative, shared-account model
  • Strong discovery instincts and curiosity about creative and production workflows
  • Ability to communicate clearly with artists, technical leads, producers, and business decision makers
  • Interest in AI, 3D, VFX, animation, games, or content creation technology

Preferred Qualifications

The Ideal Candidate


  • ACV from Enterprise tier upgrades and new Enterprise customers

Why Flow Studio, Why Now

AI is changing how content gets made, and Flow Studio is at the center of that shift. Creators have already found the product. The next chapter is bringing it to larger studios and production companies that need it at scale.


As a Flow Studio Sales Specialist, you will be one of the first sellers to do that, and you will help build the playbook every rep after you will use. If you want startup speed with enterprise backing and a front row seat to an AI product scaling upmarket, we want to talk.

Great Place to Work Certification is recognized worldwide by employees and employers alike and is the global benchmark for identifying and recognizing outstanding employee experience. Every year, more than 10,000 companies across 60 countries apply to get Great Place to Work Certified.

The Senior Analyst, Origination will support and be the analytical and coordination hub of the Origination and Contracting team, owning market fundamentals reporting, price curve management, revenue modeling, and day-to-day management of M&A. This role translates market data, vendor forecasts, and regulatory developments into pricing recommendations, deal economics, and decision-ready analysis that support origination strategy, PPA structuring, and investment approvals across Reactivate’s distributed generation, community solar and storage portfolio.

Responsibilities ⚙️

  • Produce recurring market fundamentals reports (monthly/quarterly) covering energy, capacity, REC/SREC, and ancillary service markets across key ISOs/RTOs (e.g., PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, MISO, ERCOT, CAISO)
  • Track and interpret drivers of power prices, load growth (data centers, electrification), supply additions and retirements, transmission constraints, and policy changes
  • Monitor forward curves, broker quotes, and market transactions to benchmark PPA pricing and identify shifts in offtake market conditions
  • Maintain market intelligence dashboards and summaries for leadership, origination, and finance stakeholders
  • Serve as the internal owner of third-party price curves from fundamentals vendors
  • Ingest, validate, version, and archive vendor curves; reconcile differences across vendors and releases, and document methodology changes
  • Build and maintain revenue models for solar, storage, and solar-plus-storage projects under various offtake structures, including physical and virtual PPAs, fixed-shape and as-generated contracts, tolling agreements, hedges, and merchant tails
  • Model revenue stacks including energy, capacity, RECs/SRECs, ancillary services, energy arbitrage, and community solar/DG compensation (e.g., Illinois ABP REC pricing, NY VDER/Value Stack)
  • Research utility tariffs and state-specific regulatory frameworks (e.g., net metering rules, community solar program rules, rate case outcomes) to inform origination strategy
  • Monitor, screen, and review utility and load-serving entity RFPs for energy, capacity, RECs, storage, and DG/community solar procurement, and summarize eligibility, product definitions, evaluation criteria, credit and security requirements, and key dates for go/no-go decisions
  • Prepare market updates, origination materials, pricing memos, and deal summaries for internal approval and external counterparties
  • Coordinate with Finance, Product, and Origination teams to align pricing assumptions with the deal pipeline in Salesforce
  • Manage internal M&A review process, coordinate with internal departments and be point of contact for communication with Sellers

Requirements 🎓

  • Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree a plus
  • 3 - 5+ years of experience in renewable energy origination, community solar program administration, utility regulatory analysis, or a related analytical role
  • Strong Excel skills for building pricing forecasts and tracking program economics over time
  • Familiarity with community solar and distributed generation program structures (Illinois Adjustable Block Program, NY VDER/Value Stack, or similar state programs) and interconnection processes
  • Working knowledge of utility tariff and program adder structures, with ability to read and extract relevant terms from program administrator guidance, PUC/PSC filings, and rate schedules
  • Advanced Excel modeling skills, including building integrated revenue models, scenario tools, and sensitivity analyses from scratch
  • Solid understanding of wholesale power market fundamentals, including LMP pricing, capacity markets, REC markets, and basis/congestion dynamics
  • Experience working with third-party price forecasts and forward curves, and the ability to critically evaluate vendor methodologies and assumptions
  • Proficiency in Python,SQL or similar tools for data pipelines, curve processing, and automating recurring analysis, CRM (salesforce) experience
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams across different state markets
  • Strong written communication skills; ability to translate technical/regulatory detail into clear, decision-ready summaries
  • Comfort acting as an external-facing point of contact with sellers, advisors, counsel, and counterparties, with sound judgment on when to escalate
  • Experience supporting or managing M&A diligence or project acquisition processes in renewable energy or infrastructure
  • Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future

Preferred Qualifications 💡

  • Experience with storage dispatch or production cost modeling tools (e.g., PLEXOS, Aurora, PowerSimm, or custom optimization models)
  • Experience with data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau)
  • Exposure to ISO market data sources and APIs (e.g., PJM Data Miner, NYISO OASIS, Yes Energy)
  • Familiarity with tax credit structures (ITC/PTC, transferability, adders) and their interaction with offtake pricing

Make an Impact

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. We manage services for individuals with serious mental health needs, substance use disorders, traumatic brain injuries, and intellectual/development (IDD) disabilities. Our mission is to help individuals and families build strong foundations for healthy, fulfilling lives.

Why Work for Us?

Trillium believes that empowering others begins with supporting our team. We offer our employees:

  • A collaborative, mission-driven work environment
  • Competitive benefits and work-from-home options for most positions
  • Opportunities for professional growth in a diverse inclusive culture

Every day, our work changes lives – from children thriving through early intervention and school-based therapies, to adults with severe mental illness living independently and contributing to their communities.

If you are looking for a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact on the lives of others, apply today!

What We’re Looking For

Trillium Health Resources has a career opening for a Medical Economics Analytics Manager to join our team! The Medical Economics Analytics Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for the Medical Economics Analytics Department, overseeing workflow, quality, and timely delivery of financial and healthcare analytics. This role leads the analysis, interpretation, and reporting of complex medical and financial data to support organizational strategy, cost management, utilization, and value-based care initiatives. The Manager serves as a strategic partner to Finance and Clinical teams, identifying trends and emerging issues, evaluating cost and utilization drivers, and providing forward-looking insights, retrospective analysis, and root-cause evaluations to support informed decision-making. The Manager ensures accurate, efficient, and timely reporting while overseeing team priorities, performance, and development. This role regularly communicates key trends, findings, and department activities to leadership and provides thought leadership that supports organizational goals and a data-driven culture.

On a typical day, you might:

  • Lead and supervise Medical Economics Data Analysts, supporting strategic goals, performance, training, and development.
  • Oversee Medical Economics MLR, IBNR, financial, and ad hoc reporting, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery.
  • Partner with the Director of Medical Economics to model financial impacts of policy and clinical decisions.
  • Analyze and interpret complex data using SQL, Power BI, Power Query, pivot tables, and multiple data sources.
  • Develop meaningful reports, dashboards, and analytics to support Finance, leadership, and organizational decision-making.
  • Establish best practices, promote innovation, and lead Medical Economics reporting and process improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor departmental reports, communications, and services to ensure quality, consistency, and transparency.
  • Prepare executive-level reports and presentations, provide recommendations, and communicate key findings.
  • Support hiring, performance management, disciplinary actions, and other special projects and assignments.

Employee Benefits:

Trillium knows that work/life balance is essential. That’s why we offer:

  • Typical working hours: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm; flexible work schedules with some roles with management approval.
  • Work-from-home options available for most positions
  • Health Insurance with no premium for employee coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 24 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) plus 12 paid holidays in your first year
  • NC Local Government Retirement Pension (defined-benefit plan)
  • 401k with 5% employer match and immediate vesting
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) qualifying employer
  • Quarterly stipend for remote work supplies

Qualifications

Required:

  • Associate's degree and three (3) years of experience in financial analysis and medical economics, including experience developing and writing code using SQL; OR
  • Bachelor's degree and one (1) year of experience in financial analysis and medical economics, including experience developing and writing code using SQL; OR
  • Equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Must reside within North Carolina.
  • Must be able to travel within catchment as required.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship for employment now or in the future (ex: OPT F-1, J-1).

Preferred:

  • Master’s degree
  • Five (5) years of experience with healthcare analytics, statistics, or data management
  • Supervisory experience of two (2) or more employees
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and SQL skills

To be considered, submit your application and resume through our ADP Career Center. Your resume must include:

  • Employer name, dates of service (month/year), average hours worked per week, and essential job duties

Join our Talent Community through ADP to stay informed about future opportunities. Be sure to keep your resume updated in your profile.

When a new infrastructure requirement arises, we should already know where suitable capacity is available, who controls it, when it can be delivered and what it will take to secure it.

The world’s digital experiences run on something invisible: the infrastructure and software that keep them fast, reliable, and secure. At Gcore, you’ll help design and deliver that foundation for an AI-driven world.

With 210+ edge locations, 50+ cloud regions, and thousands of GPUs, your work here can reach users and businesses across the globe.

You’ll collaborate with leading technology partners such as Intel, NVIDIA, Dell, and Equinix, and work on platforms that power digital products used around the world. Our vision is simple: to connect the world to AI, anywhere, anytime.

Want to work on technology that goes beyond a single product or industry? Join a global team of 550+ professionals building infrastructure and software that supports the entire digital ecosystem.

We are currently looking for a Global Data Center Capacity Manager to help secure the infrastructure required for the continued growth of our global cloud and AI platforms.

This is not a traditional procurement role. It is a highly market-facing position focused on ensuring we have early visibility and access to available and upcoming data center capacity before it becomes an urgent requirement.

You will build relationships across the global data center ecosystem, proactively identify capacity opportunities and maintain market intelligence, bringing qualified opportunities into the wider Procurement process for commercial negotiation and contracting.

What We’re Looking For

  • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple matters and jurisdictions.

Preferred bar admissions: California, Illinois, New York, or Massachusetts. Admission in additional jurisdictions is a plus.

Why Join Segal McCambridge?

At Segal McCambridge, you’ll have the opportunity to work on sophisticated, high-profile litigation without being limited to a single office or jurisdiction. Our national platform offers associates meaningful responsibility, access to experienced trial attorneys, and opportunities to build a long-term career in complex litigation.

  • High-profile national litigation: Work with a national team serving as coordinating counsel for prominent clients in the asbestos litigation docket.
  • Meaningful responsibility: Contribute to case strategy, discovery, motion practice, and trial preparation from the outset.

  • Career growth: Benefit from mentorship, business development support, and opportunities to earn origination and business development credit.
  • Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive salary commensurate with experience, along with performance-based bonus opportunities.

Comprehensive Benefits

Segal McCambridge offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • 401(k) with firm match
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Health savings and flexible spending accounts
  • Paid time off and parental leave
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Employee assistance and wellness programs
  • Continuing legal education and professional development support

About Segal McCambridge

Founded in 1986, Segal McCambridge is a nationally recognized litigation firm representing Fortune 500 companies and major insurers in complex litigation nationwide. Our attorneys bring substantial trial experience, deep industry knowledge, and a results-driven approach to defending our clients’ interests.

Ready to expand your toxic tort defense experience and contribute to a high-profile national litigation practice?
